rGUbthevD0.one_liner: Characterizes equivariant multi-head attention: groups only permute head clusters, and each architecture covers at most one locus component.
rGUbthevD0.problem: It is unclear whether imposing a correct symmetry on multi-head self-attention restricts expressivity beyond the intended equivariance constraint.
rGUbthevD0.method: Proves an if-and-only-if characterization of equivariant MHSA (G acts by permuting head clusters, with QK and OV matrices satisfying a group-tied constraint) and shows the equivariance locus of unconstrained MHSA is a union of many Zariski-irreducible components, of which any single analytically parameterized architecture covers at most one.
rGUbthevD0.key_idea: Equivariant MHSA layers decompose into head clusters permuted by the group, and the equivariance locus splits into many irreducible components that a single analytic parameterization cannot jointly cover.
rGUbthevD0.evidence: Theorems on equivariant MHSA, experiments on artificial tasks showing the predicted head-cluster structures, and QM9 experiments on equivariance-constraint choices in equivariant transformers.
rGUbthevD0.claimed_gains: For G=D_4 acting on C copies of the regular representation there are Omega(C^64) components with eight attention heads, and the TLDR cites over 10^96 components at token dimension 768.
rGUbthevD0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the necessary-and-sufficient characterization is a sound, fundamental theoretical contribution that unifies designs such as all-heads-equivariant and the Platonic Transformer as extremes of one picture.
rGUbthevD0.main_concern: Practical impact is unclear: the trade-off comes from counting components under exact equivariance with polynomial parameterizations, for a single layer, and the experiments are small and synthetic.

bY07ZAmiFk.one_liner: Unbiased min-min cross-entropy optimizer that caches hard negative classes per example, evaluates them exactly, and samples the rest.
bY07ZAmiFk.problem: Sampled softmax gives biased gradients for extreme multiclass cross-entropy, and uniform sampling within the unbiased min-min reformulation yields high-variance gradients and slow convergence.
bY07ZAmiFk.method: PEACH maintains a small cache of hard negative classes for each example, evaluates their contributions exactly, and uses simple random sampling to estimate the sum over the remaining classes, within the min-min reformulation where an auxiliary variable learns the normalization term.
bY07ZAmiFk.key_idea: Stratify the softmax normalization sum into an exactly computed per-example cache of hard negatives and a sampled remainder, keeping the estimator unbiased while cutting variance.
bY07ZAmiFk.evidence: Theoretical analysis of unbiasedness and variance reduction, and experiments on four large datasets using frozen features and a linear classifier (up to 796K classes, per reviewers).
bY07ZAmiFk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that caching hard negatives is a well-justified way to cut gradient variance while preserving unbiasedness, supported by correct variance formulas and results on large datasets.
bY07ZAmiFk.main_concern: The experiments cover only linear classifiers on frozen features, and the exact kNN-graph rebuild each epoch adds large wall-clock cost at 796K classes.

vBwRAh5nc2.one_liner: Defensive forecasting algorithm that obtains both online gradient boosting span guarantees and weak-to-strong boosting guarantees using one weak learner
vBwRAh5nc2.problem: Online gradient boosting promises nothing when the span lacks an accurate predictor, and online weak-to-strong boosting promises little when the weak-learning condition fails, and no single algorithm gave both guarantees.
vBwRAh5nc2.method: The Defensive Booster is a defensive forecasting algorithm for binary outcomes chosen by an adaptive adversary, given an online learner for a weak class. It operationalizes the dual view of boosting, so persistently high randomized classification error yields mistake weights forming a smooth reweighting on which every weak hypothesis has low edge.
vBwRAh5nc2.key_idea: Use defensive forecasting with the dual view of boosting, so high error produces a smooth reweighting on which all weak hypotheses have low edge.
vBwRAh5nc2.evidence: Regret and error-rate theorems, a self-bounding analysis with an O(1/T) rate in the realizable setting, separation results, and experiments on real data with linear weak learners plus finite-class synthetic experiments.
vBwRAh5nc2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that obtaining both span-based and weak-to-strong guarantees from one algorithm with a single weak learner is a fundamental, appealing result with a concise analysis.
vBwRAh5nc2.main_concern: The writing is dense and hard to follow (undefined jargon, mixed 0/1 and +1/-1 notation), which obscures the algorithm and analysis.

u02SERBXpM.one_liner: Proves two frozen random softmax-attention blocks, with only order, signs and durations chosen per task, interpolate any sequence collection.
u02SERBXpM.problem: Universal approximation for self-attention typically needs infinite width, and it is unclear whether depth alone with strong parameter sharing, as in Looped Transformers, can give universal interpolation.
u02SERBXpM.method: Uses geometric control theory (Lie-bracket arguments per reviews) to show a predefined finite set of attention blocks, composed in input-dependent order, sign and duration, maps any N sequences of n tokens to any other, at continuous and finite depth and under causal masking.
u02SERBXpM.key_idea: Compose a few fixed softmax-attention vector fields with chosen signs and durations; Lie-bracket generated directions make the compositions expressive enough to interpolate arbitrary targets.
u02SERBXpM.evidence: Theory: Theorem 3.5 (two frozen single-head blocks with Gaussian-initialized projections, valid for every N and n) at continuous and finite depth, plus causal-masking results.
u02SERBXpM.claimed_gains: not stated; theoretical results only (two frozen blocks suffice, with no bounds on depth or parameter norms).
u02SERBXpM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the result strong, clean and surprising, with a well-positioned question for looped transformers and a clearly written paper.
u02SERBXpM.main_concern: No bounds on depth, number of switches, durations or parameter norms are given, and the setting (data-dependent gains and signs, no generalization) differs from actual looped transformers, limiting practical relevance.

m2JpO4G77U.one_liner: Supervises latent multimodal reasoning with visual-dependency estimates from region-wise image masking during explicit chain-of-thought.
m2JpO4G77U.problem: Continuous latent reasoning is cheaper than explicit CoT but underperforms it on visually grounded multi-step tasks, apparently because latent states are weakly tied to task-relevant visual evidence and vary little across steps.
m2JpO4G77U.method: DepLatent masks image regions during explicit CoT to estimate dependencies between reasoning tokens and visual regions, then trains latent states with dependency-weighted alignment to relevant visual features and step-level reconstruction of CoT segments identified by changes in visual dependency. At inference the model reasons with compact latent tokens.
m2JpO4G77U.key_idea: Use masking-induced likelihood changes to map reasoning tokens to image regions, then align latent states to those regions and reconstruct CoT segments at dependency change points.
m2JpO4G77U.evidence: Six multimodal reasoning benchmarks and three vision-language backbones of varied sizes, with error analysis on 200 examples, image-masking interventions, ablations and baselines such as Heima per reviews.
m2JpO4G77U.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy over explicit CoT and latent reasoning baselines with lower inference latency, with an average 6.2% gain (comparison cut off in the abstract).
m2JpO4G77U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and the masking-based diagnosis of weak visual grounding useful, with strong gains across backbones and benchmarks and large speedups over explicit CoT.
m2JpO4G77U.main_concern: The visual-dependency signal is validated with masking-based metrics that share its construction, so the claim that weak visual grounding explains the latent-versus-explicit gap is not independently established, and some loss equations are unclear.

mKsRKa8Rbj.one_liner: Shows momentum acceleration gives sqrt(kappa) rates for Gaussian variational inference with exact expectations but not under pointwise derivative access.
mKsRKa8Rbj.problem: It is unknown whether momentum acceleration (kappa to sqrt(kappa) condition-number dependence) extends to Gaussian variational inference for strongly log-concave, log-smooth targets.
mKsRKa8Rbj.method: Casts GVI as a convex composite problem for accelerated proximal gradient with exact expectations, proves a kappa^{1-o(1)} query lower bound under pointwise derivative access, and gives variance-reduced stochastic methods that accelerate under a Lipschitz-Hessian assumption with small Hessian variation.
mKsRKa8Rbj.key_idea: Acceleration holds when Gaussian expectations are exact or Hessian variation is small, but curvature bounds alone cannot guarantee it under pointwise derivative queries.
mKsRKa8Rbj.evidence: Theorems (accelerated upper bounds and a query lower bound on a constructed family of targets) plus experiments on real datasets showing speedups across a broad range of methods.
mKsRKa8Rbj.claimed_gains: With exact Gaussian expectations GVI attains the accelerated sqrt(kappa) rate, while under pointwise derivative access any randomized algorithm needs kappa^{1-o(1)} queries on a constructed family of targets.
mKsRKa8Rbj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clear and combines an accelerated upper bound, a query-complexity lower bound for pointwise access, and a positive result showing small Hessian variation restores acceleration.
mKsRKa8Rbj.main_concern: It is unclear that the accelerated variants have lower total complexity than unaccelerated ones outside restrictive regimes where the variance term dominates, and the algorithms themselves are standard accelerated proximal methods.

ddJW429f5j.one_liner: OSWorld 2.0: 108 long-horizon computer-use workflows measuring agents on realistic multi-application tasks.
ddJW429f5j.problem: Existing computer-use benchmarks lack the realism, complexity and long-horizon demands of real computer use, so they fail to reveal the limits of frontier agents.
ddJW429f5j.method: Builds 108 workflows grounded in authentic input artifacts and stateful user-profile data, with dense final-state checkpoints and separate safety reports, targeting challenges such as streaming and proactive interaction, dynamic environments, cross-source reasoning, implicit-state inference and visual-spatial precision.
ddJW429f5j.key_idea: Tasks are end-to-end workflows grounded in authentic artifacts and stateful user profiles, graded by checkpoints that allow alternative solution paths and partial credit.
ddJW429f5j.evidence: Frontier agents evaluated under a binary-completion metric at 500 steps with partial scores, validation through human completion and agent rollouts, and analysis of state tracking and failure modes.
ddJW429f5j.claimed_gains: Claude Opus 5 with maximum thinking and batched tool calls scores best at 31.43% task completion and a 68.31% partial score, on tasks taking humans a median of about 1.6 hours and averaging 435 actions.
ddJW429f5j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills the gap between short isolated tasks and realistic long workflows, with stateful environments, dense checkpoints, partial credit and analysis beyond aggregate scores.
ddJW429f5j.main_concern: With only 108 tasks and unclear effects of evaluator and environment issues (Table 17 flags possible mismatches in 30.6-42.6% of audited trajectories), reported completion lacks uncertainty intervals and a matched bridge between benchmark releases.

ZITt6ZPPu0.one_liner: LazyFlash keeps attention forward dense and skips low-gradient query blocks in the FlashAttention backward pass to speed fine-tuning.
ZITt6ZPPu0.problem: Attention dominates long-context training cost, and existing sparse attention mostly targets inference or fails to turn sparsity into wall-clock training speedups.
ZITt6ZPPu0.method: Ranks query blocks by attention-output gradient norms and skips those contributing little to parameter updates inside the tiled FlashAttention backward kernel, adapts the skipped amount per head and step with a gradient-mass budget, and uses importance sampling to keep the dense gradient in expectation.
ZITt6ZPPu0.key_idea: The backward pass is made block-sparse by skipping query blocks with small attention-output gradient norm, with an inverse-probability importance-sampling correction preserving the dense gradient in expectation.
ZITt6ZPPu0.evidence: Experiments on long-context text and speech LLMs with a CUDA kernel inside FlashAttention, and per reviews end-to-end training speedups across model scales and context lengths (the abstract is cut off).
ZITt6ZPPu0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is practical, delivers wall-clock training speedups through a well-optimized kernel, and keeps inference dense so models are served unchanged.
ZITt6ZPPu0.main_concern: Gains are hard to attribute because related backward-sparsification work (Back Razor, PreBackRazor, BackLite) is not compared, overhead of importance estimation is not broken down, and sensitivity to the budget parameter and long-context evals are limited.

QvAAGu1wUz.one_liner: fDAG-ACDC selects the number of latent factors in causal representation models using local posterior-predictive checks with uncertainty-adaptive thresholds.
QvAAGu1wUz.problem: The right number of latent components in causal representation learning is rarely known, and standard criteria fail because extra latent structure can improve global fit by absorbing misspecification.
QvAAGu1wUz.method: Extends the accumulated cutoff discrepancy criterion (ACDC) for factor-DAGs by comparing observed and posterior-predictive distributions of each node and its estimated parents within each perturbation environment, picking the smallest candidate within a standard-error band of the best, and proves model-selection consistency.
QvAAGu1wUz.key_idea: Per-node posterior-predictive discrepancy in each perturbation environment, with the smallest factor count within a set number of standard errors of the best, replaces a hand-tuned tolerance.
QvAAGu1wUz.evidence: A consistency proof under stated conditions, simulations against validation-likelihood and oracle graph-recovery baselines, and Perturb-seq and organoid data.
QvAAGu1wUz.claimed_gains: In simulations the mean absolute selection error is 0.5 while validation likelihood and oracle graph-recovery baselines over-select by more than 3, and on Perturb-seq and organoid data it selects fewer factors than validation likelihood while matching or nearly matching larger models in prediction.
QvAAGu1wUz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles a relevant open problem in causal representation learning with a principled criterion, consistency guarantees, and experiments on simulated and real perturbation data.
QvAAGu1wUz.main_concern: Scope is narrow (f-DAGs, few factors, three baselines), most gain may come from the standard-error selection rule rather than the criterion, and sensitivity to its threshold and possible known-graph leakage in simulations are unexamined.

0UIDvpnoVa.one_liner: EHR-WM models patient histories as action-conditioned latent trajectories with a state-dependent linearization predictor.
0UIDvpnoVa.problem: Autoregressive token-prediction models of electronic health records do not separate patient state from clinical actions, which limits action-conditioned simulation.
0UIDvpnoVa.method: Represents patient histories as latent trajectories that separate patient states from observed clinical actions and learns their evolution with a state- and action-conditioned transition operator. A state-dependent linearization predictor propagates latent changes for multi-step rollout and action-conditioned simulation.
0UIDvpnoVa.key_idea: A state-dependent linearization predictor propagates latent patient-state changes under supplied clinical actions, so rollouts can be conditioned on action sequences.
0UIDvpnoVa.evidence: MIMIC-IV experiments on generated trajectories, decoded free-running rollouts against task-matched forecasting baselines, classification and time-to-event tasks against larger EHR foundation models, and action-perturbation tests.
0UIDvpnoVa.claimed_gains: A 4.39M-parameter model over a restricted high-frequency feature space is competitive but task-dependent relative to substantially larger EHR foundation models.
0UIDvpnoVa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that EHR trajectories suit world modeling, the model is competitive with other patient-trajectory methods, and the paper is clear with the expected experiments.
0UIDvpnoVa.main_concern: Only MIMIC-IV is used, actions are supplied rather than inferred, and the paper does not isolate whether generating future trajectories beats using the observed history directly for outcome prediction.

Hde0mlSPsj.one_liner: Proves two-layer ReLU CNN filters under gradient flow align to the signal axis early, then loss converges at rate O(1/t).
Hde0mlSPsj.problem: It is unclear how gradient-based training of convolutional networks learns to extract signal and ignore noise.
Hde0mlSPsj.method: The paper analyzes gradient flow on two-layer ReLU CNNs with sum-pooling, trained on exponential or logistic loss from small balanced initialization. Each input has one signal patch, with class signals in narrow antipodal cones, and noise patches orthogonal to the signal subspace.
Hde0mlSPsj.key_idea: Activated same-class signal patches in a narrow cone pull each filter toward the common axis in a self-reinforcing feedback, while orthogonal noise patches stay outside the signal subspace.
Hde0mlSPsj.evidence: Theoretical proofs under explicit data assumptions (Assumptions 1-4) with an early-phase alignment result and a convergence result; a reviewer notes code is provided.
Hde0mlSPsj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clear and the proofs rigorous, and value explicit bounds on filter alignment and subsequent loss convergence in the presence of noise with both layers trained.
Hde0mlSPsj.main_concern: Data assumptions are strong, with signal patches in very narrow cones and noise exactly orthogonal to the signal subspace, and it is unclear how the conclusions hold when these fail.

Xa7zNGGQhW.one_liner: Bounds the volume of exact-solution parameters (NESV) for single-layer transformers by input length to explain and improve length generalization.
Xa7zNGGQhW.problem: Expressivity results show whether a transformer can solve a task but not whether the learned solution generalizes to longer inputs.
Xa7zNGGQhW.method: The paper defines normalized exact-solution volume as the fraction of a bounded parameter region that solves a task exactly on every input of length n, and derives asymptotic bounds for FIRST, MAJORITY, INDEX and PARITY. The INDEX analysis exposes two error sources, which guide a modified transformer.
Xa7zNGGQhW.key_idea: Measure how fast the fraction of bounded parameter space that exactly solves a task shrinks with input length n, then structurally remove sources of that shrinkage.
Xa7zNGGQhW.evidence: Asymptotic bounds for fixed-width single-layer single-head transformers with log n-scaled attention and no residuals or layer norm, plus experiments comparing predicted trends with empirical length generalization.
Xa7zNGGQhW.claimed_gains: NESV is Theta(1) for FIRST, Theta(1/(n log n)) for MAJORITY, Theta(1/n^3) for INDEX and 0 for PARITY, and the modified model improves INDEX to Theta(n^-1) and reaches 85% accuracy at 10 times the training length versus 60% for the original.
Xa7zNGGQhW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find NESV a clear, intuitive and well-motivated way to study length generalization beyond expressivity, with helpful proof sketches and experiments in good agreement with the theory.
Xa7zNGGQhW.main_concern: The setting is restricted to single-layer, single-head transformers without residuals or normalization, and the link between volume and length generalization is only empirical, with MAJORITY a reviewer-noted counterexample.

x9LbWvc6fO.one_liner: Multiplies a known local Lyapunov function by a learned positive correction so outputs are Lyapunov near equilibrium for any parameters.
x9LbWvc6fO.problem: Neural Lyapunov functions learned from data rarely come with formal guarantees, and small approximation errors near the equilibrium can break the certificate.
x9LbWvc6fO.method: Zubov-Net multiplies an anchor (a known local Lyapunov function) by a learned positive correction, so the local Lyapunov conditions hold for every parameter choice. Training then only learns the global basin shape from trajectory data and a scaled residual of Zubov's equation, followed by formal verification of the region of attraction.
x9LbWvc6fO.key_idea: Write the network output as a known local Lyapunov function times a learned positive factor, so local Lyapunov conditions hold by construction.
x9LbWvc6fO.evidence: 22 benchmark systems with 2 to 20 state variables, comparing formally verified region-of-attraction estimates against SOS certificates, plus a universal approximation theorem for anchored networks.
x9LbWvc6fO.claimed_gains: Formally verified ROA estimates are consistently, and often substantially, larger than those of the baseline certificates across benchmarks with two to twenty state variables.
x9LbWvc6fO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the anchored architecture a simple way to guarantee the local Lyapunov conditions, less conservative than competing methods, scalable to higher dimensions, and well written.
x9LbWvc6fO.main_concern: The training target, loss terms, counterexample-guided loop and verification closely follow prior work so the new part is mainly the multiplicative anchor, and training and verification cost is not reported.

cm0fjA9Pwf.one_liner: Transformers trained on interacting-agent feedback sequences represent each agent's Bayesian belief in separate residual-stream subspaces.
cm0fjA9Pwf.problem: It is unclear whether a transformer trained on the joint behavior of interacting agents represents them as modular components or as an indivisible whole.
cm0fjA9Pwf.method: A computational-mechanics framework proves any joint stochastic process can be presented as agents in feedback, generated by a hidden Markov model whose beliefs factorize per agent. Experiments probe and intervene on transformers trained on such sequences, including belief patching in a pretrained language model.
cm0fjA9Pwf.key_idea: Joint beliefs of feedback-coupled agents factorize into per-agent components, and transformers store them in separate subspaces whose total size grows linearly with agent count.
cm0fjA9Pwf.evidence: Theorems on factorization, probing and counterfactual interventions in transformers trained on synthetic feedback sequences, in-context patching of a pretrained language model, and coarse-graining experiments.
cm0fjA9Pwf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formalization is clean and rigorous and the experiments go beyond decoding to causal interventions on belief representations.
cm0fjA9Pwf.main_concern: Experiments use small transformers on synthetic data, and per-factor probes and final-layer patching may not distinguish factored from joint representations, leaving real LLM relevance untested.

gO1SLMPGbi.one_liner: Execution-free process supervision turns outcome measurements into reusable guidance for partial GPU kernels, enabling search without executing intermediate candidates.
gO1SLMPGbi.problem: GPU kernel search depends on execution feedback, but compiling, validating, and benchmarking candidate kernels is expensive and bottlenecks scalable search and generation.
gO1SLMPGbi.method: ProcessKernel converts one-time outcome measurements into reusable guidance for unfinished kernels during autoregressive generation, enabling on-the-fly search without executing intermediates. Per reviews, a calibrated outcome reward model learns kernel ordering via learning-to-rank with scale recovered from anchor kernels, and a process reward model guides segment-level beam search.
gO1SLMPGbi.key_idea: Train a rank-calibrated outcome reward model on measured kernels and use it to supervise a process reward model that scores partial kernels, so search needs no execution of intermediates.
gO1SLMPGbi.evidence: Generated-kernel correctness and speedup across eight generators, with comparisons including Random Beam and DeepConf, ranking-fidelity measurements, and labeling cost in H100 GPU-hours.
gO1SLMPGbi.claimed_gains: Process-supervision labeling cost reduced by 76x (9.3 vs an estimated 707 H100 GPU-hours), generated-kernel correctness improved by up to 38%, and speedup of up to 21.64x.
gO1SLMPGbi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation practical, the learning-to-rank calibration of the outcome reward model well reasoned, and the results strong across several generators.
gO1SLMPGbi.main_concern: Many counted-correct kernels are not genuine Triton kernels or delegate heavy operations to PyTorch, and the reward models barely distinguish speed (speed-pair accuracy 0.512), so gains may come mostly from correctness.

MLdEdeBNWU.one_liner: Post-training attention compression that keeps complete RoPE rotary pairs ranked by joint query-key activation energy, folded into the weights.
MLdEdeBNWU.problem: Head-dimension compression reduces KV-cache memory, but existing methods reconstruct full-dimensional representations at inference, adding decoding FLOPs.
MLdEdeBNWU.method: RACE restricts reduction to coordinate selection with a shared query-key projection and shows RoPE compatibility holds if and only if complete rotary pairs are retained, then selects pairs by joint query-key activation energy on a calibration set. The reduction is folded into the model weights, cutting both KV-cache storage and attention computation.
MLdEdeBNWU.key_idea: Select whole rotary pairs by joint query-key activation energy, which minimizes a separable, calibration-dependent upper bound on post-RoPE query-key product error.
MLdEdeBNWU.evidence: Calibration-based compression of pretrained models evaluated on zero-shot and LongBench tasks against baselines such as RAP and reconstruction-based methods, with efficiency estimates (contexts up to about 64K per reviews).
MLdEdeBNWU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the reconstruction-free design practical, compatible with standard attention implementations, and consistently better than RAP, with theory on RoPE compatibility of coordinate selection.
MLdEdeBNWU.main_concern: Reviewers cite thin long-context validation (little beyond 64K), a selection criterion that minimizes a loose upper bound, and degraded quality at aggressive 50% KV-cache retention, and one sees limited novelty.

3uKKt21Vry.one_liner: Rank analysis of linear attention states motivates pruning key and query channels via rank-revealing QR to halve state size.
3uKKt21Vry.problem: Trained linear attention models often have low-rank recurrent states and so underuse capacity, and the state may be reducible post-training if its rank structure is understood.
3uKKt21Vry.method: The paper analyzes how keys and values shape the rank of the recurrent state, then proposes a hardware-aware structured pruning of key and query matrices that cuts state size while staying compatible with existing kernels. It adapts several existing pruning strategies and proposes a robust method based on rank-revealing QR decomposition.
3uKKt21Vry.key_idea: Select key and query channels with a rank-revealing QR decomposition so the pruned recurrent state preserves the effective rank identified by the theory.
3uKKt21Vry.evidence: Models of varying sizes (four families, 370M to 9B per reviews) on downstream tasks, with end-to-end speedups using existing kernels, plus theoretical analysis of state rank.
3uKKt21Vry.claimed_gains: The state of pretrained linear attention models can be halved with only a minor decrease in next-token prediction capability; no figures stated.
3uKKt21Vry.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the rank theory clean and the pruning practical, since it respects architectural constraints and existing kernels, with extensive experiments across model families and compression ratios.
3uKKt21Vry.main_concern: One reviewer argues linear-attention state storage is not a bottleneck in hybrid architectures at long context, and others note limited methodological novelty over QR-based channel selection.

kCChCaXb7h.one_liner: Transfers the best learning rate from training the last few blocks to more blocks, with precision-dependent scaling.
kCChCaXb7h.problem: Post-training such as SFT and DPO is highly learning-rate sensitive, and tuning by repeated runs is costly in compute and memory.
kCChCaXb7h.method: TipSweep searches for the best learning rate by training only the last k0 transformer blocks, then scales it for k blocks. An analytical model of update rounding explains the scaling rules, and a prototype runs the search for a 6.7B-parameter model on one 16 GiB consumer GPU.
kCChCaXb7h.key_idea: Use the number of trainable blocks as the transfer axis, scaling the optimal learning rate as k^-1 with FP32 master weights and k^-1/2 with direct BF16 updates.
kCChCaXb7h.evidence: SFT and DPO experiments on models from 1 to 7 billion parameters, profiling experiments supporting the rounding model, and a single-consumer-GPU prototype.
kCChCaXb7h.claimed_gains: The optimal learning rate scales approximately as k^-1 with FP32 master weights and k^-1/2 with BF16 weights and no master copy; learning-rate search is feasible for a 6.7-billion-parameter model on a 16 GiB GPU.
kCChCaXb7h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the number of trainable blocks a practical transfer axis for pretrained checkpoints, with a consistent BF16-versus-FP32 scaling finding and broad coverage of SFT, DPO, and model families.
kCChCaXb7h.main_concern: The cost advantage lacks a realistic baseline such as early stopping, and the rounding theory rests on assumptions that are partly circular and not fully isolated from other precision effects.

LJvGaCWmFh.one_liner: Restores the zero-sum property of softmax score gradients after BF16 casting with two rank-one corrections in FlashAttention.
LJvGaCWmFh.problem: BF16 FlashAttention backward leaks the mean key into the query gradient, so the gradient norm grew a thousandfold late in pretraining of a 450M-parameter transformer.
LJvGaCWmFh.method: GProj (gauge projection) restores the zero row sum of the softmax score gradient after the BF16 cast with two rank-one corrections. The paper also traces part of the blow-up to a forward-softmax fused multiply-add case left unfixed in FlashAttention-3.
LJvGaCWmFh.key_idea: Softmax score gradients sum to zero per row; BF16 rounding breaks this and leaks the mean key into the query gradient, so project the zero sum back.
LJvGaCWmFh.evidence: A 450M-parameter transformer pretrained on 50B tokens with FlashAttention-3, FP32 backward recomputation of two layers, and gradient-error measurements against FP32.
LJvGaCWmFh.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract, which is cut off at 'It cuts the remaining median query/key gradient'.
LJvGaCWmFh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnosis convincing and the mathematically grounded, low-overhead projection effective at bringing gradient errors near FP32 levels.
LJvGaCWmFh.main_concern: The pathology is shown mainly in a single-seed 450M run with a particular architecture (QK normalization disabled), and plain-transformer controls do not reproduce the blow-up, limiting how general the benefit is.

5hq5jNF4Bv.one_liner: A neural architecture that stays a Petri net for all weights, learning only the transition rate law for reactions.
5hq5jNF4Bv.problem: Learned reaction models and Petri-net-based networks do not guarantee Petri net semantics such as valence conservation and the enabling rule.
5hq5jNF4Bv.method: Neural Petri Flow hard-wires the firing form, locality, and the enabling rule as parameter-free layers and learns only the rate law (or a classification readout). On a valence net, atom mapping, reaction classification, and forward prediction become tasks on one firing vector.
5hq5jNF4Bv.key_idea: Prove that conservation forces the firing form and non-negativity forces the enabling rule, leaving only the rate law free to learn.
5hq5jNF4Bv.evidence: Atom mapping, reaction classification, and forward prediction experiments; reviewers cite ECREACT, FlowER, and USPTO benchmarks with ablations on the enabling mask and readouts.
5hq5jNF4Bv.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract, which is cut off before the results.
5hq5jNF4Bv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified formulation interpretable and competitive, with strong results on enzyme classification and elementary-step prediction and in training-free and low-data settings.
5hq5jNF4Bv.main_concern: The necessity of the Petri formalism is not shown since components map to existing constructs (bond-electron matrix, graph edits, valence masking), and strong forward-prediction baselines such as Chemformer and R-SMILES are omitted.

nV7YP3Xb4q.one_liner: Corrects fine-resolution forecasts of frozen backbones using disagreement with coarse-resolution forecasts via an affine corrector.
nV7YP3Xb4q.problem: A fine-resolution forecast aggregated over an interval can disagree with a forecast made directly at a coarser resolution, and this disagreement carries information about fine-resolution errors.
nV7YP3Xb4q.method: Parallax decomposes the disagreement into the aggregated fine residual and the coarse-forecast error, reducing correction to residual estimation. It fits an affine corrector whose moments combine a resolution-structured covariance from a nested aggregation chain with empirical moments from historical forecast-target pairs.
nV7YP3Xb4q.key_idea: Estimate fine-forecast residuals from cross-resolution disagreement using a structured covariance over a nested aggregation chain, without updating the backbone or seeing future observations.
nV7YP3Xb4q.evidence: 13 benchmark datasets with 7 task-specific models and 5 pretrained foundation models, with ablations.
nV7YP3Xb4q.claimed_gains: Reduces MSE by 11.8%-26.4% across task-specific backbones and by 33.2% on average across foundation models.
nV7YP3Xb4q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the correction simple, interpretable, model-agnostic, and consistently beneficial across many datasets and backbones with supporting ablations.
nV7YP3Xb4q.main_concern: Comparisons with forecast-reconciliation (e.g., MinT) and linear residual-correction baselines are missing, structured moments alone nearly match the full method, and experiments use a single seed.

rPD7JoNuMU.one_liner: Four training-free sampler modifications cool guided diffusion samples of amorphous matter, halving excess configurational entropy without retraining the score network.
rPD7JoNuMU.problem: A score-based denoiser conditioned on an experimental observable produces high-configurational-entropy samples that the conditional input cannot distinguish from the reference, a residual excess temperature that raises outliers and harms physical behavior.
rPD7JoNuMU.method: Four modifications to the sampling routine: a gate interpolating between the reverse SDE and the probability-flow ODE, guidance on low-frequency bands the observable leaves undetermined, a structural relaxation projected onto the null space of the observable's Jacobian, and a ladder of partial restarts.
rPD7JoNuMU.key_idea: Suppresses residual sampling noise by acting on directions the conditioning observable cannot see: null-space relaxation, low-frequency guidance, an SDE/ODE gate, and partial restarts.
rPD7JoNuMU.evidence: Disordered-materials case study (amorphous silicon and a second system) built on the GLASS model, with component ablations and energy evaluated with a different potential from the one used for relaxation (per reviews).
rPD7JoNuMU.claimed_gains: Together the measures halve the excess entropy on benchmark systems and reach amorphous configurations that quench kinetics have kept out of reach of direct simulation for decades.
rPD7JoNuMU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and the sampler modifications are well motivated, with a useful entropy analysis and component ablations.
rPD7JoNuMU.main_concern: The method is evaluated on a single application with one model (GLASS) and no comparison to other refinement methods, so generality beyond amorphous-structure inversion is unclear and some comparisons are confounded.

IkNhrhBFe1.one_liner: Co-trains an LLM judge to turn reference answers alone into the sole reward for on-policy reasoning-model post-training without verifiers.
IkNhrhBFe1.problem: RLVR is limited to tasks with explicit correctness signals, yet in many post-training settings good answers are recognizable but hard to score, and prior adversarial approaches need co-trained critics beside verifiable rewards or reference reasoning traces.
IkNhrhBFe1.method: Reinforced Adversarial Learning (RAL) co-trains an LLM judge to tell reference answers from policy outputs and uses the judge as the only reward for on-policy RL, with stability tricks such as Polyak averaging and thresholded updates. It is validated on three verifiable tasks with verifiers used only for evaluation, then applied to abstract generation.
IkNhrhBFe1.key_idea: Adversarial co-training in which the judge learns to separate reference answers from policy outputs and its score is the sole on-policy reward, pushing the generator toward the reference distribution.
IkNhrhBFe1.evidence: Three verifiable tasks (integer multiplication, code-based arithmetic-expression synthesis, SMILES-to-formula translation) with held-out verifiers, plus paper-abstract and NIH grant-abstract generation judged by human scientists and LLM judges.
IkNhrhBFe1.claimed_gains: Judge-only RAL with sufficiently capable judges and enough training matches or exceeds direct RLVR on verifiable tasks, and its grant abstracts are harder for human scientists and LLM judges to distinguish from real ones than those of frontier-LLM baselines.
IkNhrhBFe1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree reference-only reward learning is promising, with a well-designed verifier-held-out evaluation, judge scores that correlate with the hidden error metric, and useful stability tricks.
IkNhrhBFe1.main_concern: The explanation of why RAL works is not validated, the co-training benefit is confounded (judge and reward formulation differ from the frozen-judge baseline), and positioning against GAD, R-AIRL, and RARO is unclear.

QFH598mfYw.one_liner: Gap-free e-process tests for computerized classification under 2PL, needing no indifference region and permitting any predictable item policy.
QFH598mfYw.problem: Classical sequential probability ratio tests calibrate errors at two separated abilities, leaving behavior inside a user-chosen indifference region unresolved.
QFH598mfYw.method: Under a known 2PL response model, the authors build gap-free one-sided e-processes with finite-sample directional error control: a shrinking-reference rule, and a main rule that mixes over dyadic discrimination-standardized alternatives.
QFH598mfYw.key_idea: Mixes e-processes over dyadic, discrimination-standardized alternatives to cover every distance from the cutoff without a separated design point, keeping validity under predictable item selection.
QFH598mfYw.evidence: Theory (stopping-order bounds in an ideal centered-item experiment), known-truth simulations, and logged-response comparisons on student response datasets, which the abstract says are observational.
QFH598mfYw.claimed_gains: The shrinking rule has local mean order O(delta^-2 log^2(1/delta)) and the main mixture rule attains the optimal worst-scale order O(delta^-2 loglog(1/delta)) in an ideal experiment; per the TL;DR it is more accurate than Wald's SPRT but gives longer tests for students near the cutoff.
QFH598mfYw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the validity arguments are coherent and cover predictable item selection, with honest claim scope and a rate-optimal result in the centered-item model.
QFH598mfYw.main_concern: Added value over established anytime-valid methods (e.g., a stitched-boundary comparator) is not demonstrated, the guarantees assume a fully known 2PL model with fixed ability, and the empirical evaluation is not fully reproducible.

gp85N6Zq6R.one_liner: Benchmark where a user simulator reveals requirements gradually over multi-turn sessions, testing coding agents on interactive software engineering tasks.
gp85N6Zq6R.problem: Existing SWE benchmarks give complete requirements upfront and test autonomous implementation, unlike real workflows where requirements start vague and are refined through interaction.
gp85N6Zq6R.method: A user simulator starts with vague instructions, progressively reveals requirements, inspects the agent's workspace, and gives targeted feedback, revisions, and new constraints until the full goal is handed off. It reuses underlying tasks and final verifiers from existing benchmarks and evaluates frontier and open-weight models.
gp85N6Zq6R.key_idea: Re-runs existing SWE tasks with a workspace-inspecting user simulator that discloses requirements incrementally, so the same final verifiers measure interactive intent discovery.
gp85N6Zq6R.evidence: Frontier and open-weight models on 25 tasks from each of three source benchmarks (per a review), compared with single-turn baseline versions, plus failure audits attributing failures to causes such as simulator omission.
gp85N6Zq6R.claimed_gains: Benchmark finding, no method gains: the best models solve roughly 50% of single-turn baseline tasks but only 25% of the corresponding SWE-Interact tasks.
gp85N6Zq6R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets a practically important capability, and that reusing the same tasks and final verifiers gives a clear comparison showing a large drop in multi-turn performance.
gp85N6Zq6R.main_concern: Measurement validity is uncertain because the final verifier can penalize requirements the simulated user never disclosed (about 15-16% of audited failures), and the evaluation set is small (25 tasks from each of three benchmarks).

XmV6XsPvQr.one_liner: Trains CLIP on images from several architecturally distinct diffusion models with a programmatic hard-negative curriculum, using fully synthetic data.
XmV6XsPvQr.problem: Synthetic vision-language pre-training that scales a single generative backbone introduces generator-specific spectral biases and limits feature diversity.
XmV6XsPvQr.method: PolyGen renders each caption with an ensemble of architecturally distinct generators (a multi-positive strategy exposing disjoint visual manifolds from the same caption) and adds a Programmatic Hard Negative curriculum for fine-grained compositional understanding. It reallocates the same image budget from unique captions to multi-source variations.
XmV6XsPvQr.key_idea: Generator-Invariance Hypothesis: artifacts vary across generators while semantics are shared, so training on the union of several generators' renderings of one caption encourages encoding the shared semantics.
XmV6XsPvQr.evidence: Fixed 500k-image budget comparisons against SynthCLIP and a real CC3M-500k baseline, with ablations on ensemble composition, invariance regularization, and hard-negative timing, plus exploratory 3M and 12M runs (per reviews).
XmV6XsPvQr.claimed_gains: Outperforms SynthCLIP by +19.0% on aggregate multi-task benchmarks and +11.3% on compositional reasoning at the same data budget.
XmV6XsPvQr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fixed-image-budget design and factorial comparison of generator heterogeneity and positive density are valuable, with three-seed experiments supporting a measurable heterogeneity contribution.
XmV6XsPvQr.main_concern: The headline +19.0% mixes several design choices (higher positive density alone gives 14.1%), single-generator baselines use only a weak generator (SD 1.5), and gains at 3M and 12M images are only 0.25 and 0.64 points.

muTR3yZV21.one_liner: Builds prover-estimator debate estimators efficiently via local signed level-set optimization guided by the prover's too-high or too-low allegations.
muTR3yZV21.problem: Prover-estimator debate's existence argument for sound estimators uses reference answers unavailable to the estimator, making it non-executable, with a circuit-size upper bound exponential in the branching width.
muTR3yZV21.method: When decompositions cannot profitably change a claim's meaning, estimator construction reduces to local optimization guided by whether the prover alleges the estimate is too high or too low. Assuming efficient signed level-set optimization, the algorithm uses resettable access to a fixed prover and simulated debate scores, never hidden reference answers, and outputs an estimator with a soundness bound at polynomial cost.
muTR3yZV21.key_idea: Under a semantic admissibility restriction, estimator construction becomes signed local optimization using only the prover's high-or-low allegations on simulated debates, not hidden reference answers.
muTR3yZV21.evidence: Theoretical algorithm with a soundness bound and a conditional lower bound without the semantic restriction (abstract cut off); no empirical evaluation is mentioned.
muTR3yZV21.claimed_gains: Construction and evaluation costs polynomial in the mechanism's parameters with a soundness bound against a fixed prover; no numbers stated.
muTR3yZV21.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper makes a genuine step from existence to construction on an explicitly open debate problem, cleanly isolating the assumptions, with a lower bound locating the difficulty in faithful decomposition.
muTR3yZV21.main_concern: The semantic admissibility assumption is never instantiated or checkable in a concrete setting, and the honest prover relies on oracle-like routines that move the obfuscation problem to the honest side.

IUNg2H7JCy.one_liner: State hallucination and dynamic shift attacks on world models, defended by adversarial training of the latent encoder
IUNg2H7JCy.problem: Latent dynamic world models are a centralized point of failure for planning, evaluation, and training in embodied AI, yet their security and robustness properties are poorly understood.
IUNg2H7JCy.method: Develops two attacks, state hallucination and dynamic shift, aimed at downstream systems, and proposes a theoretical lens (a TA-MDP framework per reviewers) on robustness of latent dynamic world models. The analysis identifies robust latent encoders as the key component, and adversarial encoder training (an extended FARE per reviewers) is used as the defense.
IUNg2H7JCy.key_idea: Attack world models by hallucinating states or shifting action-conditioned dynamics, and defend by adversarially training the latent encoder, which the analysis identifies as the key robustness component.
IUNg2H7JCy.evidence: Four latent dynamic world model families (Dino World Model, Le World Model, r2Dreamer, Cosmos 3), with closed-loop planning, policy-evaluation rankings, adaptive attacks, and transfer tests.
IUNg2H7JCy.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims significant robustness improvements from adversarial encoder training, without figures)
IUNg2H7JCy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value an important, underexplored problem and a thorough study linking latent-space attacks to downstream failures, with defense evaluation including adaptive attacks.
IUNg2H7JCy.main_concern: The proof of Theorem 1 is flagged as not holding as written, and the state-preserving dynamic-shift experiment does not fully separate altered dynamics from altered perceived state.

EKdVFcc2Vm.one_liner: A JEPA-style world model restricts latent dynamics to a bilinear form, enabling fast Gauss-Newton planning and action-recoverable representations
EKdVFcc2Vm.problem: World models learn arbitrary latent dynamics, which makes planning expensive and leaves representation collapse a risk, and JEPA-style models are limited to short-horizon offline planning.
EKdVFcc2Vm.method: Restricts latent dynamics to a bilinear parameterization, shifting the modeling burden onto the encoder and structurally enforcing action recoverability to prevent collapse by construction. The bilinear structure permits a Gauss-Newton gradient-based planner in place of sampling-based search, and a broad class of nonlinear systems is shown to admit a transformation to bilinear dynamics.
EKdVFcc2Vm.key_idea: Constrain latent transitions to be bilinear in state and action, which forces the encoder to expose controllable geometry and allows Gauss-Newton planning.
EKdVFcc2Vm.evidence: Standard 2D and 3D control tasks (four LeWM-suite tasks per a reviewer) compared with SMWM and LeWM, plus longer-horizon and real-time control regimes.
EKdVFcc2Vm.claimed_gains: Reduces planning time by nearly three orders of magnitude while retaining or even improving control accuracy.
EKdVFcc2Vm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the bilinear restriction is a clever, effective idea that cuts planning time sharply while matching or surpassing LeWM and SMWM.
EKdVFcc2Vm.main_concern: Evidence is limited to four low-dimensional goal-reaching tasks, and the paper lacks a conclusion and a limitations section.

Dfse4Co8tA.one_liner: VoS learns each step's value of steering from counterfactual outcomes to decide where to correct an LLM agent
Dfse4Co8tA.problem: Uncertainty is often used to decide when to correct an LLM agent, but it is unclear whether it can guide whether, at which step, and with which mechanism to steer.
Dfse4Co8tA.method: Builds the stepwise outcome table (SOT) by steering every non-terminal step with each of four mechanisms and running each continuation to completion. VoS (Value of Steering) is a trajectory-level monitor, offline or online, that learns the value of steering at each step from SOT, with a harm-budgeted trigger limiting disturbance to successful trajectories.
Dfse4Co8tA.key_idea: Learn a value function over steps from measured counterfactual steering outcomes and gate it with a harm budget, instead of triggering on uncertainty.
Dfse4Co8tA.evidence: SOT holds about 82,000 counterfactual continuations of 1,864 trajectories from three benchmarks and two agents; VoS is compared with five existing uncertainty-triggered methods in 12 settings, with ablations.
Dfse4Co8tA.claimed_gains: VoS improves on unmodified execution in all 12 settings by 7.8 points on average and outperforms the strongest of five existing uncertainty-triggered methods in 11 settings by 2.9 points on average.
Dfse4Co8tA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value SOT as a rigorous measurement instrument that also records harm, and the finding that uncertainty detects failing trajectories but does not locate where steering helps.
Dfse4Co8tA.main_concern: Generality is untested because the monitor is refit per benchmark-agent-mechanism setting from about 82,000 re-executions, and headline comparisons lack significance tests.

jIvAcVobIh.one_liner: Graph metanetworks that coarsen and refine the input network's graph with permutation-symmetry-preserving pooling and unpooling along its layer hierarchy.
jIvAcVobIh.problem: Graph metanetworks operate on every neuron and weight of the input model, so their cost scales with parameter count and has not reached beyond small MLPs and CNNs.
jIvAcVobIh.method: H-GMNs use the input architecture's hierarchy (neurons, layers, blocks and modules) to coarsen and refine the graph with permutation-symmetry-preserving pooling and un-pooling layers, and extend to Transformers via a symmetry-preserving graph construction that enables multi-level pooling.
jIvAcVobIh.key_idea: Run message passing at multiple granularities by pooling neurons into layer- and block-level nodes and unpooling back, while respecting neuron and attention-head permutation symmetries.
jIvAcVobIh.evidence: New ResNet-18 and ViT model zoos with up to 21M parameters per model, on model evaluation, backdoor detection, and pruning tasks, with sample-efficiency and cost analyses.
jIvAcVobIh.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract's results are truncated).
jIvAcVobIh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach addresses a clear scalability limitation of graph metanetworks, is intuitive and symmetry-preserving, and shows computational and sample-efficiency benefits across several tasks.
jIvAcVobIh.main_concern: The source of the gains is unclear because some H-GMN runs use GRIT at the coarsened level while the flat baseline does not, and the hierarchy's value as an inductive bias is not isolated.

uGG2zuJPp4.one_liner: Test-time steering of recurrent reasoners that converts intermediate readout probabilities into token-wise pairwise coupling forces in the latent dynamics.
uGG2zuJPp4.problem: Inference-time methods for recurrent reasoning models only run more steps or sample more trajectories, ignoring information revealed within each trajectory.
uGG2zuJPp4.method: Readout Feedback (RoFB) converts the model's intermediate predictions into token-wise pairwise coupling forces injected into the latent dynamics at test time without retraining. The coupling is weighted by readout disagreement and gated by entropy.
uGG2zuJPp4.key_idea: Feed the model's own readout probabilities back as pairwise coupling forces on latent states, weighted by readout disagreement and gated by entropy, closing the inference loop.
uGG2zuJPp4.evidence: Three recurrent models (AKOrN, ItrSA++, TRM) on Sudoku and Maze, compared with running more steps or selecting among multiple trajectories at matched compute, with ARC-AGI-1 as a harder setting where it gives no improvement.
uGG2zuJPp4.claimed_gains: Clear gains in four of six model-task pairs and a small gain in one, reaching performance unattainable by running more steps or selecting from multiple trajectories, at comparable or lower computational cost.
uGG2zuJPp4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-loop, training-free steering idea is novel and timely, with accuracy beyond matched-compute baselines in four of six model-task pairs at small overhead.
uGG2zuJPp4.main_concern: Scope and robustness are narrow: small models on two puzzle tasks, per-pair hyperparameter tuning, gains varying with training seed, no gain on ARC-AGI-1, and constant repulsion matching RoFB on Sudoku.

mjSFbdtfNB.one_liner: Sparse-attention rollouts for long-context RLVR, with dynamic sparsity scheduling that keeps the 5th-percentile acceptance rate above a threshold.
mjSFbdtfNB.problem: Long-context rollout generation dominates RLVR training cost, and using sparse attention as the rollout worker for a dense policy trades training stability against efficiency without a known stable operating point.
mjSFbdtfNB.method: Uses sparse attention as the rollout worker while training a dense policy; a dynamic sparsity scheduler controls the lower-tail (5-percentile) per-token mismatch between sparse and dense policies during generation, and a cost model picks the scheduling that gives the best speedup.
mjSFbdtfNB.key_idea: Keep the lower-tail (5th-percentile) sparse-versus-dense token acceptance rate above a threshold by scheduling sparsity dynamically during generation, instead of tracking average acceptance.
mjSFbdtfNB.evidence: Experiments training Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, and Qwen3-8B with sparse rollout, a study of how the threshold scales with model size, and generalization to Qwen3-14B.
mjSFbdtfNB.claimed_gains: 2.2x, 2.4x, and 2.0x rollout speedups when training Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, and Qwen3-8B, with a 5-percentile mismatch threshold of 0.86 that generally works across model sizes.
mjSFbdtfNB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical and that the lower-tail acceptance rate is a useful stability indicator that enables faster sparse rollouts while largely preserving dense-policy training performance.
mjSFbdtfNB.main_concern: The 5th-percentile metric and 0.86 threshold are justified mainly empirically on three same-family models, with unclear sensitivity to training settings such as importance-sampling clipping and unverified quality under the combined KV-cache quantization speedup.

n4jJegAcQz.one_liner: Benchmark of pretraining and across-animal transfer on multi-region neural recordings from 139 mice, with three task suites.
n4jJegAcQz.problem: Fragmented evaluation protocols and a narrow focus on individual tasks make it hard to test whether large-scale neural recordings yield general-purpose representations that transfer across animals.
n4jJegAcQz.method: Builds BrainWideBench on the International Brain Laboratory Brainwide Map dataset (276 brain regions, 139 mice) with three task suites: behavior decoding, masked or future neural activity prediction, and recovery of anatomical organization. It evaluates pretraining methods under fine-tuning and zero-shot transfer to unseen animals.
n4jJegAcQz.key_idea: Evaluate pretrained neural models on one shared data split across three complementary suites (behavior decoding, neural-activity prediction, anatomy recovery) to measure across-animal transfer.
n4jJegAcQz.evidence: Systematic evaluation of pretraining methods and single-session baselines across transfer settings, including finetuning on downstream objectives and zero-shot generalization to unseen animals, on the IBL Brainwide Map data.
n4jJegAcQz.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that pretrained models generally improve substantially over single-session baselines, with gains depending strongly on transfer setting.
n4jJegAcQz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree a standardized benchmark with three complementary task suites and a broad range of pretrained and single-session baselines is a valuable shared framework for neural recordings.
n4jJegAcQz.main_concern: Conclusions are hard to attribute: negative R2/D2 scores are clipped to zero, some pretrained models add heads or capacity that confound the effect of pretraining, and few-shot or zero-shot behavioral decoding is not evaluated.

V7TOJEo6ZT.one_liner: Hyperbolic IRL parameterizes reward as hyperbolic distance between a feature vector and a learned parameter vector.
V7TOJEo6ZT.problem: Prior IRL reward functions make no assumptions about the geometry of the feature space, which can limit predictive accuracy and interpretability.
V7TOJEo6ZT.method: Reward is a function of hyperbolic distance (or Euclidean distance in a variant) between features and a learned parameter vector, tested on benchmarks and on human navigation among museum exhibits.
V7TOJEo6ZT.key_idea: Define the reward as a function of hyperbolic distance to a learned parameter vector, so that reward geometry is controlled by curvature and exposes feature conjunctions.
V7TOJEo6ZT.evidence: Comparison with linear and nonlinear IRL baselines under deterministic and stochastic policies, plus a museum navigation dataset with feature-coupling analysis.
V7TOJEo6ZT.claimed_gains: Comparable performance to the strongest existing models on established benchmarks, and better results in the low data limit and across dense environments; no numbers stated.
V7TOJEo6ZT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the compact hyperbolic reward is an interesting idea with good sample efficiency, and that the paper is well written.
V7TOJEo6ZT.main_concern: Validation is limited: interaction probes and behavioral checks do not establish conjunctive preferences, a Gaussian Process IRL baseline is missing, and tasks are spatial navigation only.

IFNylIaMx4.one_liner: Adds a small rank-r linear bottleneck in parallel with sparse autoencoders to absorb dense low-rank activation structure before sparse reconstruction.
IFNylIaMx4.problem: SAEs reconstruct the whole residual stream sparsely, although a dense low-rank component that the model relies on resists sparse decomposition and shows up as persistent dense latents.
IFNylIaMx4.method: A rank-r linear bottleneck runs in parallel with standard SAEs (BatchTopK and Matryoshka) so dense structure is absorbed before sparse reconstruction. The authors characterize the absorbed component as top principal components and outlier dimensions and test it with ablations.
IFNylIaMx4.key_idea: Let a parallel low-rank linear path absorb the dense principal-component structure of activations so the sparse dictionary reconstructs only the remainder.
IFNylIaMx4.evidence: Gemma-2-2B layer 12 with a rank-24 bottleneck, replicated on 10 further matched pairs over two model families, five additional sites, and both SAE architectures, plus mean-ablation causal tests.
IFNylIaMx4.claimed_gains: On Gemma-2-2B layer 12, a rank-24 bottleneck reduces dense latent count by up to 83% while improving sparse probing and targeted probe perturbation; mean-ablating the subspace raises next-token cross-entropy from 1.90 to 3.75, and removing the whole dense pathway raises it to 9.3.
IFNylIaMx4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating a dense low-rank component from sparse features is simple, conceptually appealing, and yields useful gains across several interpretability metrics.
IFNylIaMx4.main_concern: Methodological overlap with prior sparse-plus-dense work (Lubana et al., ICLR 2026) is not acknowledged, and generalization is thinly tested (two models, a rank sweep on one setup) with design choices poorly motivated.

jcLUYqqAOU.one_liner: Proves label-noise SGD recovers low-rank matrices in two-layer linear matrix sensing from large initialization, while full-batch GD does not.
jcLUYqqAOU.problem: How stochasticity changes implicit regularization in over-parameterized two-layer linear networks for matrix sensing, beyond the diagonal-network setting.
jcLUYqqAOU.method: Compares full-batch gradient descent with SGD plus additional label noise on the same data and large initialization. For a low-rank target it proves GD does not recover the true matrix while noisy SGD reaches arbitrarily small error, with an empirical study of depth.
jcLUYqqAOU.key_idea: Persistent label noise drives a sharpness-minimizing flow, tying noise covariance to Hessian trace and inducing a weighted nuclear-norm bias toward the low-rank target.
jcLUYqqAOU.evidence: Theorems with proofs under noiseless Gaussian measurements, plus an empirical depth study on a few small synthetic instances (per reviews).
jcLUYqqAOU.claimed_gains: Proves GD fails to recover the true matrix while noisy SGD achieves recovery to arbitrarily small error; no numerical results stated.
jcLUYqqAOU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled comparison (same data, architecture, initialization and step size) and the rigorous GD-versus-noisy-SGD separation beyond diagonal networks.
jcLUYqqAOU.main_concern: The guarantee is existential (step size, stopping time and complexity are not bounded explicitly) and concerns injected label noise rather than the stochasticity of practical SGD.

Ekr8bXkKgX.one_liner: Dataset and benchmark of annotated physical-anomaly tubes plus eye-tracking in AI-generated videos, for evaluating VLM detection and localisation.
Ekr8bXkKgX.problem: Generated videos often misrepresent physical laws, and there is little data to localize such anomalies for explainable detectors or for testing VLM physics understanding.
Ekr8bXkKgX.method: GenTell-Gaze contains 380 generated videos over 80 physics-based scenes and six generators, with 1,070 manually annotated spatio-temporal anomaly tubes and eye-tracking from 129 participants. GenTell-Bench evaluates VLMs on real-versus-generated classification and on recognising, classifying and localising anomalies, and tests whether gaze helps.
Ekr8bXkKgX.key_idea: Pair human-annotated spatio-temporal anomaly tubes with human gaze data on generated videos, so gaze can be tested as an aid to VLM anomaly localisation.
Ekr8bXkKgX.evidence: VLM evaluations from video classification to temporal and spatio-temporal localisation, with and without gaze information.
Ekr8bXkKgX.claimed_gains: VLM performance falls substantially from classification to temporal and spatio-temporal localisation; dataset has 380 videos, 1,070 tubes and 129 participants; no accuracy numbers stated.
Ekr8bXkKgX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark well motivated, with spatio-temporal tube annotations and gaze data filling a data gap and evaluation across multiple settings.
Ekr8bXkKgX.main_concern: Analysis of the gaze data versus the annotations is limited (unclear what each contributes), and the main finding appears driven by the VLMs' baseline bias.

DhZoJjdjzK.one_liner: Shows poison data that teaches nothing alone implants a backdoor trait when mixed with clean data lacking the trigger.
DhZoJjdjzK.problem: Safety methods that audit or filter training data in isolation may miss data that is harmless alone but creates a hidden backdoor in combination.
DhZoJjdjzK.method: Models are fine-tuned on a poison dataset tied to a trait T with and without similarly formatted clean data, and a simple regression model explains the effect: task and trigger co-occur in the poison data so regularization attributes T to the task, while trigger-free clean data shifts attribution to the trigger.
DhZoJjdjzK.key_idea: Clean data without the trigger changes credit assignment: regularization attributes the trait to the task when poison always co-occurs with it, but to the trigger once clean data separates them.
DhZoJjdjzK.evidence: Subliminal learning of backdoor behaviors, inoculation prompting of reward-hacking transcripts, generalization from archaic bird names, and an MNIST classifier with mislabeled data.
DhZoJjdjzK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the phenomenon interesting and the demonstrations strong and comprehensive across subliminal-learning and regular SFT setups.
DhZoJjdjzK.main_concern: Reviewers argue the effect is not very surprising given classic backdoor intuition, and the simple ridge-regression explanation may not justify conclusions for LLMs.

vIKL50JGOJ.one_liner: Reduces adversarial linear MDPs to linear bandits over expected features using an approximate separation oracle for the unknown policy set.
vIKL50JGOJ.problem: For episodic linear MDPs with unknown transitions, adversarial losses and bandit feedback, prior work gets either sqrt(K) regret with an inefficient algorithm or suboptimal K^(3/4) regret.
vIKL50JGOJ.method: The method treats the problem as an adversarial linear bandit whose action set is the policies' expected feature vectors, which is unknown and only estimable through exploration. An approximate separation oracle either returns executable policies from queried features or refines an outer approximation of that set.
vIKL50JGOJ.key_idea: Build an approximate separation oracle that either produces executable policies for queried feature vectors or refines an outer approximation of the unknown set of expected features.
vIKL50JGOJ.evidence: Theoretical regret analysis; no experiments are described in the abstract or reviews.
vIKL50JGOJ.claimed_gains: First sqrt(K) regret with a polynomial-time algorithm, using only aggregate loss feedback, versus K^(3/4) regret for the prior efficient result.
vIKL50JGOJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper closes a long-standing gap by reaching the optimal K-dependence with polynomial computation using interesting techniques.
vIKL50JGOJ.main_concern: The algorithm is polynomial-time but heavy (at least dHK^2 oracle calls) and built from existing components, so its efficiency and technical novelty are questioned.

uMP0RuSTLf.one_liner: Trains a linear query-key projection with a listwise reference-free preference loss plus top-k cross-entropy to reduce attention dimension.
uMP0RuSTLf.problem: It is unclear which training objective for a query-key projection best preserves a pretrained model's behavior, since matching the full attention distribution with KL may not be the best signal, especially in long contexts.
uMP0RuSTLf.method: DimPO combines listwise preference optimization with no reference model and a lightweight top-k cross-entropy term for head fidelity, trained offline from a frozen model's attention patterns with query and key projections optimized independently per layer.
uMP0RuSTLf.key_idea: Treat the key ranking for each query as a listwise preference and also supervise only the top-weighted keys, rather than matching the full attention distribution.
uMP0RuSTLf.evidence: LLaMA3.2-3B, LLaMA3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Qwen3-4B Instruct models on short-context and long-context tasks, with ablations and compatibility tests with SnapKV and MagicPig.
uMP0RuSTLf.claimed_gains: Pairwise preference objectives outperform the triplet objective baseline and, on short-context tasks, retain 98% of the original score when projecting to half the dimension, per the truncated abstract.
uMP0RuSTLf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the objective well motivated and sensible, with consistent gains over baselines, smooth degradation as compression grows, and compatibility with other compression methods.
uMP0RuSTLf.main_concern: Ablations do not separate the ranking loss from the top-k KL term, and the contribution over prior projection methods such as MatryoshkaKV and the handling of RoPE need clarification.

gWVQlRxcOn.one_liner: Benchmark from medRxiv preprint version histories testing whether LLMs still select superseded findings, with unchanged-claim controls.
gWVQlRxcOn.problem: Standard benchmarks cannot separate stale medical knowledge from a failure to acquire current knowledge during pretraining.
gWVQlRxcOn.method: MEDLAPSE derives 1,787 finding lineages from 14,172 multi-version medRxiv preprints. Each superseded finding is matched to its updated successor and to paper-specific retention claims that check familiarity with the paper.
gWVQlRxcOn.key_idea: Pair each superseded finding with an updated successor and unchanged within-paper claims to separate outdated memory from unfamiliarity.
gWVQlRxcOn.evidence: 16 open-weight and commercial LLMs on Q&A tests, plus existing post-hoc correction methods (including unlearning) tested for generalization.
gWVQlRxcOn.claimed_gains: Finding rather than gain: the 16 LLMs select the superseded finding in 30.3% of queries on average while still recalling the retained, unchanged claims.
gWVQlRxcOn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the realistic benchmark built from actual scientific revisions and the broad evaluation of 16 LLMs and correction methods.
gWVQlRxcOn.main_concern: Answering unchanged control claims correctly does not show prior exposure to the paper, and the latest preprint version is not necessarily medical ground truth.

8fY1W6qFzz.one_liner: Offline RL for driving that constrains interaction-level distribution shift using contrastive density-ratio estimation of ego-agent compatibility.
8fY1W6qFzz.problem: Constraining shift only in the ego action space can accept trajectories that are well supported marginally but poorly supported jointly with surrounding agents' logged behavior.
8fY1W6qFzz.method: ICDP decomposes joint-support degradation exactly into an ego-support component and a residual interaction-support component, and recovers the residual through contrastive density-ratio estimation without explicit joint-density modeling or surrounding-agent prediction.
8fY1W6qFzz.key_idea: Estimate the residual interaction-support term by contrastive density-ratio estimation with shared negatives, and use it to constrain reward-driven policy improvement.
8fY1W6qFzz.evidence: Reactive closed-loop nuPlan and InterPlan evaluations, a controlled backbone comparison against BC and unconstrained offline RL, and deployment on a full-scale truck per reviews.
8fY1W6qFzz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the ego-versus-interaction support decomposition a clear, principled motivation, with encouraging closed-loop results.
8fY1W6qFzz.main_concern: Gains are not tied to the interaction-residual mechanism, since ablations against ego-only or joint-score regularization and direct validation of the estimator are missing.

0zKvHiBU5l.one_liner: Online free-energy learning coupling a neural model to biased MD, training several tempering levels with one convex variational objective.
0zKvHiBU5l.problem: Free-energy landscapes over collective variables must be learned without data available in advance, while MD sampling gets trapped in metastable states.
0zKvHiBU5l.method: VESPER uses the evolving neural free-energy model to bias MD, and learns from the difference in mean parameter gradients between biased MD configurations and auxiliary walkers exploring the flattened model in CV space. Levels with different temperature-boosting factors share one minimizer, so all train one model without reweighting, optionally with replica exchange.
0zKvHiBU5l.key_idea: Every tempering level has the physical free energy as the minimizer of a convex variational objective, so data from all levels trains one shared model without reweighting.
0zKvHiBU5l.evidence: A convergence proof for coupled overdamped dynamics without replica exchange under log-Sobolev and Polyak-Lojasiewicz assumptions, analytic landscapes up to 100 dimensions, and alanine peptide and chignolin systems per reviews.
0zKvHiBU5l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the construction principled and elegant, with a convex objective, a common minimizer across tempering levels, and sound theory.
0zKvHiBU5l.main_concern: The benefit of the multi-level ladder and of replica exchange is not separated or shown at matched sampling budget, since four-level ladders use four times the MD.

5jXNrkexEm.one_liner: Shows learned query encoders reach far below the recall document indices allow, and proves statistical-query hardness of learning perfect-recall encoders.
5jXNrkexEm.problem: Recent work studies the embedding dimension needed for retrieval, but not whether learned query encoders can reach the maximum recall of a frozen document index.
5jXNrkexEm.method: They measure the maximum recall achievable for a frozen document index and compare it with learned single-vector query encoders on retrieval benchmarks. They also construct a task with a small one-hidden-layer ReLU perfect-recall encoder that any statistical-query learner needs exponentially many queries to learn.
5jXNrkexEm.key_idea: Separate the geometric capacity of the document index from learnability of the query encoder, using a task with a representable perfect-recall encoder that is SQ-hard to learn.
5jXNrkexEm.evidence: Real-world retrieval benchmarks with Ranking SVM recall as the reference, LoRA-trained encoders per reviews, and a theoretical SQ lower bound.
5jXNrkexEm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments expose unused retrieval capacity and that the SQ lower bound adds theoretical weight by shifting focus to query-side learnability.
5jXNrkexEm.main_concern: Experiments use small training sets and fixed training choices, so learning difficulty is not separated from limited data, and the SQ construction is idealized.

Nd1UxCaWZU.one_liner: Sparse cubical filtrations cut persistent-homology cost for topology-preserving segmentation loss by omitting unimportant regions.
Nd1UxCaWZU.problem: PH-based topology losses are often too slow to use, especially for 3D data with large patches, because runtime is driven by processing information unimportant to the downstream objective.
Nd1UxCaWZU.method: They compute persistent homology on sparse cubical filtrations that omit high-valued regions, following the principles of Betti Matching, and use it as an optimization objective in segmentation training.
Nd1UxCaWZU.key_idea: Drop cubical cells of unimportant, confident regions from the filtration before PH computation, keeping the optimization signal close to the dense counterpart.
Nd1UxCaWZU.evidence: Six datasets in 2D and 3D, comparisons to topology-aware baselines, runtime analysis, threshold ablations and a reduced setting against dense Betti Matching.
Nd1UxCaWZU.claimed_gains: Computational costs reduced by factors of up to 100 on real datasets, and topological accuracy improved by up to 80% across six datasets while maintaining pixel- and region-based accuracy.
Nd1UxCaWZU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method removes a real bottleneck, making PH-based losses practical for large 3D patches, with a broad empirical study across six datasets.
Nd1UxCaWZU.main_concern: Betti-matching error is close to the training objective so the headline gain is less independently convincing, with weaker or mixed changes in VOI, NSD, clDice and Dice.

1rjUGTgKvy.one_liner: Boltzmann generators for the grand canonical ensemble: variable-size models conditioned on chemical potential, or a factorized particle-number plus canonical-density model.
1rjUGTgKvy.problem: Boltzmann generators sample fixed-particle-number systems, so they cannot directly handle grand canonical ensembles where particle numbers fluctuate.
1rjUGTgKvy.method: Two designs: one conditions a variable-size generative model on chemical potential and samples particle number and configuration jointly; the other factorizes the distribution into a particle-number distribution and a canonical Boltzmann density, reusing any existing Boltzmann generator and giving a tractable likelihood for self-normalized importance sampling (SNIS).
1rjUGTgKvy.key_idea: Factorize the grand canonical distribution into p(N) and a canonical Boltzmann density, with the known linear chemical-potential dependence encoded analytically, so any canonical generator can be reused.
1rjUGTgKvy.evidence: Experiments on a Lennard-Jones fluid and methane adsorption in a zeolite, showing grand canonical observables, generalization across chemical potentials, and correction via SNIS and grand canonical Monte Carlo.
1rjUGTgKvy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending Boltzmann generators to variable particle numbers is relevant and useful, the factorized design is simple and principled, and particle-number densities are learned well.
1rjUGTgKvy.main_concern: The practical benefit of correcting the joint distribution is only partly shown (GC-SNIS raises particle-number error and cost comparisons omit generation and likelihood costs), and baselines such as Morph and Metropolis GCMC are weak.

SiLhCnQaZn.one_liner: EvolveGym scores fixed-budget top-variant recovery for directed evolution, and EvolveRank ranks variants via pairwise preference classification.
SiLhCnQaZn.problem: Existing benchmarks such as ProteinGym reward ordering an entire mutational landscape rather than recovering the best variants under the small screening budgets of real directed-evolution rounds.
SiLhCnQaZn.method: EvolveGym covers three tasks (beneficial single mutations, multi-mutant assembly, site-saturated library search) over measured deep mutational scanning data. EvolveRank turns n measurements into all n(n-1)/2 pairwise comparisons and aggregates a learned preference classifier into a global ranking.
SiLhCnQaZn.key_idea: Rank variants by aggregating a learned pairwise preference classifier over all measurement pairs, rather than regressing noisy fitness values.
SiLhCnQaZn.evidence: EvolveGym spans 487 single-substitution assays (96 functional), 44 multi-mutant landscapes and 15 combinatorially complete landscapes, benchmarking 17 methods at a matched budget of 80 measurements.
