SiLhCnQaZn.claimed_gains: EvolveRank places 77.5% of its 16 nominations in the true top 5% of each single-mutation assay at a matched budget of 80 measurements; the abstract is cut off before further comparisons.
SiLhCnQaZn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark measures an outcome that matters in practice, with a clear, simple and effective ranking algorithm and a well-partitioned task and protocol design.
SiLhCnQaZn.main_concern: Methods are benchmarked only on the authors' own tasks without published-split anchors, sensitivity to budget and nomination size is untested, and the tasks and EvolveRank components overlap with existing work.

PfxIWVHXl0.one_liner: Chooses which transferred KV entries to recompute and retain using one receiver-side probe token's attention.
PfxIWVHXl0.problem: In multi-agent LLM systems a sender's imported KV cache is context-dependent and may not match the receiver's context, and the receiver may need only part of the message.
PfxIWVHXl0.method: AttuneKV forwards only the first receiver-side token after the message before any recomputation; layerwise attention ranks message positions for recomputation, and the attention-output change from removing each entry ranks positions for retention.
PfxIWVHXl0.key_idea: One forwarded receiver token's attention ranks message positions for recomputation, and the output change from removing each entry ranks them for retention.
PfxIWVHXl0.evidence: TTFT and memory measured against dense prefill, RelayCaching and CacheBlend at up to 12,288 message tokens, with quality reported on GSM8K, MMLU and HumanEval per the reviews.
PfxIWVHXl0.claimed_gains: At 12,288 incoming tokens, a 2.92× TTFT speedup over dense prefill, 1.45× over RelayCaching and 1.12× over CacheBlend, and 2.0× lower KV-handoff memory (0.75 vs. 1.50 GiB of message KV).
PfxIWVHXl0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-token probe is a cheap, practical way to drive both recompute and retention decisions, with careful timing accounting and notable TTFT and memory reductions.
PfxIWVHXl0.main_concern: Limited novelty, since the recompute and retention scores resemble existing methods (KVShare, SnapKV, CAOTE), and speed and quality are never measured on the same workload.

wjO8F2KPxN.one_liner: Zero-shot LLM-text detector scoring the gap between a frozen surrogate's forward and reversed-text cross-entropy losses.
wjO8F2KPxN.problem: Existing zero-shot detectors measure predictability only in forward reading order and miss a complementary reverse-order signal.
wjO8F2KPxN.method: Tide computes cross-entropy losses of a text and its reversal in one batched call to a frozen surrogate LLM and combines the two losses into a single directional asymmetry score.
wjO8F2KPxN.key_idea: LLM-generated text loses disproportionately more predictability than human text when reversed, so the forward-reverse loss asymmetry serves as the detection score.
wjO8F2KPxN.evidence: A new dataset of 225,000 documents across five domains, five frontier LLMs, six languages and six adversarial attacks, compared with nine zero-shot baselines.
wjO8F2KPxN.claimed_gains: Average AUROC of 0.978, 4.7% higher than the best of nine zero-shot baselines, and it nearly doubles the true-positive figure at a 0.1% false-positive rate (sentence truncated in the abstract).
wjO8F2KPxN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, cheap and zero-shot, with extensive experiments across domains, generators and attacks showing clear gains over baselines.
wjO8F2KPxN.main_concern: It is unclear that reversal specifically is responsible, since other perturbations such as block shuffling perform almost the same, and novelty over prior reverse-loss detectors is limited.

rKWA7Zj17a.one_liner: Proves that coupled attention and value gradient dynamics make multi-head softmax transformers specialize heads by latent component in ICL.
rKWA7Zj17a.problem: How multiple attention heads learn to specialize during training for in-context learning lacks theoretical understanding.
rKWA7Zj17a.method: They analyze training dynamics and generalization of a multi-head softmax transformer on compositional ICL tasks, where each input has several latent components independently mapped to output components, jointly tracking attention and value parameters.
rKWA7Zj17a.key_idea: Coupled gradient updates of attention and value parameters amplify weak initial differences between heads into complementary roles, each head matching and retrieving a different latent component.
rKWA7Zj17a.evidence: Finite-step convergence and generalization to unseen component combinations and out-of-domain pattern families are proved, with validation on synthetic and real experiments.
rKWA7Zj17a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of head specialization in ICL is interesting and the finite-step analysis of coupled attention and value updates is technically solid within the studied setting.
rKWA7Zj17a.main_concern: The theory depends on a restrictive setup, with heads initialized near the true component subspaces and independent latent components, so specialization from random initialization is not explained.

oo5nCPTX5o.one_liner: Stochastic implicit DC method for Fréchet regression on bounded-curvature manifolds, sampling positive-weight terms with a logarithmic correction for variance reduction.
oo5nCPTX5o.problem: Fréchet regression has query-dependent, possibly negative weights; difference-of-convex methods are mostly limited to Hadamard manifolds and curvature-aware methods need repeated full-data model evaluations.
oo5nCPTX5o.method: VERI-FRIDA samples the positively weighted terms and adds a logarithmic correction so the model gradient equals variance-reduced estimates of the full gradient. It links inexact implicit updates to estimator error to obtain two convergence guarantees under explicit geometric and negative-weight conditions.
oo5nCPTX5o.key_idea: Sample the positively weighted squared-distance terms and add a logarithmic tangent-space correction so the sampled model's gradient equals a variance-reduced estimate of the full gradient.
oo5nCPTX5o.evidence: Convergence theory under geometric and negative-weight conditions covering several variance-reduced estimators, plus experiments whose details are not visible in the truncated abstract.
oo5nCPTX5o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the model construction well motivated and the theoretical analysis comprehensive, with a unified condition covering several estimators.
oo5nCPTX5o.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the method combines FRIDA with existing Riemannian variance-reduced estimators under a standard analysis template, and assumptions (small geodesic ball, bounded negative weight) restrict practical scope.

oImZFKHFgl.one_liner: Federated VLN where heterogeneous clients share language-side modules and locally trained generative replay, avoiding averaging incompatible navigator backbones.
oImZFKHFgl.problem: Federated vision-language navigation averages native models, which requires matching parameter shapes, so agents with different capacities cannot collaborate.
oImZFKHFgl.method: Four stages train a human-instruction encoder and transformation, a federated Speaker that turns local route context into pseudo-instructions, a feature generator aligned with human features, and pseudo-instruction navigation. Clients upload only the designated shared modules and keep their own navigator; inference uses the human-instruction path.
oImZFKHFgl.key_idea: Share only compatible language-side modules through a common instruction-feature interface while each client keeps its own navigator, with a federated Speaker supplying pseudo-instructions from local routes.
oImZFKHFgl.evidence: R2R validation split (1,021 held-out instructions, 56 seen environments) and 2,349 human instructions in 11 unseen environments, with comparisons against FedVLN baselines.
oImZFKHFgl.claimed_gains: Mixed federation reaches 64.45% SR and 61.69% SPL on R2R validation; cross-width sharing beats within-width sharing by 3.134 points in pooled SR and 3.225 points in pooled SPL.
oImZFKHFgl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sharing a language interface is a sensible, well-motivated way for clients with different parameter dimensions to collaborate, with positive cross-group gains.
oImZFKHFgl.main_concern: Heterogeneity is narrow (two widths of the same Seq2Seq Listener), the contribution of each of the four stages is not isolated, and communication, memory and compute costs are unmeasured.

1LQg9N8lly.one_liner: Benchmark of human-written, open-ended image and video questions probing implicit temporal, spatial, social and abstract inference in multimodal LLMs.
1LQg9N8lly.problem: Existing visual benchmarks target either expert-level academic analysis or low-level perception, leaving the intuitive reasoning people do about implicit information largely untested.
1LQg9N8lly.method: HSS spans diverse image and video inputs organized under a structured taxonomy, with each item paired with human-written prompts. Reviews describe 522 tasks across 11 subdomains that survived three review rounds out of 3,466 authored tasks, scored on free-form answers.
1LQg9N8lly.key_idea: Test implicit inference rather than explicit perception, using curated natural image and video items whose answers must be inferred, such as past causes, affordances and social authority.
1LQg9N8lly.evidence: Many MLLM families evaluated against twenty human annotators, with alternative LLM judges, frame-budget sweeps and paired agentic comparisons per the reviews.
1LQg9N8lly.claimed_gains: Participants reach 93.1% accuracy while state-of-the-art models fall well short; reviews cite the best model at 53.6%.
1LQg9N8lly.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it fills an under-served axis (implicit inference versus explicit perception) with rigorous curation and a large, hard-to-saturate human-model gap.
1LQg9N8lly.main_concern: The 93.1% human baseline is under-documented (possible overlap with task authors, no response-time control), and subdomain-level analyses rest on few items without uncertainty estimates.

FITdNxccVZ.one_liner: Physics-guided graph masked autoencoder whose decoder analytically fixes the conservation-determined flow component, enabling virtual sensing beyond sensor coverage.
FITdNxccVZ.problem: Flow networks have sensors on only a subset of edges, so the network state is partially known and anomalies outside sensor coverage can go undetected.
FITdNxccVZ.method: A graph masked autoencoder on the full network uses incidence-aware message passing and adaptive masking. Its decoder lets conservation parameterize the reconstruction space, analytically determining the constrained component of missing flow and learning only the remaining degrees of freedom, and a time-series foundation model adds zero-shot transfer and anomaly detection.
FITdNxccVZ.key_idea: Parameterize the reconstruction space by flow conservation, solving the constrained component analytically and learning only the remaining null-space degrees of freedom inside a masked graph autoencoder.
FITdNxccVZ.evidence: Experiments on physical flow networks, including traffic and power networks per the reviews, against diverse baselines, plus anomaly detection on unobserved edges from reconstructed flows.
FITdNxccVZ.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims substantially improved flow reconstruction over diverse baselines, with larger gains farther from observed sensors.
FITdNxccVZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining conservation constraints with graph learning through null-space projection is a reasonable way to reconstruct flows beyond sensor coverage, with gains under sparse sensing.
FITdNxccVZ.main_concern: The incremental contribution is not isolated from prior work such as FlowSymm and existing time-series graph foundation models, and the zero-shot evaluation setting is unclear.

k3Fq32o5Lm.one_liner: Per-client memory windows sized to noise, arrival rate and drift, refreshed by restarted accelerated solves, for tracking drifting federated objectives.
k3Fq32o5Lm.problem: A single shared window makes a fast-changing client carry the sampling noise of a slow, nearly stationary one when the server tracks the minimizer of the clients' weighted average loss.
k3Fq32o5Lm.method: Each client keeps a memory window sized to its own noise, arrival rate and drift rate, refreshed by a restarted accelerated method starting from a common point. The paper proves a tracking-error upper bound and a lower bound that puts different groups of clients on different drift clocks.
k3Fq32o5Lm.key_idea: Size each client's retained history to its own noise, arrival rate and drift instead of using one common window; tracking error then depends on per-client weighted terms.
k3Fq32o5Lm.evidence: Upper and lower bound theory, plus experiments on weather (temperature station) data and clinic records per the reviews.
k3Fq32o5Lm.claimed_gains: Tracking error bounded by R(sum of w_m^{3/2} sigma_m sqrt(gamma_m/lambda_m))^{2/3}, never worse than any common window and strictly better when noise and drift are uneven; bounds agree up to a constant for boundedly many refresh scales.
k3Fq32o5Lm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well formulated and the client-wise tracking quantity with a matching lower bound a meaningful theoretical result, with simple experiments supporting when client-specific windows should help.
k3Fq32o5Lm.main_concern: Practical evidence is limited: the rule needs known drift and noise bounds, and gains largely disappear in recorded weather order and shrink against a data-floored common window in the clinic study.

pv7nN90v3n.one_liner: Bayes-referenced criterion relating forecast amplitude to target alignment to separate excessive contraction from optimal averaging in time series forecasts.
pv7nN90v3n.problem: Forecasts vary less than observed futures and this is read as over-smoothing, yet the Bayes-optimal predictor under squared loss also averages over plausible futures, so reduced variation alone does not show a deficiency.
pv7nN90v3n.method: A framework for variation across predictions for similar inputs and within forecast trajectories derives an observable criterion linking predictive amplitude to target alignment, identifying excessive contraction along the current prediction direction without estimating the Bayes-optimal predictor.
pv7nN90v3n.key_idea: Under squared loss, the optimal scalar rescaling of a prediction toward realized targets matches rescaling toward the Bayes-optimal predictor in expectation, so excess contraction is observable from data alone.
pv7nN90v3n.evidence: Eight forecasting models across six benchmark datasets, with lookback and horizon fixed to 96 per the reviews.
pv7nN90v3n.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract reports that predictive contraction is widespread and that stronger contraction is consistently associated with larger forecasting error.
pv7nN90v3n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it offers a useful hyperparameter-free diagnostic that challenges the assumption that reduced forecast variation is itself a model deficiency.
pv7nN90v3n.main_concern: The Bayes-referenced identity holds only in expectation yet is applied to single noisy target realizations at window level, and novelty over prior rescaling and error-decomposition work is not established.

zOQ0HAXFKi.one_liner: Native-resolution convolutional VLM encoders plus quantized location tokens with Gaussian distance-aware loss for fast on-device dense grounding.
zOQ0HAXFKi.problem: On-device generalist VLMs with dense grounding face costly high-resolution visual encoding and lengthy autoregressive decoding of many spatial locations.
zOQ0HAXFKi.method: FastVLM2 adapts pretrained ConvNeXt and FastViTHD backbones to arbitrary resolutions through instruction tuning, represents grounding outputs with quantized location tokens, and adds a Gaussian distance-aware soft cross-entropy loss to recover accuracy lost to quantization. It also introduces a training-free confidence estimator for grounding.
zOQ0HAXFKi.key_idea: Adapt conv/hybrid encoders to native resolution for cheap input, and quantize coordinates into location tokens trained with a Gaussian distance-aware soft cross-entropy for cheap output.
zOQ0HAXFKi.evidence: VQA and grounding benchmarks (RefCOCO, COCO mAP per the reviews) on a MacBook M1 Max against Qwen3-VL-4B, with ablations on positional encoding, training schedules, coordinate initialization, losses and confidence scoring.
zOQ0HAXFKi.claimed_gains: FastVLM2-4B matches Qwen3-VL-4B on VQA accuracy with 4.6x lower prefill latency on an M1 Max, and quantized location tokens cut the output-token budget by over 60% versus textual coordinates.
zOQ0HAXFKi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives a strong accuracy-latency trade-off on shared hardware, a useful training-free confidence score, and extensive ablations.
zOQ0HAXFKi.main_concern: Individual techniques are largely established (FastVLM backbone, CoordConv, 2D RoPE, quantized tokens), and ablations use shorter schedules and different LLM backbones than the final five-stage SFT plus RL model.

FQLXFg2bba.one_liner: Near-isometric residual layer (normalization, shifted ReLU, 1/K depth scaling) keeps Jacobians well conditioned so deep RL networks train stably.
FQLXFg2bba.problem: RL agents still use networks a few layers deep because adding layers degrades performance: hidden-layer Jacobians drift from isometry and features lose rank under the non-stationary, bootstrapped RL objective.
FQLXFg2bba.method: A simple residual layer keeps deep networks close to an isometry; reviews describe it as a residual layer with normalization, shifted ReLU and a 1/K depth scaling factor, motivated by NTK analysis of Jacobian singular values and feature rank.
FQLXFg2bba.key_idea: Keep each layer's Jacobian near an isometry with a residual block scaled by 1/K, so deviations do not multiply with depth and features keep rank.
FQLXFg2bba.evidence: Per the reviews, five algorithms (PQN, SAC, TD3, PPO and goal-conditioned), five benchmarks, three optimizers and depths from 1 to 64, against SimbaV2 and multi-skip baselines.
FQLXFg2bba.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims deep networks train stably across value-based, actor-critic and goal-conditioned algorithms and outperform shallow networks and recent deep architectures at matched depth and parameters.
FQLXFg2bba.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple, theory-motivated fix with a clear analysis of why depth fails in RL, backed by broad experiments across algorithms, benchmarks and optimizers.
FQLXFg2bba.main_concern: Baseline comparisons are uneven (SimbaV2 only on SAC, optimizers differ between proposed and baseline networks), compute cost of depth is not weighed, and most results use only three seeds.

DR0qHuYqlL.one_liner: Empirical audit of how MoE compression (expert merging, pruning, quantization, sparsity) and calibration data mix change fairness, bias and safety.
DR0qHuYqlL.problem: The fairness, bias and safety effects of compressing MoE language models, especially expert compression and its calibration data, are poorly understood.
DR0qHuYqlL.method: A study across three MoE architectures that compares compression algorithms and calibration data mixtures on fairness and safety behavior, adds prompt-matched generation diagnostics, and runs targeted expert-level interventions.
DR0qHuYqlL.key_idea: Measure fairness, bias and safety changes under several compression families and calibration mixtures, then probe individual experts to show that removing a few can flip refusals.
DR0qHuYqlL.evidence: Per the reviews, three architectures, nine methods, two compression ratios, three calibration mixtures and three seeds, evaluated on BBQ, ToxiGen, CrowS-Pairs, AdvBench, XSTest and IFEval.
DR0qHuYqlL.claimed_gains: Pruning just three of the 6,144 experts in Qwen3-30B-A3B can turn a refusal of a harmful AdvBench request into compliance, whereas 8-bit and group-wise 4-bit quantization of the same experts never change the refusal.
DR0qHuYqlL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is timely and the experimental matrix is broad, adding a safety dimension that MoE compression work usually omits.
DR0qHuYqlL.main_concern: Findings are largely descriptive with limited mitigation guidance, and safety and bias measurement is fragile (AdvBench is dated, substring matching, ToxiGen near chance at baseline, an arbitrary aggregate metric).

lXKpB0x7vq.one_liner: Parameter-free soft-argmax averaging sign-invariant quadratic Veronese features to read out lines on the projective plane.
lXKpB0x7vq.problem: Undirected lines have two sign-related parameter representatives, so no coordinate domain admits an average that respects proximity, and standard soft-argmax can miss a target on which the evidence concentrates.
lXKpB0x7vq.method: Veronese soft-argmax averages sign-invariant quadratic features of candidates and recovers the line from their average. The same representation yields a training objective whose value bounds the error of the recovered line.
lXKpB0x7vq.key_idea: Average sign-invariant quadratic (Veronese) features instead of signed coordinates, recover the line from the averaged matrix, and reuse the same representation for the loss.
lXKpB0x7vq.evidence: Proofs that predictions approach the target as evidence concentrates, with sufficient conditions for uniqueness on real projective spaces of any dimension; synthetic line experiments and horizon estimation in real images.
lXKpB0x7vq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it pins down a concrete geometric failure of coordinate readouts with an explicit counterexample and offers a simple, parameter-free, mathematically sound fix.
lXKpB0x7vq.main_concern: Measured gains are not clearly tied to the failure the theory explains (they appear mainly under unseen strong noise), and real-image baseline configurations were tuned on test performance with little stability evidence.

nNsH1TaHkL.one_liner: Finite-sample comparison of clipped and unclipped Polyak-Ruppert averaged SGD under heavy-tailed noise with finite p-th moments.
nNsH1TaHkL.problem: Gradient clipping is widely used to stabilize training, but it may not improve the statistical accuracy of averaged SGD even under heavy-tailed noise.
nNsH1TaHkL.method: Derives high-probability finite-sample bounds for clipped and unclipped averaged SGD under finite conditional p-th moments with p at least 2, shows sharpness of the unclipped heavy-tail term via an exact one-dimensional quadratic recursion, extends to projected convex SGD, and gives concrete costs of clipping.
nNsH1TaHkL.key_idea: Unclipped averaged SGD's Gaussian term dominates its deviation bound under explicit accuracy/confidence conditions, so clipping need not help; fixed clipping inflates variance or shifts the limit.
nNsH1TaHkL.evidence: Theoretical bounds (Theorems 3.1 and 3.2, Proposition 5.1), a scalar Gaussian quadratic example, and a small quadratic prediction experiment per the reviews.
nNsH1TaHkL.claimed_gains: The heavy-tail correction depends logarithmically rather than polynomially on the inverse failure probability; at p=2 the confidence dependence of the leading bound improves; every fixed finite threshold increases asymptotic variance on a scalar Gaussian quadratic.
nNsH1TaHkL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a meaningful theoretical contribution with explicit accuracy-confidence conditions that quantify when unclipped averaging is Gaussian-dominated, plus concrete costs of clipping.
nNsH1TaHkL.main_concern: Comparison with existing high-probability bounds is not clearly articulated, so novelty is hard to assess, and the single quadratic experiment with fixed-threshold clipping limits practical guidance.

Tt2J9vywNs.one_liner: Recurrent per-token memory across transformer layers, updated by recursive least squares, unifying residual, AttnRes and mHC depth mixing.
Tt2J9vywNs.problem: Residual connections accumulate layer outputs additively, and newer depth-aggregation alternatives such as mHC and AttnRes lack a unified view of storing and retrieving information across layers.
Tt2J9vywNs.method: Depth Memory frames depth mixing as a memory stream that is queried to enrich each layer's input and written back with the layer's output. Linear Depth Memory propagates a residual, a memory and an inverse-covariance stream, solving a depth regression online with recursive least squares, with a hardware-aware implementation that cuts peak activation memory.
Tt2J9vywNs.key_idea: Treat depth mixing as online regression: a memory stream read before each layer and updated after it by recursive least squares, alongside the standard residual stream.
Tt2J9vywNs.evidence: Language-model comparisons against PreLN, mHC and Block AttnRes at 400M and 1.5B scale per the reviews, ablations swapping RLS for delta-rule or outer-product updates, and throughput and memory measurements.
Tt2J9vywNs.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract; reviews report about 1% additional parameters over PreLN and a validation perplexity of 9.15 at 1.5B.
Tt2J9vywNs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a coherent, well-motivated framework that unifies PreLN, AttnRes and mHC, preserves the residual path, and improves perplexity.
Tt2J9vywNs.main_concern: Empirical gains are modest relative to added complexity: RLS beats simpler delta-rule and outer-product updates by only 0.0041 and 0.0050 nats in single-seed ablations, with higher training memory and lower throughput than Block AttnRes.

CHy7sejNlH.one_liner: Trains TRM-style recurrent reasoners from terminal verifier or energy feedback alone, without ground-truth solutions.
CHy7sejNlH.problem: Recursive reasoning models are typically trained on ground-truth solutions, which are unavailable for many constraint satisfaction and combinatorial optimization problems.
CHy7sejNlH.method: The solution-free variant (uTRM) combines latent deterministic recurrence with stochastic refinement of explicit candidate assignments, trained from a black-box verifier or energy function's terminal feedback (via PPO per a review). Credit assignment is truncated to the final recursive cycle.
CHy7sejNlH.key_idea: Train latent recurrence plus stochastic candidate refinement with RL on terminal verifier feedback, truncating credit assignment to the final recursive cycle to enable depth extrapolation.
CHy7sejNlH.evidence: Graph Coloring, Maximum Independent Set and Sudoku (Sudoku-Extreme), under sequential batch-one evaluation and parallel draws, with test-time scaling along latent recurrence, explicit refinement and parallel search axes.
CHy7sejNlH.claimed_gains: Matches the strongest published result on 5-color, 50-node Graph Coloring under batch-one evaluation, and solves 93.90% of Sudoku-Extreme puzzles with 100 independent parallel draws per puzzle.
CHy7sejNlH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is relevant and the paper is clear, with promising results on MIS and Sudoku and a sensible motivation for learning without solutions.
CHy7sejNlH.main_concern: Experiments do not convincingly show superiority: Layer Evals is only a proxy for compute, baselines are not evaluated uniformly across problems, verifiers are unspecified, and novelty over unsupervised-objective TRM training is limited.

cBsfDpH5EP.one_liner: Recycles discarded noisy queries into new post-training tasks via a source-grounded instruction generator guided by induced-response quality.
cBsfDpH5EP.problem: Quality-based selection discards many real-user preference examples that have limited value in their original form but may still be useful sources of supervision.
cBsfDpH5EP.method: ReSource uses noisy queries as sources for new tasks, trains a source-grounded instruction generator, and uses the quality of induced responses as a proxy for instruction utility to guide both training and instruction selection. Reviews add that the recycler is trained with SFT and GRPO and preference pairs use ArmoRM best/worst selection.
cBsfDpH5EP.key_idea: Convert a rejected query into a new task grounded in its content, scoring candidate instructions by the quality of the responses they induce.
cBsfDpH5EP.evidence: Source-matched comparisons of recycled versus raw supervision on AlpacaEval2, Arena-Hard and WildBench across training-data amounts, plus mixing with retained data and training other models.
cBsfDpH5EP.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims recycling consistently improves downstream performance over raw supervision across three benchmarks and different amounts of training data.
cBsfDpH5EP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the source-matched comparisons show recycling beats raw supervision, and that reusing discarded data is practically useful.
cBsfDpH5EP.main_concern: Baselines are limited (no query-rewriting or standard synthetic-instruction baselines) and total construction cost is not matched, so it is unclear where the gain comes from.

fIcuQrilGL.one_liner: Probabilistic wildlife movement forecaster for any species and horizon, using ecologically inspired architecture shared across spatiotemporal scales.
fIcuQrilGL.problem: Existing wildlife movement forecasters only modestly outperform simple statistical approaches and are specialized to individual species and predefined forecasting horizons.
fIcuQrilGL.method: STEPPY produces forecasts for any species and any time horizon dynamically at prediction time, using ecologically inspired architectural designs that learn patterns shared across species and scales, without explicit environmental predictors. Reviews cite components such as space and time relative positional encoding, history inputs and a decoder.
fIcuQrilGL.key_idea: One model trained across species and scales, with ecologically inspired inputs, relative space-time positional encoding and a decoder that forecasts at arbitrary horizons at prediction time.
fIcuQrilGL.evidence: Evaluation built on MoveBench (per a review) on future trajectories of seen and held-out individuals with probabilistic metrics such as Energy Score, plus ablations of each component.
fIcuQrilGL.claimed_gains: Improves probabilistic forecasting by 18% on future trajectories of individuals seen in training and 20% on held-out individuals, without explicit environmental predictors.
fIcuQrilGL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it shows clearly better forecasting accuracy than prior baselines, with a complete ablation study and good handling of context length and temporal gaps.
fIcuQrilGL.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited because all components are existing modules, and the work looks incremental over the MoveBench dataset paper, with thin baseline and metric descriptions.

xguY6fI02Y.one_liner: Proves minimax rates showing learning against monotone adversaries pays an inherent log(n/d) factor beyond VC dimension one.
xguY6fI02Y.problem: Larsen et al. showed ERM attains O((d/n)log(n/d)) under monotone adversarial insertions and asked whether the extra logarithm is an artifact of specific algorithms or inherent to the lack of exchangeability.
xguY6fI02Y.method: Constructs lower bounds over classes of VC dimension d and known finite insertion budgets that match the ERM upper bound, and extends the same rates to Littlestone dimension. Reviews note the lower bound uses a deliberately constructed class and about n^2 appended examples.
xguY6fI02Y.key_idea: Build hypothesis classes where correctly labeled insertions that depend on the clean sample break exchangeability and force an extra log(n/d) factor on any learner.
xguY6fI02Y.evidence: Theoretical minimax analysis only; no experiments are mentioned.
xguY6fI02Y.claimed_gains: Minimax expected error is Theta(1/n) at d=1 and Theta((d/n)log(n/d)) for d at least 2, and the same rates hold with Littlestone dimension, so the online-to-batch rate O(d_L/n) is unattainable.
xguY6fI02Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it cleanly resolves open questions from prior work with a lower bound that applies to any learner and separates monotone-adversary learning from PAC learning.
xguY6fI02Y.main_concern: Results are limited in scope (only a logarithmic gap, proven for a deliberately constructed class), and the construction and proof are hard to follow without more intuition.

6Fddxv0uZa.one_liner: GRPO-trained agent that selects actions together with natural-language creativity levels to generate more diverse, original scientific ideas.
6Fddxv0uZa.problem: LLMs' low-entropy bias yields homogeneous, predictable outputs that limit open-ended scientific ideation.
6Fddxv0uZa.method: AI Night-Scientist models creativity along action, process and outcome axes and trains models with GRPO, exposing them to varying degrees and forms of creativity so they learn when and how to depart from predictable reasoning. Reviews describe creativity as controlled through action-specific natural-language instructions.
6Fddxv0uZa.key_idea: Reinforcement learning over actions paired with semantic creativity-level instructions teaches the model when to explore versus exploit, instead of raising decoding temperature.
6Fddxv0uZa.evidence: Comparisons with the base model, RL-trained ReAct and temperature-controlled agents, measuring diversity of research directions and contribution types, predicted citation impact and originality, with a human study.
6Fddxv0uZa.claimed_gains: Expands research directions by 27.8% and contribution types by 14.9% over the base model, and improves predicted citation impact by up to 32.0 percentage points and originality by 66.2 points.
6Fddxv0uZa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that controlling exploration through interpretable action-level creativity instructions is useful and that the comparisons with RL-trained ReAct and temperature baselines are valuable.
6Fddxv0uZa.main_concern: The reward is not validated as a proxy for useful novelty, and the strongest RL baseline (ReAct-RL) already captures much of the gain, so the benefit of creativity levels is smaller than the abstract's headline numbers.

U3lkSsdT33.one_liner: Regresses the velocity at re-noised states toward the reference velocity shifted by the clean sample's reward gradient, avoiding trajectory backpropagation.
U3lkSsdT33.problem: Transporting reward gradients backward along sampling trajectories is prohibitively expensive, and existing first-order approximations estimate trajectories with few-step samples and evaluate reward gradients off-policy.
U3lkSsdT33.method: SERF re-noises endpoint samples and regresses the trained velocity at the re-noised states against the reference velocity shifted by the clean image's reward gradient. The objective is motivated through stochastic optimal control as an approximation to the true reward gradient direction.
U3lkSsdT33.key_idea: Replace backward gradient transport with the reward gradient at the clean endpoint, applied as a shift to the reference velocity at independently re-noised states.
U3lkSsdT33.evidence: Post-training Stable Diffusion 3.5 on PickScore and HPSv2.1, compared with existing methods on reward improvement, image quality, output diversity and training efficiency.
U3lkSsdT33.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims favorable trade-offs among reward improvement, image quality and output diversity versus existing methods, and high efficiency.
U3lkSsdT33.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple, computationally efficient alternative to full-trajectory reward backpropagation, with no trajectory storage and a strong reward-quality-diversity trade-off.
U3lkSsdT33.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to RSM and other endpoint-gradient and re-noising work, related work is incomplete, and the theoretical guarantees rely on a Gaussian location-family assumption that needs clearer qualification.

IlNqX0B95x.one_liner: Caches per-token random projections of teacher hidden states, coarsely quantized, to run hidden-state distillation offline at logit-distillation cost.
IlNqX0B95x.problem: Hidden-state distillation has no compact offline counterpart to cached logit distillation: existing methods either run teacher inference inside the training loop or need enormous storage.
IlNqX0B95x.method: A per-token random projection of the teacher's hidden states, coarsely quantized, is stored as the cache, so hidden-state distillation runs from a cache of the same order of size as the logit cache. Reviews note the loss computed from the sketch is an unbiased estimator of the true loss.
IlNqX0B95x.key_idea: Compress teacher hidden states with a per-token random projection plus coarse quantization, so the sketch-based loss is an unbiased estimate of the full hidden-state distillation loss.
IlNqX0B95x.evidence: Four teachers of 1.5B to 8B parameters, student runs of up to 15B tokens, held-out loss at 1B tokens and downstream accuracy, against full-state and logit-only distillation.
IlNqX0B95x.claimed_gains: With 32x compression, students need at most about 2% more training tokens than full-hidden-state students to reach the same held-out loss at 1B tokens and about 1% more over runs up to 15B tokens, while logit-only students need 1.4 to 1.7 times as many.
IlNqX0B95x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is well motivated and theoretically justified, cuts cache storage substantially, and nearly matches full-state distillation.
IlNqX0B95x.main_concern: Evidence is limited to at most 15B tokens in a single pass with single-layer supervision, logit baselines lack the ground-truth CE term, and novelty relative to concurrent work needs discussion.

TZJ8Z6Dl0M.one_liner: Quantizes tensor-parallel all-reduce using frozen, calibration-derived communication scales shared across ranks and requests, avoiding scale-agreement rounds.
TZJ8Z6Dl0M.problem: Tensor-parallel all-reduce still communicates in BF16 and takes a large share of prefill time (up to 37% on DeepSeek-V3.1), and dynamic quantization would need an extra communication round for scale agreement.
TZJ8Z6Dl0M.method: Quantar freezes communication scales calibrated once and shares them across ranks and requests so reduced values map back to the correct sum. Reviews add that it uses FP16 accumulation, NVLS and fused producer/consumer operations.
TZJ8Z6Dl0M.key_idea: Use static, calibration-time scales shared by all ranks so quantized values can be summed directly in the all-reduce, with widened accumulation to avoid repeated FP8 rounding.
TZJ8Z6Dl0M.evidence: Eight B300 GPUs and eight RTX PRO 6000 GPUs on dense and MoE models, compared with per-hop FP8, with MMLU-Pro and nine benchmarks across 33 subtasks for quality.
TZJ8Z6Dl0M.claimed_gains: Up to 1.81x faster communication boundary and 1.28x faster prefill on eight B300 GPUs (1.92x and 1.61x on eight RTX PRO 6000), up to 1.24x over per-hop FP8, and MMLU-Pro changes by at most 0.42 percentage points across five models.
TZJ8Z6Dl0M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a coherent algorithm-system solution to a real communication bottleneck, with end-to-end measurements on modern multi-GPU systems and near-BF16 accuracy.
TZJ8Z6Dl0M.main_concern: The static-scale choice (calibration maximum times a fixed headroom of 32) is not systematically justified, the theory adds little beyond general static quantization feasibility, and decoding is not evaluated.

XKwX0wrBv9.one_liner: Learns an SDE's transition kernel with boundary-conditioned flow architecture trained on Chapman-Kolmogorov consistency from trajectory-free marginal samples.
XKwX0wrBv9.problem: Observing transitions in SDEs such as molecular dynamics needs millions of sequential integration steps, and existing supervised amortization approaches require long simulated trajectory data.
XKwX0wrBv9.method: KC-maps model the distribution of the process integrated from an initial time and state to any given time (the weak solution), using only marginal samples plus known drift and diffusion coefficients. Boundary conditions are built into the architecture (normalizing-flow coupling layers per a review) and the Chapman-Kolmogorov equation supplies the training objective.
XKwX0wrBv9.key_idea: Enforce boundary conditions in the network architecture and train only a two-hop Chapman-Kolmogorov consistency loss, so the transition kernel is learned from marginal samples and known drift and diffusion.
XKwX0wrBv9.evidence: A toy potential and three peptides per the reviews, assessing equilibrium distributions, mode coverage and TICA, energy and torsion W2 against baselines; the abstract is truncated before results.
XKwX0wrBv9.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; reviews report faster simulation and better exploration of metastable states than baselines.
XKwX0wrBv9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Chapman-Kolmogorov formulation is elegant and well written, fills a literature gap, and shows faster simulation and better metastable-state exploration.
XKwX0wrBv9.main_concern: Kinetics are not validated (no transition rates or relaxation times), the practical benefit is unclear since training still needs many MD-generated configurations, and experiments are limited.

Ne1CKI7ey9.one_liner: Optimizes diffusion noise with Sep-CMA-ES against kinematic and inverse-dynamics feasibility constraints, making motion physically feasible without retraining.
Ne1CKI7ey9.problem: Motion diffusion models generate diverse motion that often violates physical constraints, limiting use in simulation and control.
Ne1CKI7ey9.method: At inference time, PhysibleMDM runs black-box optimization of the diffusion noise with Sep-CMA-ES against surrogate constraints: kinematic checks (ground penetration, slip, self-collision) and dynamic feasibility from a cone-program inverse-dynamics inner loop. An autoregressive scheme chains optimized segments into long sequences.
Ne1CKI7ey9.key_idea: Search the diffusion noise gradient-free with Sep-CMA-ES to minimize surrogate kinematic and inverse-dynamics residual costs, leaving the pretrained motion model frozen.
Ne1CKI7ey9.evidence: 100 motion styles on an SMPL humanoid and 11 sequences for a custom bipedal robot, compared with several baselines including gradient-based ones, plus a downstream RL tracking experiment per the reviews.
Ne1CKI7ey9.claimed_gains: Reduces mean ground penetration, self-collision penetration and ground slip by 75%, 92% and 74% on the SMPL humanoid, and gives a median 89.5% reduction in per-sequence mean acceleration-reconstruction error on a bipedal robot (remaining figures truncated).
Ne1CKI7ey9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is training-free and practical, with gradient-free search suited to non-smooth contact constraints, an inverse-dynamics feasibility proxy, and consistent gains across kinematic and dynamic metrics.
Ne1CKI7ey9.main_concern: The optimization is very slow (about 4,515 seconds per horizon in the bipedal jump), results are single stochastic runs without variance, dynamic evaluation is thin, and PhysDiff is not compared.

orXzecE63B.one_liner: Nearly tight space bounds for attention approximation when key-query cosine similarities lie in a small interval around zero.
orXzecE63B.problem: Prior near-tight worst-case space bounds for attention rely on instances where queries align perfectly with keys, contradicting the anisotropy observed in real transformers.
orXzecE63B.method: Assumes key/query cosine similarities lie in a small interval around zero, then gives a nearly space-optimal algorithm (importance sampling per the reviews) with a matching space lower bound, and shows uniform sampling is nearly optimal for a typical parameter range.
orXzecE63B.key_idea: Restrict query-key cosine similarity to a small interval and use sensitivity-based sampling to compress the KV cache, with a matching lower bound whose hard instances exhibit anisotropy.
orXzecE63B.evidence: Upper and lower bound proofs, plus empirical key/query cosine statistics across three models, layers, context lengths and benchmarks per the reviews; no end-to-end compression experiments.
orXzecE63B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the bounded-similarity setting is a meaningful refinement of worst-case analyses, the bounds match, and the result gives a clean reason why uniform sampling works well in practice.
orXzecE63B.main_concern: The empirical intervals do not verify the every-pair assumption (attention sink excluded, quantile-based ranges), the bounds stay exponential and may be vacuous at practical sizes, and there are no end-to-end experiments.

FIakJL1eiv.one_liner: Cryptographic characterization of resource gaps under which targeted attacks must transfer or admit a defense, separating classification from generative tasks.
FIakJL1eiv.problem: It is unclear when giving the attacker more resources than the defender guarantees either a transferable attack (TA) that fools every bounded defender or an adversarial defense (AD).
FIakJL1eiv.method: Proves that with a quadratic resource gap every learnable, cheap-to-evaluate classification task admits a TA or an AD, constructs a generative task admitting neither under cryptographic assumptions (LWE, circular security), and shows a defense that spends extra resources after seeing the input can beat any fixed published model.
FIakJL1eiv.key_idea: Under LWE-based constructions, a defense that computes after seeing the input can be strictly stronger than any fixed published model with equal resources, breaking the TA/AD dichotomy for generative tasks.
FIakJL1eiv.evidence: Theoretical proofs under hardness of learning with errors and circular security; no experiments are mentioned.
FIakJL1eiv.claimed_gains: With a quadratic resource gap every learnable classification task with cheap models admits a TA or an AD; for a constructed generative task the dichotomy fails below a quadratic gap.
FIakJL1eiv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the separation between adaptive and static defenses for generative tasks is an interesting, nontrivial extension of the framework of Gluch et al. (2025).
FIakJL1eiv.main_concern: The framing overstates practical relevance (jailbreaks, inference-time compute), the gain over Gluch et al. may be mostly in parameters, and resource accounting in Lemma 28 appears inconsistent (O(S) versus O(S + S_E)).

D80UKm3vAN.one_liner: Video relighting by diffusion-refining a PBR rendering of the input under target illumination, rather than translating the input directly.
D80UKm3vAN.problem: Inverse-plus-forward rendering gives noisy reconstructions and misses global illumination, while generative video-to-video relighting limits control and temporal stability and lacks paired training data.
D80UKm3vAN.method: LightCrafter renders a PBR proxy of the input video under the target illumination and trains a video diffusion model to translate that proxy into the final relit video, so illumination is baked into the proxy. Reviews note it uses DiffusionRenderer G-buffers, overlapping-window inference, and paired synthetic plus unpaired real training data.
D80UKm3vAN.key_idea: Bake target illumination into a PBR proxy video and train a video diffusion model to refine the proxy into the final relit video.
D80UKm3vAN.evidence: A paired synthetic test set, MIT multi-illumination and DL3DV real data, human preference studies and data ablations, against DiffusionRenderer, UniRelight and Light-X per the reviews.
D80UKm3vAN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating physical control (PBR proxy) from generative refinement is well motivated, enables light insertion, material editing and compositing, and is supported by several complementary experiments.
D80UKm3vAN.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited since PBR-render refinement exists, quantitative gains are mostly in-distribution, and the pipeline depends on the quality of DiffusionRenderer G-buffers.

NhMTrXUiF3.one_liner: Per-client stopping rule halts local SGD when the average update's direction or magnitude departs from an early-round reference.
NhMTrXUiF3.problem: The number of local steps in federated learning shapes communication cost and the optimization trajectory, but the best fixed count depends on data heterogeneity and is hard to choose in advance.
NhMTrXUiF3.method: Each client picks its local step count by comparing the direction and magnitude of its average update with a reference formed early in the round, using only signals from local SGD with no extra model evaluations or communication. The analysis relates the rule to local curvature and local alignment to global descent.
NhMTrXUiF3.key_idea: Stop a client's local steps once its running average update no longer stays close to the early-round reference update in both direction and magnitude.
NhMTrXUiF3.evidence: Experiments under a fixed budget of total local updates on three benchmarks (MNIST and CIFAR-100 among them per the reviews), plus an analysis in an isotropic quadratic limit.
NhMTrXUiF3.claimed_gains: Reduces communication rounds with accuracy close to the best fixed count; reviews cite 22.77-36.13% fewer rounds than FIXED-10 at kappa=0.7.
NhMTrXUiF3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the rule is simple and cheap because it reuses quantities already computed during local SGD, and it cuts communication rounds at similar accuracy.
NhMTrXUiF3.main_concern: Empirical evidence is thin (three seeds, one kappa value, heterogeneity study on MNIST only, a single CIFAR-100 partition), and adaptive stopping can bias the combined update and introduce drift.

n5HdB3efUe.one_liner: Shows next-step-prediction Transformers expose structural causal parents through log-density gradients only under four identifying conditions.
n5HdB3efUe.problem: It is unclear when prediction by autoregressive Transformers recovers causal structure in lagged structural causal model time series, and where attention-based or predictive readouts mislead.
n5HdB3efUe.method: Distinguishes predictive parents from structural parents, proves they coincide under four identifying conditions so structural parents can be read from the gradient of the log-density learned by next-step prediction, and shows that with hidden causes, instantaneous effects or pooled regimes other past variables become predictive parents, producing causal illusions.
n5HdB3efUe.key_idea: Read structural parents from the gradient of the log-density learned by next-step prediction; the readout is valid only when predictive and structural parents coincide.
n5HdB3efUe.evidence: Decoder-only Transformers on synthetic lagged SCMs varying mechanisms, noise, dimensions and lag horizons, plus CausalTime benchmarks and a Transformer-versus-MLP comparison per the reviews.
n5HdB3efUe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives a principled characterization of when predictive dependencies are structural, validated edge by edge on synthetic systems across mechanisms, noise types, dimensions and lags.
n5HdB3efUe.main_concern: Validation in realistic settings is limited, baselines cannot detect shape-only causes by design, and MLPs achieve comparable readouts, so the Transformer-specific framing in the title may mislead.

CY8ruaJqfH.one_liner: Conditions GRPO policy ratios on opposite-outcome responses from the same group and corrects the advantage baseline by reward-confidence covariance.
CY8ruaJqfH.problem: GRPO treats each sampled output as independent during optimization, leaving unused the contrast between correct and incorrect solutions within the same group.
CY8ruaJqfH.method: BICC lets the model cross-reference successful and failed reasoning traces during optimization, and RCC dynamically adjusts the advantage baseline using reward-confidence covariance derived from a first-order approximation of the variance-minimizing estimator. Both operate on the sampled group alone and apply to GRPO and its variants.
CY8ruaJqfH.key_idea: Condition each sample's policy ratio on responses of the opposite outcome from its group so correct and failed traces inform each other, with a covariance-corrected advantage baseline.
CY8ruaJqfH.evidence: Qwen3-4B and Phi-4-mini on Math500, AMC 2023 and AIME 2024/2025 across GRPO and five variants (Dr.GRPO, ASPO, GMPO, DAPO, GSPO per the reviews), with same-class conditioning and larger-rollout controls.
CY8ruaJqfH.claimed_gains: BICC improves GRPO and five of its variants in 54 of 56 comparisons, by 0.3 to 1.9 points, with larger gains on the weaker models (remainder truncated).
CY8ruaJqfH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple, adds no inference cost, and is tested across several GRPO variants and model families with useful same-class and larger-rollout controls.
CY8ruaJqfH.main_concern: The theoretical justification is flawed (the claimed equivalence to token-level GRPO and the uniform gradient bound under clipping do not hold), and training on context-conditioned ratios differs from test-time inference.

FxOoRCe2cx.one_liner: Explains few-shot adaptation of latent dynamics models to visual shifts via a globally shared, low-dimensional functional correction under foundation representations.
FxOoRCe2cx.problem: Latent dynamics models on pretrained foundation representations adapt to dynamics-preserving visual shifts from only a few target-domain episodes, but why they are so sample-efficient is unexplained.
FxOoRCe2cx.method: Decomposes the required functional correction into a globally shared component and a state-dependent remainder, and analyzes its statistical accessibility (low cross-episode latent variability), low-dimensional parameter updates, and transport structure linking representation geometry to pretrained dynamics.
FxOoRCe2cx.key_idea: Foundation representations make the required correction mostly global and low-dimensional, and the state-dependent remainder concentrates in a lower-dimensional subspace than under source-specific representations.
FxOoRCe2cx.evidence: Analyses on two 2D planar environments (PushT zoom-out and background-colour shifts per the reviews) comparing DINO representations with source-specific encoders, including spectral and restricted fine-tuning analyses.
FxOoRCe2cx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it offers a coherent, mathematically clean diagnostic framework that separates global from state-dependent recovery and shows differences between DINO and source-specific encoders.
FxOoRCe2cx.main_concern: The explanatory quantities are oracle post-hoc measures not tied to the actual few-shot learner, cross-representation comparisons are incomplete, and experiments cover only two 2D environments with synthetic shifts.

HvUasiZs5s.one_liner: Sparse volumetric VAE with a conditional diffusion transformer generates 3D structural topologies from sparse load-and-fixity encodings.
HvUasiZs5s.problem: High-resolution 3D topology optimization needs repeated finite element analyses, and data-driven approaches lack large 3D datasets and are limited in problem scale and boundary-condition diversity.
HvUasiZs5s.method: OAT3D introduces a sparse problem encoding for load and fixity conditions and combines a sparse volumetric variational autoencoder with a conditional diffusion transformer, trained on a new dataset of 501,865 optimized topologies generated with 51,800 GPU-hours.
HvUasiZs5s.key_idea: Encode loads and supports as sparse conditioning and generate density fields with a latent diffusion transformer over a sparse volumetric VAE, replacing repeated finite element solves.
HvUasiZs5s.evidence: A new dataset with structures up to one million elements; evaluation on that dataset (in-distribution), a partially overlapping NITO-3D subset, best-of-N and post-optimization statistics, and IoU ablations per the reviews.
HvUasiZs5s.claimed_gains: The visible abstract states dataset scale (501,865 topologies from 51,800 GPU-hours, up to one million elements); reviews cite a 45.9x speedup over conventional topology optimization for a single raw candidate.
HvUasiZs5s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dataset is large and diverse, about four times NITO-3D, and that the sparse generative design with mechanics-informed conditioning is interesting and fast.
HvUasiZs5s.main_concern: The speedup counts only one raw candidate while reliable designs need best-of-N and post-optimization, evaluation is in-distribution on the authors' own dataset, and the shape- and resolution-free claim is overstated.

UlEjebCQsy.one_liner: Rewritable regional watermark fields combined with an authenticated live reference to classify images as current, superseded or unissued across reissues.
UlEjebCQsy.problem: Valid watermarks can persist on superseded releases or unapproved edits, and even a current release can contain regions last authorized at different revisions.
UlEjebCQsy.method: Generational Stratigraphy Fields (GSF) combine watermark evidence with an authenticated live reference to the current release. Each reissue embeds new generation labels in approved regions and inherited labels elsewhere, preserving history without requiring old watermarks to survive edits, with abstention when evidence is insufficient.
UlEjebCQsy.key_idea: Each reissue freshly embeds generation labels per region, with approved regions getting the new label and others inheriting, while an authenticated live head resolves current versus superseded status.
UlEjebCQsy.evidence: A complete-output reissuance evaluation following 480 histories through four releases with each AI editor's entire output, plus reader ablations and delivery transformations.
UlEjebCQsy.claimed_gains: 99.67% accuracy classifying issued images as current or superseded and 94.09% recall of unissued edits; after three reissues it recovers regional labels with 93.13% median accuracy and localizes the latest approved revision with 92.86% IoU.
UlEjebCQsy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is real, the formalization (four-way status with abstention) is clean, and the evaluation covers complete editor outputs and lifecycle events with informative failure reporting.
UlEjebCQsy.main_concern: It is unclear the watermark does the work, since a registry keyed by a lineage ID or perceptual hash is never run as a baseline, and headline recall is measured on full-regeneration editors.

ylZr4sGnoq.one_liner: Router-side controller that redirects only confidence-ambiguous expert choices away from overloaded experts, with an overhead-aware gate, for replica-free MoE serving.
ylZr4sGnoq.problem: Expert-parallel MoE inference is bottlenecked by routing-induced load imbalance, and replication-based placement consumes GPU memory and does not correct transient router imbalance.
ylZr4sGnoq.method: BLAZE redirects only confidence-ambiguous expert choices away from overloaded experts or EP ranks, locks high-confidence decisions, and computes mixture weights from the original router scores. An overhead-aware activation gate bypasses the controller on small effective MoE batches.
ylZr4sGnoq.key_idea: Penalize overloaded experts only where the router margin is ambiguous, keep confident choices and original mixture weights, and skip the controller when batches are too small to benefit.
ylZr4sGnoq.evidence: GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, GPT-OSS-120B (MLPerf accuracy runs) and DeepSeek-R1, including MLPerf-style serving scenarios.
ylZr4sGnoq.claimed_gains: Within 1.6 percentage points of vanilla accuracy on GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-30B-A3B versus a 44-49 point collapse for random or worst-ranked replacement; three MLPerf runs on GPT-OSS-120B pass the official threshold; the gate avoids a 16% TPOT regression on DeepSeek-R1.
ylZr4sGnoq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it tackles an important practical bottleneck with a memory-light, replica-free, CUDA-Graph-compatible implementation and a thorough system evaluation.
ylZr4sGnoq.main_concern: The benefit over close inference-time routing methods such as LASER is not established and novelty is limited, and the margin threshold varies widely across models while the serving evaluation uses a fixed threshold that costs accuracy.

zSCeVSxGO1.one_liner: Two-time-scale scalarization method moving weights by objective-space repulsion via entropic mirror descent, plus outer evolutionary search, for Pareto coverage.
zSCeVSxGO1.problem: Scalarization shifts multi-objective optimization onto weight selection, and the weight distribution that spreads solutions evenly over the Pareto front is governed by a non-injective, often discontinuous solution map.
zSCeVSxGO1.method: TWARD descends an entropic reference-point (smoothed Tchebycheff) scalarization on a fast scale, with a parameter tau controlling coverage, while entropic mirror descent on a slow scale moves the weights on the simplex under objective-space repulsion, converted into a closed-form weight update. An outer evolutionary genome search adds coverage.
zSCeVSxGO1.key_idea: Parametrize the smoothed Tchebycheff reference point by log-weights so objective-space repulsion becomes a closed-form weight update, run on a slow scale beside fast decision-variable descent.
zSCeVSxGO1.evidence: Theory for fixed-weight gradient descent (Theorem 1) and experiments on Pareto front coverage including disconnected and degenerate fronts per the reviews; the abstract is truncated before results.
zSCeVSxGO1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is relevant and the objective-space repulsion mechanism, with its closed-form translation into weight updates, is an interesting and intuitive route to better front diversity.
zSCeVSxGO1.main_concern: The theory does not cover the algorithm actually run (no convergence guarantee for the coupled two-time-scale dynamics or the curved-front approximation error), and the motivation for two time scales is unclear.

x4MHP0lQ9v.one_liner: Recursively decomposes a hard geometric constraint into local conditions to give exact invertible coordinates for fixed-endpoint protein backbones.
x4MHP0lQ9v.problem: Constrained protein generators enforce hard geometric constraints by modifying the generative process or repairing outputs, yet designs such as antibody loops must connect exactly to fixed structural boundaries.
x4MHP0lQ9v.method: RCC, a generator-independent framework, recursively decomposes a global hard constraint into local compatibility conditions and assembles exact local parameterizations into explicit coordinates for valid structures. For fixed-endpoint backbones it gives exact, invertible coordinates on regular regions, enabling probability modeling, generation and guidance while keeping constraints satisfied.
x4MHP0lQ9v.key_idea: Reparametrize the feasible set with explicit coordinates built from recursively decomposed local constraints, so guidance and sampling always operate on valid backbones.
x4MHP0lQ9v.evidence: Pretrained protein generators on antibody-loop design, fragment inpainting and motif-linker design plus prospective CDR-H3 design, with Riemannian-gradient and post-hoc repair baselines per the reviews.
x4MHP0lQ9v.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims RCC preserves existing generators' behavior while enforcing exact geometry and enabling effective guidance over valid structures.
x4MHP0lQ9v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the generator-independent, mathematically grounded formulation, which makes endpoint and link-length constraints feasible by construction, is conceptually appealing.
x4MHP0lQ9v.main_concern: The empirical benefit is unclear: Riemannian gradient plus Newton performs comparably or better, baselines are limited, and none of 64 tested sequences recovered the designed loop within 2 angstroms after sequence re-design.

qEHg8aiG2l.one_liner: Learns stochastic gates over SAE features under an expected-L0 penalty to find a sparse feature set reproducing a model's prediction.
qEHg8aiG2l.problem: SAEs show what a layer represents but not which features a prediction depends on, and intervention-based methods assess features one at a time and overlook their interactions.
qEHg8aiG2l.method: SLI casts the inverse problem as sparse selection: stochastic gates over the entire feature dictionary are jointly optimized under an expected-L0 penalty to preserve the prediction, while the counterfactual representation induced by the selected features is obtained in closed form through the frozen decoder, keeping the procedure end-to-end differentiable.
qEHg8aiG2l.key_idea: Jointly select a sparse SAE feature set with stochastic gates, decode the gated code through the frozen decoder, and optimize so the model's prediction is preserved.
qEHg8aiG2l.evidence: A Transformer-based transcriptomic foundation model on two clinical prediction tasks, treatment response in inflammatory bowel disease and synovial endotype in rheumatoid arthritis, using a single SAE per the reviews.
qEHg8aiG2l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a real limitation by identifying jointly sufficient feature sets rather than individual rankings, with a coherent formulation and biologically plausible features.
qEHg8aiG2l.main_concern: Evidence is not robust: explanations come from a single SAE and single optimization run, sufficiency of a small feature set does not show the model depends on it, and no benchmarks or SAE quality diagnostics are reported.

VG6BlmCGWO.one_liner: Stores Shampoo-type preconditioner factors in their current orthogonal basis to speed QR updates and allow cheap subspace updates preserving orthogonality.
VG6BlmCGWO.problem: QR-based updates in Shampoo-based methods such as KL-Shampoo and SOAP become costly for large preconditioning matrices.
VG6BlmCGWO.method: A preconditioner reparametrization maintains factors in the current orthogonal basis, which exposes input structure that speeds full-basis QR and lets dynamically selected basis vectors be updated cheaply via subspace QR while preserving full-basis orthogonality. A mixed-precision, batched QR implementation adds speed, and the framework covers KL-Shampoo, SOAP and KL-SOAP.
VG6BlmCGWO.key_idea: Keep preconditioning factors in the current orthogonal basis so QR inputs are structured and subspace updates retain full-basis orthogonality without re-orthogonalization.
VG6BlmCGWO.evidence: Training runs of SOAP-type and KL-Shampoo methods in mixed precision, per-step timing on an 8000x8000 matrix, and runtime studies over refresh interval and subspace size, compared with Muon per the reviews.
VG6BlmCGWO.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims reduced computational overhead, improved training of SOAP-type methods in mixed precision, and KL-SOAP matching or exceeding KL-Shampoo.
VG6BlmCGWO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reformulation is clear and simple, drops into existing Shampoo-type code, is equivalent in exact arithmetic for the full-basis update, and gives consistent gains.
VG6BlmCGWO.main_concern: Runtime evidence is thin: timing centers on one 8000x8000 matrix, end-to-end plots do not compare against the original KL-Shampoo or SOAP, and the claimed gain with plain PyTorch QR is never timed.

TtFY35CKTP.one_liner: Analysis showing language-vision cosine-similarity token pruning in VLAs suppresses redundancy along a visual-typicality axis rather than selecting semantically relevant tokens.
TtFY35CKTP.problem: It is unclear what language-guided token pruning in vision-language-action models actually selects, since methods rank tokens by attention, spatial redundancy or language relevance.
TtFY35CKTP.method: Starts from a simple language-vision cosine-similarity pruning criterion on pre-decoder representations, evaluates it on OpenVLA-OFT, and characterizes each backbone's embedding geometry to determine what the score ranks and when it suffices to decide which tokens to drop.
TtFY35CKTP.key_idea: The cosine-similarity score's projection geometry acts as a redundancy suppressor along the visual-typicality axis, so what it selects is set by each backbone's embedding geometry.
TtFY35CKTP.evidence: Four VLA models on three robotic datasets, with instruction-substitution and geometry analyses and comparisons with methods such as VLA-Pruner and VLA-Cache per the reviews.
TtFY35CKTP.claimed_gains: On OpenVLA-OFT the criterion reduces latency by up to 1.68x with only a 1% drop in success rate, and performs competitively with more complex pruning methods.
TtFY35CKTP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives an insightful, coherent mechanistic explanation of what the pruning signal measures, with broad evaluation and meaningful efficiency gains.
TtFY35CKTP.main_concern: The claim that the simple criterion surpasses state-of-the-art pruning is not supported (VLA-Pruner has a higher average success rate), the scope is narrow (single keep ratio, no real-robot experiments), and results are backbone-dependent.

gGIRUXrPww.one_liner: Expresses the probabilistic-robustness gradient as a distribution-weighted decision-boundary integral via the co-area formula, estimated by Gaussian-kernel Monte Carlo.
gGIRUXrPww.problem: Existing probabilistic-robustness (PR) training relies on surrogate risk objectives or adversarial-search adaptations, leaving the first-order behavior of PR itself unexplored.
gGIRUXrPww.method: Under mild regularity conditions, the PR gradient is written via the co-area formula as a distribution-weighted integral over the decision boundary. A Gaussian kernel serves as a computational probe, giving a Monte Carlo estimator of the PR first variation that is also explored for PR-oriented training (NPR-Aug. in the reviews).
gGIRUXrPww.key_idea: Write the PR gradient as a probability-weighted decision-boundary integral (co-area formula), so the update aggregates many boundary points instead of a single nearest one.
gGIRUXrPww.evidence: Low- and high-dimensional experiments; reviews cite low-dimensional checks of predicted NPR change against numerical boundary motion and high-dimensional runs on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18.
gGIRUXrPww.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the geometric interpretation of boundary location, probability weighting and parameter sensitivity clear, and the low-dimensional experiments consistent with the theory.
gGIRUXrPww.main_concern: One review calls the theory a direct application of long-established shape-derivative results with weak positioning against prior work, and another notes high-dimensional experiments only on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18 and missing ablations.

QRzEN2w1oQ.one_liner: Per-prompt adaptive rollout budgets, set from initial-model successful lengths, curb response-length growth in RL for competitive coding.
QRzEN2w1oQ.problem: RL for code inflates response length mostly on problems the model already solves, while length penalties are hard to tune and fixed budgets shorten outputs at the expense of hard problems.
QRzEN2w1oQ.method: Each prompt is capped at a multiple of the initial model's median successful length, rarely solved prompts keep the full budget, and responses truncated at the cap are masked from the loss instead of penalized.
QRzEN2w1oQ.key_idea: Set a per-prompt token budget from the initial model's median successful length (full budget for rarely solved prompts) and mask truncated responses from the loss rather than penalizing them.
QRzEN2w1oQ.evidence: Competitive-programming RL with training contexts up to 256k tokens, evaluated on LiveCodeBench and LiveCodeBench-Pro against a fixed-budget baseline and tuned length penalties.
QRzEN2w1oQ.claimed_gains: Versus a fixed-budget baseline, mean response length drops by over 30% on LiveCodeBench with no loss in accuracy, and by 25% on LiveCodeBench-Pro at a 1.5-point accuracy cost.
QRzEN2w1oQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis linking initial solvability to length growth is useful and the adaptive-budget method is simple and practical.
QRzEN2w1oQ.main_concern: Accuracy differences are within noise (one training run per configuration, error bars over decoding seeds only), and the method is heuristic with limited novelty and missing comparisons to related length-control methods.

g6QwrH2Bn9.one_liner: FlowSRL stabilizes diffusion and flow RL with deviation clipping and a learned flow-matching baseline, plus mechanisms against diversity collapse.
g6QwrH2Bn9.problem: Online RL post-training of diffusion and flow models needs training tricks to stay stable and collapses the diversity of generated samples.
g6QwrH2Bn9.method: Deviation clipping places a trust region on the velocity update, and the update is anchored to a learned flow-matching baseline instead of the policy itself. Diversity is addressed by restricting the policy to refine trajectories the pretrained model begins or by an entropy reward bonus, and search during rollouts handles hard-reward problems.
g6QwrH2Bn9.key_idea: Clip the deviation of the velocity-regression target as a trust region and anchor it to a learned flow-matching baseline rather than to the policy itself.
g6QwrH2Bn9.evidence: Standard text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, OCR, PickScore per the reviews) on SD3.5-Medium, 2D toy experiments, small-update-batch runs, and hard-reward problems with rollout search.
g6QwrH2Bn9.claimed_gains: Matches or outperforms prior diffusion RL methods at significantly smaller batch sizes and roughly 2x faster convergence.
g6QwrH2Bn9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the stability and compute-efficiency gains are supported by several experiments, with the 2D toy experiments clarifying the failure modes.
g6QwrH2Bn9.main_concern: Empirical scope is narrow (a single SD3.5-Medium backbone, text-to-image only), the stability proof assumes idealized continuous updates, and the search configuration is left as TBD in Table F.1.

b9cESikp4B.one_liner: A 4B agent trained on synthesized cross-source bridge trajectories joining SQL and web evidence, via SFT then RL.
b9cESikp4B.problem: Agents struggle when evidence must cross structured (database) and unstructured (web) sources, and no method explicitly teaches cross-source reasoning.
b9cESikp4B.method: Starting from validated single-source tasks (text-to-SQL or web search), the pipeline fabricates the missing source around a bridge entity from the seed's own output and keeps a sample only when construction gates confirm neither side alone suffices. The agent is trained on this data with supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.
b9cESikp4B.key_idea: Extend single-source seed tasks across the structured-unstructured boundary by fabricating the missing source around a bridge entity, filtered by gates that require both sources.
b9cESikp4B.evidence: Evaluated on the HybridDeepResearch benchmark against the Qwen3.5-4B base model; reviews also cite BrowseComp, BrowseComp-Plus, SQL2S and Spider 2.0-lite results and SQL-only, search-only and union fine-tuning baselines.
b9cESikp4B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-source evidence over databases and the web is a relevant target and that the bridge-construction pipeline with anti-shortcut gates is a concrete, reproducible way to get hard hybrid data, with sizable gains for a 4B model.
b9cESikp4B.main_concern: All hybrid results come from a single 120-question benchmark run in the authors' own local corpus and harness, with no variance reporting and insufficiently controlled attribution of gains to the proposed data.

oI1qYqcrkY.one_liner: Evaluates LLMs as builders of executable game-playing automata, scored by Elo from offline head-to-head tournaments across 20 games.
oI1qYqcrkY.problem: Benchmarks mostly measure interactive, live-play capability and not the utility of the durable autonomous artifacts an AI can build.
oI1qYqcrkY.method: Each LLM writes Python automata (executable policies) for strategic board games. Code generation is separated from execution, so the programs are run offline in head-to-head matches to compute Elo ratings.
oI1qYqcrkY.key_idea: Separate artifact generation from execution: score LLMs by the Elo of the Python policies they write, played offline in tournaments with no LLM calls at match time.
oI1qYqcrkY.evidence: 20 games, 5,200 Python automata from 52 LLMs and over 2,500,000 offline matches; reviews add comparisons with human-written engines and live LLM play, ranking-stability checks and reasoning-level experiments.
oI1qYqcrkY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating LLMs as builders of reusable artifacts is well motivated and that the evaluation is extensive, spanning many games and models with cost-efficient offline matches.
oI1qYqcrkY.main_concern: Scores may conflate strategic reasoning with code or formatting errors, and the intra-model qualifier and the added value of the full cross-model tournament are not sufficiently justified.

CPLXxx7aN5.one_liner: Benchmark of 717,948 simulated time series for reconstructing tower bending moments from accelerometer and SCADA signals, scored by fatigue damage.
CPLXxx7aN5.problem: Strain gauges on floating offshore wind turbine towers are rare, and no public benchmark scored bending-moment reconstruction by the fatigue damage it implies.
CPLXxx7aN5.method: FLOATSense provides 717,948 time series from 19,404 OpenFAST simulations of three 22 MW floating tower designs, with the six realizations of each operating condition kept in one split. Evaluation separates aggregate damage accuracy from realization tracking across twenty learned models and a physics-based baseline.
CPLXxx7aN5.key_idea: Score reconstructed bending-moment histories by the fatigue damage they imply, separating aggregate damage accuracy from within-condition realization tracking.
CPLXxx7aN5.evidence: Twenty learned models and a physics-based baseline evaluated across operating regimes, tower designs and sensor configurations on OpenFAST simulations.
CPLXxx7aN5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dataset addresses a concrete problem and that scoring by fatigue damage, with aggregate accuracy separated from realization tracking, is a useful evaluation design.
CPLXxx7aN5.main_concern: Only 47 simulations per tower are available during review so headline results cannot be reproduced, and all targets come from one simulated turbine family with a fixed 50-epoch training budget.

4TlsbbYFm6.one_liner: Meta-learns a coupling between surrogate gradients and generative transport so integrated surrogate changes along paths match oracle value differences.
4TlsbbYFm6.problem: Surrogate methods extrapolate poorly beyond observed data, generative methods may follow paths inconsistent with local improvement directions, and sparse labels give little differential information to learn their coupling.
4TlsbbYFm6.method: DIAL is a meta optimization framework that learns the surrogate-generative coupling across a population of similar functions consistent with the observed target data, using violations of the differential-to-integral relation as an alignment signal. Reviews list Gaussian processes, MAML, flow matching and Doob's h-transform as components.
4TlsbbYFm6.key_idea: Integrating surrogate differential changes along a mass-transport path must recover the oracle value difference between endpoints; violations of this relation align surrogate gradients and generative transport.
4TlsbbYFm6.evidence: Reviews report experiments on eight optimization tasks (including discrete TFBind8 and TFBind10), ablations of differential and integral alignment, and comparison with ROOT under the same GP construction.
4TlsbbYFm6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling local surrogate gradients with global generative transport is an interesting, clearly motivated idea, and that removing alignment lowers mean performance.
4TlsbbYFm6.main_concern: The theoretical justification of integral alignment is unclear because a conservative gradient field's path integral depends only on fixed endpoints, and evidence for the claimed mutual error-correction mechanism is insufficient.
