OWlbp6QYsD.one_liner: Automated red-teaming framework that jointly generates tasks, executable environments and attacks targeting persistent state of claw-style agents.
OWlbp6QYsD.problem: Persistent-state attacks on claw-style agents (config files, memory, skills) are hard to evaluate because existing benchmarks are manual, small and quickly outdated, and automated red-teaming only optimizes payloads in predefined scenarios.
OWlbp6QYsD.method: AutoRedClaw explores tasks, environments and attacks jointly and generates end-to-end attacks with the environments needed to run them, using a strict quality-checking protocol, execution-based validation and task-driven environment construction to keep costs low. It releases RedClaw-Bench, a 300-case benchmark with adapters for different agent frameworks.
OWlbp6QYsD.key_idea: Jointly generate attack tasks, executable environments and persistent-state payloads, keeping a case only if execution-based validation shows the attack works.
OWlbp6QYsD.evidence: RedClaw-Bench (300 cases) evaluated by attack success rate across agent frameworks via adapters, with a probe agent used for validation; the abstract is truncated before results.
OWlbp6QYsD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that persistent-state security for claw-style agents is an important problem and that the automated end-to-end pipeline and RedClaw-Bench are practically useful beyond manually built benchmarks.
OWlbp6QYsD.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing ablations of framework components and missing controlled comparisons with other benchmarks or frameworks, plus possible selection bias from keeping only cases the probe agent executes.

mOi88wJx9h.one_liner: Analyzes seven Forward-Forward variants with a Boundary Proximity Index, comparing against random-weight networks to see which misclassified points training rescues.
mOi88wJx9h.problem: Forward-Forward variants are judged by linear-probe accuracy, which over-credits learning because random untrained convolutional weights already score well above chance and one accuracy number hides which points training fixes.
mOi88wJx9h.method: Defines the Boundary Proximity Index (BPI), a multiclass margin normalized by a class-centroid reference, and measures per-sample rescue and breakage rates relative to a random-weight baseline for seven Forward-Forward and related layer-local methods.
mOi88wJx9h.key_idea: Normalize each point's multiclass probe margin by a class-centroid reference (BPI) and track which initially misclassified points training rescues, relative to random-weight features.
mOi88wJx9h.evidence: Seven Forward-Forward variants and related layer-local methods compared with random-weight networks and backpropagation using linear probes, layer-wise ablations and null controls.
mOi88wJx9h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is comprehensive, with random-network and backpropagation controls and sample-level rescue and breakage analysis that goes beyond aggregate accuracy.
mOi88wJx9h.main_concern: Limited novelty and unclear added value of BPI over plain linear probing, with the robustness of the probe and normalization protocol only partially validated.

ohoBftcCww.one_liner: Self-supervised 3D geometry from unposed images: hide held-out views only from the 3D representation and align sparse- with dense-context features.
ohoBftcCww.problem: Self-supervised 3D geometry methods avoid trivial solutions by separating camera and scene branches or restricting context and held-out view interaction, which sacrifices cross-view correspondence.
ohoBftcCww.method: Held-out views are excluded only from the 3D representation while a shared backbone uses all views for correspondence. Sparse-context features are aligned with dense-context features as an extra geometric training signal, and features are also aligned with a frozen vision foundation model, all without geometric annotation.
ohoBftcCww.key_idea: Place the visibility asymmetry in the 3D representation rather than in feature extraction, and align sparse-context features to dense-context features as a training signal.
ohoBftcCww.evidence: Controlled experiments varying only where the asymmetry is placed, ablations of each component, and comparisons with prior self-supervised methods on depth and pose estimation.
ohoBftcCww.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and the controlled studies of where to place the asymmetry are well designed, with the minimal-change design improving depth and pose over prior designs.
ohoBftcCww.main_concern: Comparison fairness and generality are questioned: the model is initialized from a Pixio encoder that also supplies semantic guidance, and results use a single backbone with little analysis of the guidance loss.

mdfPmiv7f7.one_liner: Dynamically steers model activations against reward hacking using vectors from labeled rollouts, gradient optimization, or an anti-hacking model spec.
mdfPmiv7f7.problem: Reward hacking causes costly failures in production systems, and monitoring and mitigating it in realistic settings with tool calls and long contexts is hard.
mdfPmiv7f7.method: A dynamic intervention applies steering directions obtained three ways (difference-in-means from labeled rollouts, gradient-optimized vectors, and vectors extracted when the model references an anti-reward-hacking spec), perturbing representations less than uniform residual-stream addition. Reviews describe capping, adding and flooring variants.
mdfPmiv7f7.key_idea: Apply steering directions dynamically (activation capping) instead of adding one uniform vector to the residual stream, so representations are perturbed less.
mdfPmiv7f7.evidence: Reviews describe one model tested on 30 ImpossibleBench LiveCodeBench tasks with long multi-turn tool-call rollouts, uncorrupted-task checks and a prompting baseline; the abstract also reports transfer of coding-derived vectors to other domains.
mdfPmiv7f7.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that reward hacking is significantly reduced without correspondingly significant costs to coherence or capability.
mdfPmiv7f7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting is realistic (long, multi-turn agentic rollouts with tool calls) and that steering substantially reduces hacking without significantly hurting performance.
mdfPmiv7f7.main_concern: Evidence rests on one model and 30 ImpossibleBench LiveCodeBench tasks, and the reduction may reflect the model giving up earlier rather than behaving more honestly.

yUBw8ooX1o.one_liner: Proves Theta(sqrt T) minimax online smooth calibration and calibration distance via a two-test lower-bound principle with a single oblivious adversary.
yUBw8ooX1o.problem: Tight online minimax rates for smooth calibration and calibration distance were open, with a gap between the known Omega(T^{1/3}) and O(sqrt T) bounds.
yUBw8ooX1o.method: A general two-test lower-bounding principle forces the forecaster to incur Omega(sqrt T) calibration error through a single carefully constructed pair of calibration tests. It is applied to delayed feedback and to online kernel calibration, giving matching lower bounds for a wide class of kernels including Gaussian and Laplace.
yUBw8ooX1o.key_idea: Force Omega(sqrt T) calibration error through a single carefully constructed pair of calibration tests, realized by one oblivious adversary.
yUBw8ooX1o.evidence: Theoretical proofs of minimax rates for smooth calibration, calibration distance, delayed feedback and kernel calibration; no experiments are described.
yUBw8ooX1o.claimed_gains: Settles the minimax rate for smooth calibration and calibration distance at Theta(sqrt T), closing the gap between Omega(T^{1/3}) and O(sqrt T).
yUBw8ooX1o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that closing the long-standing gap to a tight rate is a meaningful result and that the two-test principle, which needs only an oblivious adversary, is elegant and broadly applicable.
yUBw8ooX1o.main_concern: The introduction is dense and hard to follow, and the fast-rate kernel results in Section 4 rest on artificial geometric constructions that fit poorly with the main storyline.

R2XYACmMVK.one_liner: Model-free deterministic policy gradient for continuous-time RL using multi-step TD value estimates and per-perturbation advantage-rate derivative learning.
R2XYACmMVK.problem: In continuous-time RL for controlled diffusions with unknown dynamics, shorter observation intervals lower the signal-to-noise ratio, making the effect of action changes hard to estimate.
R2XYACmMVK.method: AdvG estimates values with multi-step temporal-difference error and learns the action derivative of the advantage rate from individual exploratory perturbations, pairing perturbations with local residuals within each cell (Cell-Pairing in the reviews). A critic-stability analysis yields joint actor and critic convergence guarantees.
R2XYACmMVK.key_idea: Decouple value estimation (multi-step TD over a time window) from advantage-rate action-derivative estimation (individual exploratory perturbations matched with local residuals).
R2XYACmMVK.evidence: Finite-sample convergence theory for nonlinear controlled diffusions; reviews cite experiments on LQ control and noisy pendulum tasks against SAC, TD3, DDPG and CT-DDPG.
R2XYACmMVK.claimed_gains: Establishes an O(T^{-2/5}) joint actor-critic convergence rate with exact critic features and an actor gradient estimator with mean-squared error O(T^{-2/3}) that is minimax optimal.
R2XYACmMVK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algorithm cleanly separates multi-step value estimation from per-perturbation action-derivative estimation and that the finite-sample joint actor-critic guarantee is a solid theoretical contribution.
R2XYACmMVK.main_concern: Experiments are limited to simple LQ control and noisy pendulum tasks with neural critics, leaving a gap to the fixed-critic theory, and claims about baseline degradation are overstated.

Eg1GBLzKmB.one_liner: Recurrence-aware quantization recipe for linear-recurrent LLMs: value-axis scale grouping, decay-based mixed precision and stochastic rounding for state.
Eg1GBLzKmB.problem: Quantization tooling was built around softmax Transformers, whose numerical properties and KV-cache state differ from the fixed-size recurrent state of linear-recurrent models.
Eg1GBLzKmB.method: QReS combines value-axis scale grouping, decay-based mixed-precision allocation and stochastic rounding for recurrent-state quantization. It is motivated by controlled 1.3B experiments showing decayed recurrences develop much weaker residual outlier channels than softmax attention.
Eg1GBLzKmB.key_idea: Quantize the recurrent state with value-axis scale groups, allocate precision by decay rate, and use stochastic rounding to handle repeated state updates.
Eg1GBLzKmB.evidence: Controlled 1.3B comparisons of sequence mixers, plus tests on Qwen-3.5 9B, Nemotron-H 8B and Kimi-Linear 48B-A3B; reviews note vLLM integration with end-to-end serving on H100.
Eg1GBLzKmB.claimed_gains: Robust 8-bit state quantization and faster decoding across Qwen-3.5 9B, Nemotron-H 8B and Kimi-Linear 48B-A3B; the abstract is truncated before further numbers.
Eg1GBLzKmB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled architectural comparisons give useful insight into how decay affects quantization robustness and that the end-to-end vLLM evaluation shows practical relevance.
Eg1GBLzKmB.main_concern: There is no direct comparison with existing recurrent-state quantization methods such as Q-Mamba or Nemotron under matched settings, so the incremental benefit and novelty of the components are not established.

QwErjR529K.one_liner: Learns multi-scale segment relevance for long-video frame selection by composing clip relevance, trained by self-distillation from video QA alone.
QwErjR529K.problem: VLMs see long videos through few frames, but existing relevance signals work at one fixed temporal scale, score frames in isolation, or need grounding annotations and expensive model passes.
QwErjR529K.method: SPAN uses a query-conditioned composition operator that propagates relevance from base clips to arbitrarily coarse segments, learned by self-distillation (composed clips must reconstruct the video's own representation) from video-QA tuples. A nested, tree-structured knapsack then allocates the frame budget across the segment hierarchy.
QwErjR529K.key_idea: Propagate relevance from base clips to coarser segments with one query-conditioned composition operator, trained so composed clips reconstruct the video's representation.
QwErjR529K.evidence: Four long-video benchmarks and two VLM families; reviews cite a comparison with a temporally supervised selector (VideoITG) and training on about 200,000 video-QA examples.
QwErjR529K.claimed_gains: SPAN improves on uniform sampling by an average of 5.47 points; the abstract is truncated before the comparison with the strongest baseline.
QwErjR529K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning segment relevance from video-QA data without grounding annotations is valuable and that the evaluation covers multiple benchmarks, model scales and frame budgets with good results.
QwErjR529K.main_concern: Learned relevance is validated only through downstream QA accuracy, not against temporal-grounding annotations, so it is unclear whether the selected frames match the true evidence.

P4b3uLxhnC.one_liner: Inference-time search for RNA inverse design that learns dependencies from folding mismatches and uses an online surrogate to rank edits.
P4b3uLxhnC.problem: Learned RNA generators can miss exact structural matches outside their training distribution, and search is costly because correcting one pairing error can create new errors beyond a fixed repair scope.
P4b3uLxhnC.method: From candidates generated for a target secondary structure, KnitNet uses mismatched folds to infer nucleotide dependencies and adapt a joint repair strategy, while an online surrogate learns which edits are promising. It adapts to each structural regime by changing only the optimization signal to match the verifier.
P4b3uLxhnC.key_idea: Use verifier feedback (mismatched folds) to infer nucleotide dependencies for joint repair, with an online surrogate that ranks which edits to try.
P4b3uLxhnC.evidence: Five secondary-structure benchmarks including OpenKnot57 (Eterna100 per the reviews), plus 3D self-consistency targets, compared with continued sampling and search baselines such as NEMO.
P4b3uLxhnC.claimed_gains: Exact solve rates rise by an average of 21 percentage points over continued sampling with 70% less time-to-solve across five benchmarks, and KnitNet is the first method to reach exact computational matches on all OpenKnot57 pseudoknotted structures.
P4b3uLxhnC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pseudoknot results are strong (57/57 computational matches on OpenKnot57 in individual runs) and that comparisons with continued sampling use matched initial pools and wall-clock budgets.
P4b3uLxhnC.main_concern: Novelty is seen as mostly integration of prior components, and evaluation depends on the same computational predictors used during optimization, with no independent or experimental validation.

4RrFlQ9I1J.one_liner: Reframes GPCR EC50 regression as concentration-conditional classification, then fits a Hill curve to the model's predicted activation probabilities.
4RrFlQ9I1J.problem: Predicting GPCR activity and potency (EC50) remains difficult for existing drug-target affinity and censored-regression approaches.
4RrFlQ9I1J.method: For each training protein-molecule pair, concentrations are sampled uniformly and labels are deterministic far from the EC50 and soft in the transition region, and a concentration-conditional model learns P(active|s,m,c). Querying across concentrations yields a Hill curve whose upper asymptote gives activity and whose inflection point in log c gives EC50.
4RrFlQ9I1J.key_idea: Train on concentration-conditional activation labels derived from EC50, then read activity and EC50 from a Hill curve fitted to the model's predictions across concentrations.
4RrFlQ9I1J.evidence: M2OR dataset, compared with drug-target affinity baselines, censored regression and activity classifiers, with ablation studies.
4RrFlQ9I1J.claimed_gains: On M2OR, EC50 estimation error of 0.683 log units, an improvement of 0.399 log units over drug-target affinity baselines and 0.205 over censored regression, with competitive activity classification (MCC 0.665 in the i.i.d. setting).
4RrFlQ9I1J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework ties learning to the experimental dose-response workflow, using measured EC50, inactive and lower-bound observations in one formulation, and that it outperforms the baselines.
4RrFlQ9I1J.main_concern: The supervision is essentially threshold classification built from EC50 by predefined rules, so gains may not reflect true dose-response recovery, and RMSLE is computed only on correctly predicted active pairs.

8UBXpZ0n2K.one_liner: Co-speech motion via a frozen multimodal LLM that plans two-second directives, executed by a Warp-VQVAE motion model with audio-conditioned re-timing.
8UBXpZ0n2K.problem: Speech-to-motion correspondence is highly ambiguous, which makes generation hard to control and inspect.
8UBXpZ0n2K.method: A frozen multimodal language model uses pretrained knowledge, speech context, recent memory and retrieved examples to predict two-second behavioral plans (directives), and a specialized executor realizes them as motion. Warp-VQVAE re-times the latent space by temporal warping to sync with speech, and BEAT2-Directive supplies 101,660 speech-directive-motion triplets to supervise the interface.
8UBXpZ0n2K.key_idea: Connect LLM behavioral planning and motion execution through explicit editable directives, with audio-conditioned temporal warping in the VQVAE latent space for rhythmic synchrony.
8UBXpZ0n2K.evidence: BEAT2 single- and all-speaker benchmarks with FGD, a human preference study on unseen TED speech, plus ablations, alternative language-model directors and a persona-editing demonstration.
8UBXpZ0n2K.claimed_gains: FGD of 3.631 on the single-speaker and 2.76 on the all-speaker benchmark, reducing FGD by 11% and 38% versus prior methods, plus the highest aggregate human preference on unseen TED speech among compared methods.
8UBXpZ0n2K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the explicit, editable directive interface is practical, supports persona editing without retraining the executor, and that the BEAT2-Directive dataset and ablation-rich evaluation are useful.
8UBXpZ0n2K.main_concern: The benefit of LLM planning is not firmly established (the executor without directives already reaches FGD 3.920 and no confidence intervals are given), and temporal warping may cause abrupt, overly rhythmic motion.

hQtz3IQNLM.one_liner: Q-Hankeling regularizes Q-learning with a jointly learned linear-recurrence penalty on short replay trajectory chunks, exploiting low-rank Hankel structure.
hQtz3IQNLM.problem: Sample-efficient RL needs exploitable structure in value estimates, and the low-rank temporal structure of value sequences along trajectories had not been identified or used.
hQtz3IQNLM.method: Q-Hankeling learns linear recurrence coefficients jointly with the critic and penalizes recurrence residuals within trajectory chunks sampled from replay, avoiding explicit Hankel matrices or SVD. It is integrated into DQN, Efficient Rainbow, TD3 and SAC.
hQtz3IQNLM.key_idea: Penalize recurrence residuals of Q-values within replay chunks using linear-recurrence coefficients learned jointly with the critic, a temporal-predictability prior from low-rank Hankel structure.
hQtz3IQNLM.evidence: Empirical Hankel-rank analysis of learned critics on Classical Control, MuJoCo and Atari, a mixing-based theoretical argument, and Q-Hankeling added to DQN, Efficient Rainbow, TD3 and SAC.
hQtz3IQNLM.claimed_gains: On Atari-100k, mean human-normalized score rises from 0.463 to 0.530 across 26 games, an improvement of approximately 14%.
hQtz3IQNLM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the temporal low-rank view of value sequences is an interesting perspective and that the recurrence regularizer is simple, integrates with several RL algorithms and gives gains across many settings.
hQtz3IQNLM.main_concern: The link between the low-rank Hankel hypothesis and the practical regularizer is incomplete, the method resembles prior temporal regularization, and it hurts some tasks (for example a 6% drop on Acrobot).

7SjXsz9A80.one_liner: Test-time adaptation for prototype networks that minimizes binary entropy of prototype similarities, balanced against output entropy by estimated prototype reliability.
7SjXsz9A80.problem: Prototype-based interpretable networks are limited by their training data and lose robustness under distribution shift, and prototypes had not been used for test-time adaptation.
7SjXsz9A80.method: ProtoTTA minimizes the binary entropy of prototype similarities, adaptively balancing it with output entropy using a label-free estimate of prototype reliability, and stabilizes updates with geometric filtering and weighting by prototype importance and model confidence. It also adds interpretability metrics and a VLM-based evaluation framework.
7SjXsz9A80.key_idea: Minimize binary entropy of prototype similarities alongside output entropy, with the mix set by a label-free prototype-reliability estimate and updates filtered geometrically.
7SjXsz9A80.evidence: Four prototypical backbones on four benchmarks in fine-grained vision, histopathology and NLP; reviews cite three seeds, paired tests, ablations, and comparison with output-entropy minimization and EATA.
7SjXsz9A80.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is the first test-time adaptation method for part-prototype networks, covers several prototype architectures, and checks that explanations are preserved, with ablations showing prototype-level signals help beyond output entropy.
7SjXsz9A80.main_concern: Reviewers see little beyond standard entropy-based test-time adaptation, with small margins over the best baseline, an unclear contribution of the prototype loss on some models, and small, dated benchmarks.

Kryd7MYvKJ.one_liner: Samples a symmetry template, then jointly diffuses lattice, coordinates and atom types in Cartesian space with a Wyckoff-constrained loss.
Kryd7MYvKJ.problem: Generative models often fail to reproduce crystal symmetry, and explicitly enforcing symmetry has yielded fewer stable and novel structures than unconstrained generation.
Kryd7MYvKJ.method: GEODE first samples symmetry templates, then jointly generates the lattice, atomic coordinates and atom types while preserving the specified symmetry through a Wyckoff-constrained loss. Cartesian diffusion gives coordinate noise a consistent physical scale, and sampling-time template filtering and template-based property guidance are added.
Kryd7MYvKJ.key_idea: Diffuse lattice and coordinates in Cartesian space conditioned on a sampled symmetry template, enforcing the symmetry with a Wyckoff-constrained loss.
Kryd7MYvKJ.evidence: Unconditional generation on MP20 (and Alex-MP-20 per the reviews) scored by mSUN, point-group distribution comparisons, a controlled comparison with fractional-coordinate diffusion, template filtering, and classifier-free guidance of permittivity.
Kryd7MYvKJ.claimed_gains: Unconditional mSUN rate of 11.9% versus 7.7% for the next best symmetry-aware model, and template filtering raises mSUN by about 6% without retraining.
Kryd7MYvKJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree GEODE reaches the best mSUN among symmetry-aware methods on MP20, matches the training set's point-group distribution, and that template filtering improves quality without retraining.
Kryd7MYvKJ.main_concern: On the larger Alex-MP-20 dataset its mSUN (29.20%) is far below a symmetry-agnostic baseline (62.4%), and sampling is slow (17 hours for 2500 structures).

ruxbHpoG5G.one_liner: Feeds pretrained representations into a diffusion transformer as training-time query tokens behind an asymmetric attention mask, dropped at inference.
ruxbHpoG5G.problem: Existing ways to use pretrained representations in diffusion transformers either align activations through an explicit loss (REPA) or make the representation a variable the model must generate (joint diffusion).
ruxbHpoG5G.method: Asym-DiT adds representation tokens that read the latent through an asymmetric mask but are never read by it; each solves its own denoising task and its loss reaches the latent only through backpropagation. The tokens are removed at inference at no added cost.
ruxbHpoG5G.key_idea: Add representation tokens as training-time queries that read the latent but are never read by it, so their denoising loss shapes latent states only via backpropagation.
ruxbHpoG5G.evidence: Text-to-music generation compared with vanilla DiT, REPA and joint-diffusion baselines, from scratch and as short fine-tuning; reviews cite ReDi and REG baselines and scaling up to 1.7B parameters.
ruxbHpoG5G.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports large improvements over vanilla DiT, REPA and joint-diffusion baselines without numbers.
ruxbHpoG5G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, adds no inference cost or parameters, and gives meaningful gains both from scratch and as a fine-tuning stage where REPA helps little.
ruxbHpoG5G.main_concern: All experiments use one internal, unreleased text-to-music corpus with baselines re-implemented for audio, so the evidence for generality is narrow and lacks a standard public benchmark.

5uXtcxjM1p.one_liner: Action-conditioned network world model of diffusion dynamics serves as fast evaluator in a coding-agent loop designing network intervention algorithms.
5uXtcxjM1p.problem: Designing algorithms for interventions on complex networks requires scoring many candidates over sampled trajectories, and the cost of simulation becomes a bottleneck.
5uXtcxjM1p.method: An action-conditioned Network World Model learns a network's diffusion dynamics under interventions, applies each action and predicts the outcome. A coding agent designs and refines executable algorithms using feedback from full rollouts, action-level credit and counterfactual probes over alternative interventions.
5uXtcxjM1p.key_idea: Replace Monte Carlo simulation with a learned action-conditioned network world model as the evaluator in an LLM coding-agent loop with rollout, credit and counterfactual feedback.
5uXtcxjM1p.evidence: Eight network tasks and five diffusion models scored on a shared referee, compared with the strongest reported baselines, and a rollout speed comparison against NDlib Monte Carlo.
5uXtcxjM1p.claimed_gains: Designed algorithms match or exceed the strongest reported baseline in 138 of 141 settings, with up to 14.5 times faster rollouts than Monte Carlo (abstract truncated).
5uXtcxjM1p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is reasonable, separating known intervention rules from learned diffusion dynamics, with broad evaluation across eight tasks and five diffusion models and readable, transferable programs.
5uXtcxjM1p.main_concern: The contribution of the learned world model is not isolated: no experiment swaps in the exact vectorized Oracle simulator or Monte Carlo as evaluator, and the speed-up is compared only against NDlib Monte Carlo.

6wHdHqhDuM.one_liner: Replaces the score with a high-frequency dithered cosine of the model value, giving gradient-free Langevin and reverse-diffusion sampling.
6wHdHqhDuM.problem: Sampling from energy-based and score-based generative models normally needs gradient or score evaluations, which are unavailable or ill-behaved for non-smooth energies.
6wHdHqhDuM.method: The drift term containing the score is replaced by sqrt(alpha*omega)*cos(omega t + k log p_theta(x)); in the high-frequency averaging limit this recovers Langevin MCMC and the reverse-time SDE of score-based diffusion. Convergence is proved by extending bounded extremum-seeking averaging to Ito processes, using one forward evaluation per time step.
6wHdHqhDuM.key_idea: Use a high-frequency dithered cosine of the model's log-density value as the drift, so extremum-seeking averaging recovers the gradient without derivatives.
6wHdHqhDuM.evidence: Proofs that dithered Ito SDE trajectories converge to the target SDE with an explicit O(omega^{-1/2}) mean-square rate under global bounds, extended to C^{1,1}, Sobolev and Lipschitz energies; reviews also mention experiments on energy-based and other generative models.
6wHdHqhDuM.claimed_gains: Provable convergence with an explicit O(omega^{-1/2}) mean-square rate under global bounds, using one forward evaluation per time step regardless of dimension.
6wHdHqhDuM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that bringing extremum seeking to zeroth-order sampling is a promising idea and that the theoretical guarantees and regularity extensions are clearly stated.
6wHdHqhDuM.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty beyond established extremum-seeking machinery, little intuition for the mechanism, and unclear experiments without comparison to other Langevin or zero-order samplers.

WmNoxelHod.one_liner: Proves LLM-style next-token predictors are equivalent to monotone compression algorithms, with monotonicity needed iff infinitely-often one-way functions exist.
WmNoxelHod.problem: The empirical link between LLM capability and compression ability lacks a theoretical account.
WmNoxelHod.method: They model LLMs as next-token predictors, show a monotone (order-preserving) compressor can be built from a predictor and vice versa with error preserved up to an additive gap of 2, and show monotonicity is required for this iff infinitely-often one-way functions exist.
WmNoxelHod.key_idea: Monotone (order-preserving) encodings, as in arithmetic coding, convert between next-token predictors and compressors while preserving error up to an additive gap of 2.
WmNoxelHod.evidence: Theoretical proofs only; reviews note the paper has no empirical results or discussion of practical use.
WmNoxelHod.claimed_gains: The equivalence between next-token predictors and monotone compressors preserves the error up to an additive gap of 2.
WmNoxelHod.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives important theoretical results connecting LLMs to monotone compression such as arithmetic coding, including a cryptographic characterization of when monotonicity is needed.
WmNoxelHod.main_concern: The paper does not discuss practical applications or empirical benefits of the monotonicity result.

qFLCslbbXM.one_liner: Agentic framework that audits individual benchmark tasks for hidden dependencies, specification gaps, and weak grading logic.
qFLCslbbXM.problem: Expert-authored benchmark tasks contain implicit assumptions, incomplete environment specifications, and brittle evaluation logic that human annotation cannot reliably catch.
qFLCslbbXM.method: Auto Benchmark Audit (ABA) runs an agent over individual tasks using a shared evidence schema and rubric, applied to 168 benchmarks across nine domains and validated by expert review and upstream PRs.
qFLCslbbXM.key_idea: An agent inspects each benchmark task against an evidence schema and rubric and flags issues with evidence pointers, severity rationales, and suggested repairs.
qFLCslbbXM.evidence: 168 benchmarks across nine domains (frontier LLM benchmarks and prior NeurIPS publications), expert review and independent third-party reports such as upstream PRs, and leaderboard re-ranking after filtering flagged tasks.
qFLCslbbXM.claimed_gains: ABA identifies issues on over 25.7% of tasks, and filtering them raises average performance on SWE-bench Verified by 9.9% and on Terminal-Bench 2 by 9.6%.
qFLCslbbXM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the audit is a substantial, actionable resource with broad coverage of validity issues, supported by validation against externally identified defects.
qFLCslbbXM.main_concern: Validation is limited (human review covers 54 major and 30 minor findings from 12 benchmarks), and it is unclear whether the audit rubrics were developed or tuned against the external validation set.

58VHZl4u5V.one_liner: RNA language model keeps a low-rank pair state across Transformer layers, updated by antidiagonal convolutions and read as attention bias.
58VHZl4u5V.problem: RNA language models use BERT-style Transformers that keep only per-token representations between layers, so pairwise RNA structure is not explicitly modeled.
58VHZl4u5V.method: OptimRNA augments the token stream with a pair state initialized from canonical pairs supported by stem-compatible neighborhoods and updated every layer from token representations via signed low-rank transformations propagated by antidiagonal convolutions that encode stem patterns. Later layers read it as a bounded attention bias, and training remains sequence-only masked language modeling.
58VHZl4u5V.key_idea: A persistent low-rank pair state, refined with antidiagonal convolutions matching RNA stem geometry, biases attention while training stays sequence-only MLM.
58VHZl4u5V.evidence: Zero-shot secondary-structure prediction on four benchmark datasets, supervised fine-tuning against larger foundation models, controlled ablations, and mechanistic analyses.
58VHZl4u5V.claimed_gains: Outperforms all evaluated RNA-LMs in zero-shot secondary-structure prediction on three out of four benchmark datasets; the TL;DR adds that a 34M-parameter model competes with models 20 to 50 times its size.
58VHZl4u5V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture is biologically motivated and efficient, with strong secondary-structure results, controlled ablations, and useful analysis of how structure emerges across layers.
58VHZl4u5V.main_concern: Conceptual novelty over ERNIE-RNA and AlphaFold-style pair representations is unclear, there is no matched-compute comparison (the pair pathway raises step time about 2.3x), and transfer beyond secondary structure is modest or mixed.

40OL9kOMSX.one_liner: Improves sEMG hand-pose decoding with position decoding, multi-task training, and metadata-conditioned layers that use user ID only during training.
40OL9kOMSX.problem: sEMG hand-pose decoding on emg2pose can benefit from information unavailable at test time (initial pose, user and sample metadata), but standard training does not exploit it.
40OL9kOMSX.method: PI-EMG uses position decoding, multi-task tracking and regression training so initial-pose conditioning helps regression, and Metadata-conditioned Layers (McLayers) that stochastically switch between metadata-conditioned and generic mappings in training and use generic mappings at test time.
40OL9kOMSX.key_idea: Stochastically route each layer between metadata-conditioned and generic mappings in training, defaulting to generic at test, to exploit privileged metadata.
40OL9kOMSX.evidence: The emg2pose benchmark tracking and regression tasks, with multiple training seeds and user-level statistics, plus a typing task on emg2qwerty per reviewers.
40OL9kOMSX.claimed_gains: Position decoding reduces tracking errors by 3.5%-5.1% relative to matched velocity models, multi-task training reduces regression error by 5.3%-8.0%, and McLayers improve emg2pose performance by 1.3%-6.8% versus an optimized baseline.
40OL9kOMSX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the work is a solid experimental effort that updates baselines on emg2pose, with simple McLayers and consistent gains across hand-pose and typing tasks supported by seeds and ablations.
40OL9kOMSX.main_concern: Direct comparisons with closely related privileged-information and shared/subject-specific methods such as TRAM and DResNet are missing, as are capacity-matched controls for McLayers.

rXCd0qViJ1.one_liner: Training-free decoding for MLLMs that picks low- and high-entropy visual-attention layers as positive and negative anchors to adjust final-layer logits.
rXCd0qViJ1.problem: MLLMs hallucinate even when relevant visual information exists in intermediate layers, and it is hard to identify which intermediate layer holds useful visual information.
rXCd0qViJ1.method: At each decoding step, AEDG selects a low-entropy layer as a positive anchor and a high-entropy layer as a negative anchor and uses them to adjust the final-layer prediction. It needs no parameter updates and no additional forward computation.
rXCd0qViJ1.key_idea: Rank layers by the entropy of their visual attention: concentrated (low-entropy) layers act as positive anchors and dispersed (high-entropy) layers as negative anchors in contrastive decoding.
rXCd0qViJ1.evidence: Experiments on representative MLLMs (LLaVA-1.5-7B, Qwen-VL-Chat, and GLM-4V-9B per reviews) on CHAIR and POPE, with layer-selection comparisons and a per-token latency measurement.
rXCd0qViJ1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free, and cheap at inference, with strong object-hallucination results and evidence that entropy-based layer selection beats alternative selection criteria.
rXCd0qViJ1.main_concern: Evidence for the key assumption that lower-entropy layers are more reliable is indirect, gains on some backbones are small, and implementation details and ablations (candidate window, confidence gate) are missing or limited to LLaVA.

wZj8oLznJK.one_liner: Conditional flow matching conditioned on current source and generated target states transports Markov trajectories, with mixing-time-dependent sample complexity bounds.
wZj8oLznJK.problem: Sequence-to-sequence transport tasks such as time-series domain adaptation lack a method that turns a source trajectory into one following target Markov dynamics, learned from one source and one target trajectory.
wZj8oLznJK.method: Given one source and one target trajectory, it learns a conditional flow that maps a fresh source trajectory into the target dynamics. The flow conditions on the current source and generated target states so the target Markov structure is preserved under recursive generation.
wZj8oLznJK.key_idea: Reduce trajectory transport to learning a conditional transition flow whose input is the current source state and the previously generated target state.
wZj8oLznJK.evidence: Population correctness under regularity assumptions, a finite-sample error bound with a mixing-time factor and a matching lower bound, and experiments on synthetic data and supervised EEG-to-image retrieval on THINGS-EEG2.
wZj8oLznJK.claimed_gains: No numeric gains visible in the truncated abstract; the TL;DR states improvements in EEG-to-image retrieval, and the error bound carries a factor proportional to the mixing time.
wZj8oLznJK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clearly motivated and the theory (population correctness and sample-complexity bounds) is rigorous, with a simple simulation-free algorithm and both synthetic and EEG experiments.
wZj8oLznJK.main_concern: The EEG experiment does not isolate flow matching as the source of improvement (it is trained jointly with the retrieval loss, with no matched-size adapter or no-flow ablation), and the method combines established components.

gX9kCOLOYW.one_liner: Shows task-aware compression with a mismatched fixed classifier induces perception constraints, and matching a target distribution improves classification.
gX9kCOLOYW.problem: Perception constraints are usually defined against the source distribution, and it is unclear which constraints arise naturally when the secondary task is classification by a classifier mismatched to the source.
gX9kCOLOYW.method: They study compression where the primary task is reconstruction and the secondary task is classification or a statistical test, at varying levels of available domain information. They use the naturally emerging perception constraints to design rate-minimal schemes that maximize secondary-task utility.
gX9kCOLOYW.key_idea: Require the reconstruction distribution to match a target distribution where the fixed classifier's decision boundaries are well defined, a sufficient condition that controls classification error.
gX9kCOLOYW.evidence: Information-theoretic analysis (a coding theorem and a closed-form Bernoulli case per reviews) and neural experiments using an adversarial Wasserstein objective.
gX9kCOLOYW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mismatched fixed-classifier compression setting is concrete and well motivated, with an interpretable sufficient condition linking distribution matching to classification performance.
gX9kCOLOYW.main_concern: The framing of an equivalent perception constraint overstates what is a sufficient surrogate, and neural experiments optimizing an adversarial Wasserstein estimate do not validate the TV- and KL-based guarantees.

4VwFrf5lgL.one_liner: Fine-tunes Llama-3.1-8B by supervising low-dimensional internal geometry, Fourier or helical structure, with no output supervision.
4VwFrf5lgL.problem: It is unknown whether the geometric structure of neural representations can serve as a sufficient learning signal for improving model behavior without supervision on outputs.
4VwFrf5lgL.method: Llama-3.1-8B is fine-tuned on month arithmetic by supervising internal representations of the input month and offset (Fourier harmonics), and on line-break prediction by supervising a helical character-count representation, using an idealized target in a low-dimensional residual-stream subspace.
4VwFrf5lgL.key_idea: Supervise an idealized low-dimensional geometric target in the residual stream, such as Fourier harmonics or a helix, in place of a task loss on outputs.
4VwFrf5lgL.evidence: Two tasks on one model with random-subspace and shuffled-assignment controls, alternative fine-tuning methods, and activation patching of the ideal geometry.
4VwFrf5lgL.claimed_gains: Geometry supervision reaches performance similar to standard fine-tuning without output supervision; a review reports month-arithmetic accuracy rising from 36.3% to 73.3%, against 54.3% for a matched task LoRA.
4VwFrf5lgL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a practical demonstration that mechanistic knowledge of internal geometry can shape training objectives, with useful controls and an interesting result that patching ideal geometry does not recover the gains.
4VwFrf5lgL.main_concern: Evidence is limited to two highly structured tasks on a single model, and ablations do not isolate how much the idealized geometry contributes beyond supervising the right internal variables.

FMEP7v655t.one_liner: RL query rewriting that credits individual edits by comparing retrieval quality with and without each edit, using semantic retrieval feedback.
FMEP7v655t.problem: Ranking-based rewards for LLM query rewriters are sparse when relevant products are not retrieved and coarse when different retrieval outcomes leave ranks unchanged.
FMEP7v655t.method: CGS uses a relevance teacher to score retrieved products against evidence about user intent and a semantic list utility to separate outcomes beyond labeled-product ranks. It assigns each edit credit by comparing retrieval quality when the edit is removed from the complete rewrite and when it is applied to the source query alone, while keeping ranking reward as the objective for the whole rewrite.
FMEP7v655t.key_idea: Edit-level counterfactual credit, taken as the minimum of the removal and standalone-application effects on semantic retrieval utility, is added on top of the sequence ranking reward.
FMEP7v655t.evidence: H&M and Amazon ESCI with a dense retriever, compared with GRPO, Rec-R1, OSPO, VinePPO, and PPO baselines plus credit-construction ablations over three seeds.
FMEP7v655t.claimed_gains: CGS improves NDCG@100 by 10.3% on H&M and 4.9% on Amazon ESCI.
FMEP7v655t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sparse and coarse ranking rewards are a real limitation and that edit-level counterfactual credit is intuitive, with ablations validating where the semantic feedback is placed.
FMEP7v655t.main_concern: Reproducibility and fairness are weak: edit alignment and deletion mapping are underspecified, baseline reproductions are weak without significance tests, and the relevance teacher may bias credit.

EmRRl6RdGn.one_liner: Feed-forward surround-view 4D Gaussian splatting on a VGGT-based backbone with metric depth anchoring and static-dynamic decomposition.
EmRRl6RdGn.problem: Scalable driving simulation needs feed-forward reconstruction that handles metric geometry, all surround cameras, and dynamic content without bounding boxes, tracklets, or optical-flow labels.
EmRRl6RdGn.method: X-Splatter processes all surround cameras jointly on a VGGT-Omega backbone with cross-camera attention. Depth Anchoring Fine-tuning moves geometry from relative to metric space using LiDAR supervision, and Static-Dynamic Decomposition Learning combines dynamic gating, static-promoting regularization, and intermediate-frame supervision for self-supervised motion learning.
EmRRl6RdGn.key_idea: Anchor geometry to metric depth first, then learn motion through a gated static-dynamic Gaussian split with static-promoting regularization and intermediate-frame supervision.
EmRRl6RdGn.evidence: Training and evaluation on all surround views of the Waymo Open Dataset, zero-shot transfer to nuScenes and Argoverse 2, and ablations of the components.
EmRRl6RdGn.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports the best full-image and dynamic-region view-synthesis quality, lowest metric-depth RMSE and cross-view 3D error among evaluated baselines on Waymo, and better zero-shot results on nuScenes and Argoverse 2, without figures).
EmRRl6RdGn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly handling metric geometry, surround coverage, and unlabeled dynamics is a useful combination, with clear links between components and problems and strong reported gains.
EmRRl6RdGn.main_concern: The comparison is not matched, since STORM and DGGT were trained on three front cameras while X-Splatter uses all five, and ablations do not isolate the proposed components from inherited capabilities.

mOPRJ6oPfF.one_liner: Single denoiser jointly generates football trajectories, possession, and insertion-flow event narration, with LAG augmentation fixing text under-generation.
mOPRJ6oPfF.problem: Multi-agent motion generators show where agents go but not what happens, and insertion-only flows under-generate text at few steps because the model reads its own short text as evidence of a short target.
mOPRJ6oPfF.method: They extend joint continuous-discrete diffusion with a text modality so one denoiser generates trajectories, the possession sequence, and an event narration under a shared timestep, with the narration grown by an insertion-only edit flow. LAG is a one-line training augmentation that repairs the length collapse.
mOPRJ6oPfF.key_idea: Add a text stream grown by an insertion-only edit flow to joint trajectory diffusion, and counter the model's learned length bias with the LAG training augmentation.
mOPRJ6oPfF.evidence: A season of a top European league and public World Cup 2022 data, with five-seed World Cup results, LAG settings, a post-hoc narration baseline, and narration-based editing.
mOPRJ6oPfF.claimed_gains: At ten calls LAG improves narration content by a fifth and CIDEr two- to threefold, surpassing the unaugmented model at fifty calls and matching it at a hundred.
mOPRJ6oPfF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that joint trajectory-narration generation is a useful direction for interpretable simulation and that LAG is a small change with clear gains and an informative under-generation analysis.
mOPRJ6oPfF.main_concern: The benefit of joint over trajectory-then-narrate generation is weakly established (carrier-consistency F1 up only 0.02, mixed CIDEr), and LAG leaves the under-generation problem partly unresolved.

gobTbfTWH2.one_liner: Distills only pairwise risk ordering from a transcriptome-trained survival teacher into a histopathology-only student using a pairwise logistic loss.
gobTbfTWH2.problem: Molecular reconstruction or representation matching for missing modalities can require learning variation beyond survival, and numerical survival distillation can shift the student's optimal predictions because teacher and student see different modalities.
gobTbfTWH2.method: OPD trains a teacher on the auxiliary modality alone and transfers pairwise risk ordering derived from its survival curves with a pairwise logistic loss, alongside a survival loss that handles right censoring. The student's inference architecture is unchanged.
gobTbfTWH2.key_idea: Match the teacher's pairwise risk ranking rather than event probabilities or score gaps, because probability matching provably shifts the student's optimum when inputs differ.
gobTbfTWH2.evidence: Eight cancer benchmark datasets and four WSI backbones with transcriptome data as the training-only modality, plus ablations on teachers, distillation objectives, and the distillation weight.
gobTbfTWH2.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off after mentioning extensive experiments; a reviewer cites an average gain of 3.99 C-index points).
gobTbfTWH2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation for ordinal rather than numerical transfer is clear and that the method is simple, architecture-agnostic, and improves all backbones across cohorts.
gobTbfTWH2.main_concern: The improvement over the Risk MSE numerical-distillation baseline is modest, and a teacher-free pairwise ranking loss control is missing, so gains may reflect ranking supervision rather than privileged information.

oIZP1TKjHh.one_liner: Evaluates multilingual LLM capability by round-trip translation, scoring semantic gaps between original text and its back-translation.
oIZP1TKjHh.problem: Standard multilingual benchmarks mostly measure mathematical reasoning and factual recall rather than multilingual proficiency, and thinking variants beat instruct variants there yet often do worse on real-world multilingual tasks such as LMArena.
oIZP1TKjHh.method: Given text in a source language, translate it to a target language and back, then compare the result with the original to expose multilingual generation failures, with no human reference translations or more capable multilingual judge required. The authors release Lost in Translation (LiT), a round-trip benchmark spanning widely spoken languages.
oIZP1TKjHh.key_idea: Score multilingual generation by the semantic gap between original text and its round-trip translation, judged in English so no stronger multilingual judge is needed.
oIZP1TKjHh.evidence: Correlation with LMArena user ratings across models (six models per reviews), plus error and reasoning-language analyses of the MT-AIME24 and INCLUDE benchmarks.
oIZP1TKjHh.claimed_gains: Round-trip translation correlates almost perfectly (rho = 0.94) with user ratings on LMArena.
oIZP1TKjHh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis showing existing benchmarks conflate reasoning and knowledge with language proficiency is valuable, and that round-trip translation is a smart, reference-free proxy that correlates with LMArena.
oIZP1TKjHh.main_concern: The headline correlation rests on only about six models with a judge validated by the same correlation, and translation chains with low-resource languages lack direct human validation.

9CLIgl5JGV.one_liner: Composition-neutral guidance subtracts the per-base mean guidance logit update across positions to stop classifier-free guidance skewing DNA base composition.
9CLIgl5JGV.problem: Stronger classifier-free guidance in DNA diffusion models raises predicted chromatin accessibility but shifts base composition away from real sequences and distorts motif frequencies.
9CLIgl5JGV.method: CNG subtracts the mean guidance logit update across positions for each base, removing sequence-wide base preferences from the update without retraining. It is applied to BaseDiff, their 21.6M-parameter convolutional discrete diffusion model, and generators are compared by accessibility-quality trade-off curves.
9CLIgl5JGV.key_idea: Remove the position-averaged, per-base component of the guidance logit update so guidance cannot shift global base composition.
9CLIgl5JGV.evidence: Two datasets, two accessibility predictors (Enformer and ChromBPNet per reviews), and trade-off-area comparisons against DNA-Diffusion and D3.
9CLIgl5JGV.claimed_gains: CNG reduces composition shifts and improves agreement with real motif frequencies with little change in predicted accessibility, and BaseDiff with CNG gets larger trade-off areas than DNA-Diffusion and D3 with fewer than one quarter of their parameters.
9CLIgl5JGV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the composition-bias problem is clearly identified and the training-free correction is simple and supported by GC-content and motif analyses, with strong results from a small model.
9CLIgl5JGV.main_concern: CNG is evaluated only on BaseDiff while competitors use plain guidance, so portability is untested, and the evaluation relies on computational proxies rather than experimental validation.

TV49ZW7SlO.one_liner: Repairs quantum programs with an LLM guided by a typed diagnosis built from linter output, API evidence, and quantum-semantic rules.
TV49ZW7SlO.problem: LLM program repair that works on classical code struggles with quantum-specific operations, semantics, and frameworks, especially relative-phase and noncommuting operation-order faults.
TV49ZW7SlO.method: Static linter diagnostics, API evidence, and quantum-semantic rules feed a decision model (Jev) that produces a structured typed diagnosis; a separate repair LLM uses it with a textual circuit rendering to repair iteratively. Also introduces a multi-framework fault-injection methodology across Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, and OpenQASM.
TV49ZW7SlO.key_idea: A decision model converts static quantum-specific evidence into a typed diagnosis that conditions an iterative repair LLM along with a textual circuit rendering.
TV49ZW7SlO.evidence: Controlled fault injection across Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, and OpenQASM against five baselines, plus external validation on real-world Bugs4Q-Robust faults.
TV49ZW7SlO.claimed_gains: With GPT-4o, QuRepair achieves 62.83% overall repair success, 15.83 percentage points above the strongest baseline at 47.0%.
TV49ZW7SlO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the matched fault-injection design validated across four frameworks, the coverage of five baselines and a real-bug benchmark, and the practical relevance of quantum semantic errors.
TV49ZW7SlO.main_concern: No component ablations isolate the contribution of Jev, static diagnostics, API evidence, or circuit rendering, and comparison with single-attempt direct repair confounds structured diagnosis with extra iterations.

1HYMFmmTjI.one_liner: Fits an affine combination of score estimates queried at multiple points to reduce bias and variance in score-based sampling.
1HYMFmmTjI.problem: Score estimators built by MCMC, importance sampling or rejection sampling often operate far beyond regimes where mixing time and error control hold, giving large bias and variance.
1HYMFmmTjI.method: It splits a fixed computation budget across multiple queries of the base score estimator at different points, then fits a single pooled estimate as a linear combination (an affine map) that minimizes bias and variance at the target location. Reviews describe the query points as different signal levels with regression coefficients.
1HYMFmmTjI.key_idea: Split a fixed budget across score queries at several signal levels, then fit a linear combination that minimizes bias and variance at the target point.
1HYMFmmTjI.evidence: Analysis of the optimal affine post-processor and experiments on difficult targets (log-concave with large condition number, multimodal, high-dimensional) against computation-matched score estimators; reviewers note the main claim is not rigorously proved.
1HYMFmmTjI.claimed_gains: Reduces score estimation error versus the computation-matched base estimator queried at a single point and improves sample quality on difficult targets; no numbers stated.
1HYMFmmTjI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple and general, works on any score estimator at little extra cost, and gives substantial empirical gains by using multiple noise levels.
1HYMFmmTjI.main_concern: The theory does not rigorously prove that splitting a fixed budget across signal levels beats spending it on a single estimate, and the extra regression cost and choice of levels are not fully discussed.

ugQKFbx8FY.one_liner: FlexCone runs ADMM on an exact relaxation of conic programs, returning a minimum-violation point when infeasible.
ugQKFbx8FY.problem: Conic subproblems from linearization or convexification in sequential convex programming are often infeasible, and existing solvers only certify infeasibility, leaving controllers with stale solutions that violate constraints.
ugQKFbx8FY.method: ADMM is applied to an exact relaxation of the conic program that recovers the original solution when feasible and converges to a minimum-violation point otherwise. Every instance runs the same operations, so it batches on a GPU and can be trained by deep unfolding.
ugQKFbx8FY.key_idea: Penalize distance to the cone in the objective so ADMM treats feasible and infeasible instances with the same operations and returns a minimum-violation point when infeasible.
ugQKFbx8FY.evidence: Standard convex benchmarks, closed-loop model predictive control with infeasible subproblems, and neural network robustness certification, compared with learned projection-based solvers and hand-built slack formulations solved with first-order and interior-point solvers.
ugQKFbx8FY.claimed_gains: Learned FlexCone matches or improves on learned projection-based solvers, eliminates the constraint violations and collisions of the standard fallback in MPC, and completes more episodes or reaches the goal faster than hand-built slack formulations; no numbers stated.
ugQKFbx8FY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that returning a bounded minimum-violation point for infeasible subproblems is useful for SCP and MPC and that the idea is simple and fits existing solvers.
ugQKFbx8FY.main_concern: The residual and termination criterion do not clearly distinguish convergence to a penalized infeasible point from satisfaction of the original cone constraints.

ByZKXmIAKy.one_liner: Compresses recurrent-state checkpoints of hybrid LLMs with truncated SVD for prefix caching in SGLang.
ByZKXmIAKy.problem: Prefix reuse in hybrid models needs full recurrent-state checkpoints at cached boundaries, which increases memory pressure, eviction and repeated prefill.
ByZKXmIAKy.method: HiServe compresses recurrent states with truncated SVD asynchronously on the GPU and reconstructs full states on reuse, leaving existing model kernels unchanged. It is built as a prefix caching system on SGLang.
ByZKXmIAKy.key_idea: Recurrent states are approximately low rank, so a truncated SVD stores compact factors that are reconstructed to full-size states on cache hits.
ByZKXmIAKy.evidence: Low-rank analysis across five recurrent and hybrid models, benchmark and long-context checks, multi-turn ShareGPT replay with Qwen3.5-4B on an NVIDIA GB10, and Marconi trace-driven simulations.
ByZKXmIAKy.claimed_gains: At rank 16, 3.98x storage reduction (3.73x with convolution states), benchmark-score changes of -0.63 to +2.00 points, 11.5% higher throughput and 47.9% lower mean time to first token versus SGLang's uncompressed prefix cache at 15.23 GB, and a 20.0-point mean cache-hit-rate gain in simulation.
ByZKXmIAKy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely, the method is simple and practical because it needs no kernel changes, and the low-rank finding gives a useful storage-fidelity trade-off.
ByZKXmIAKy.main_concern: Baselines and scope: serving is compared only against uncompressed FP32 checkpoints, with no BF16 or INT8 baselines (INT8 matches or beats SVD in some KL tests), plus one model, one GPU and one cache budget, and no isolated reconstruction-overhead measurement.

qsbSeKOShX.one_liner: Single preference-conditioned RL policy iteratively improves complete multi-objective combinatorial solutions with local moves, without an external search framework.
qsbSeKOShX.problem: Neural multi-objective combinatorial optimisation is dominated by learning-to-construct, and the few learning-to-improve methods depend on external search frameworks such as an MOEA or local search.
qsbSeKOShX.method: SUPL2I is a standalone preference-conditioned learning-to-improve method unified across problem sizes. It builds one representation per objective from its related node features and addresses where to inject the preference given node positions and how to treat a local move that yields a nondominated solution; reviewers mention SC-RoPE and a Pareto-based acceptance rule.
qsbSeKOShX.key_idea: A preference-conditioned RL policy with one representation per objective and SC-RoPE positional encoding proposes local moves; an acceptance rule handles nondominated outcomes.
qsbSeKOShX.evidence: Experiments on Bi-TSP, Tri-TSP, and Bi-CVRP report hypervolume against neural methods and conventional solvers such as WS-LKH, with ablations; inference uses parallel preference-conditioned trajectories with elite preservation and sharing per reviewers.
qsbSeKOShX.claimed_gains: Reported to outperform existing neural methods and LKH with weighted-sum scalarisation; no numbers stated.
qsbSeKOShX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a standalone single-model learning-to-improve method with competitive hypervolume results on MOTSP and MOCVRP and supporting ablations.
qsbSeKOShX.main_concern: Novelty is limited because components build on existing learning-to-improve and multi-objective techniques, and results are confined to MOTSP and MOCVRP with higher inference cost than learning-to-construct.

49c5j80Kyj.one_liner: Active learning that gradient-ascends Laplace predictive variance over free-form deformation control points to synthesize geometries a neural operator finds uncertain.
49c5j80Kyj.problem: Neural operators trained on PDE datasets built from a few parameterized base shapes generalize poorly to unseen geometric features, since small geometry changes can induce very different physical dynamics.
49c5j80Kyj.method: AGS equips a few base geometries with low-dimensional free-form deformations and maximizes the Laplace-approximation predictive variance of the solution field with respect to the deformation control points by gradient ascent. The synthesized geometries expand the training set's coverage of the geometry manifold.
49c5j80Kyj.key_idea: Use Laplace predictive variance as a differentiable surrogate for operator error and ascend it with respect to free-form-deformation control points to generate hard training geometries.
49c5j80Kyj.evidence: Experiments on two-dimensional airfoils and reaction-diffusion per reviewers; the abstract says Laplace variance is shown empirically to be a surrogate for operator error over unseen shapes.
49c5j80Kyj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the out-of-distribution geometry problem is well motivated and AGS improves OOD performance, with a principled framework combining Laplace-approximated operators and differentiable free-form deformation.
49c5j80Kyj.main_concern: Validation is limited to 2D airfoils and reaction-diffusion, and the Laplace variance surrogate becomes overconfident far from the training distribution, so the method relies on heuristics such as trust regions.

NNxYSewmeu.one_liner: Rescales an adversarial example's perturbation along its direction to query the teacher near its decision boundary for robust distillation.
NNxYSewmeu.problem: Robust teachers do not classify all adversarial examples correctly, and conventional robust distillation ignores where these examples lie relative to the teacher's decision boundary.
NNxYSewmeu.method: ADBD starts from an adversarial example generated with coordinated teacher-student information and keeps its perturbation direction while scaling the magnitude. If the teacher misclassifies it, the perturbation is shrunk toward the boundary while staying teacher-correct; if the teacher is correct, it is extended along the same direction to probe a farther region where the teacher remains correct.
NNxYSewmeu.key_idea: Scale the perturbation magnitude by bisection depending on whether the teacher classifies the adversarial example correctly, producing query points near the teacher's boundary on its correct side.
NNxYSewmeu.evidence: Evaluated across three datasets, two robust teachers, two student architectures, and PGD, C&W, and AutoAttack, against ARD, IAD, RSLAD, AKD, AdaAD, and SmaraAD.
NNxYSewmeu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and ADBD generally beats the chosen baselines under PGD, C&W, and AutoAttack across datasets and teacher-student pairs.
NNxYSewmeu.main_concern: Limited novelty, since the method resembles AdaAD's inner optimization, MMA's boundary search, and Friendly Adversarial Training, and the computational overhead of extra teacher evaluations is not reported.

icC94MucwX.one_liner: Procedurally generated physics videos pair with parameters and runnable code to test recovery of executable simulations.
icC94MucwX.problem: Existing video-physics benchmarks do not establish whether models can infer dynamics and parameters well enough to regenerate scenes from code.
icC94MucwX.method: PhySimCode asks models to infer physical laws and parameters from raw video and produce runnable Python simulations. Its procedural generators pair videos with source code, sampled parameters, and structured reasoning traces covering laws and numerical methods.
icC94MucwX.key_idea: Evaluate video understanding by requiring parameter recovery and executable simulation code that reproduces the observed physical dynamics.
icC94MucwX.evidence: The benchmark contains 160.6K samples across 162 physics phenomena using SciPy and PyBullet, and the abstract reports evaluating ten models.
icC94MucwX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider executable simulation generation a meaningful test beyond motion descriptions and appreciate the range of generated physics scenarios.
icC94MucwX.main_concern: Parameter-recovery evaluation does not establish identifiability when camera scale, symmetries, or different parameter combinations produce equivalent motions.

tGqgJ0rkYV.one_liner: A combinatorial search scaffold tests proposed algorithms against open problems explaining polynomial coefficients and identities.
tGqgJ0rkYV.problem: Assessing mathematical discovery requires difficult open problems with concrete candidate solutions and checks against invalid shortcuts.
tGqgJ0rkYV.method: qtBench collects open algebraic-combinatorics problems and provides a scaffold for manipulating objects, testing proposed algorithms, and detecting cheating. It evaluates frontier AI systems and discusses release and proof-verification issues arising from AI discovery.
tGqgJ0rkYV.key_idea: Require agents to construct combinatorial algorithms explaining polynomial data, then screen candidate solutions within a domain-specific testing scaffold.
tGqgJ0rkYV.evidence: The benchmark comprises 29 open problems, with frontier-model evaluations and proposed solutions obtained in collaboration with OpenAI.
tGqgJ0rkYV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the algebraic-combinatorics setting a useful, difficult test of mathematical discovery with concrete solution checks.
tGqgJ0rkYV.main_concern: Unavailable proposed solutions and internal-model runs prevent independent scrutiny and reproduction of the reported discovery results.

C9LIwN1t1n.one_liner: Signed Choquet diet terms combine with trajectory networks to forecast biomarkers and condition scan-free 3D body generation.
C9LIwN1t1n.problem: Structured longitudinal health measurements lack a direct connection to pretrained 3D human generators when participant-specific scans are unavailable.
C9LIwN1t1n.method: SCT separates background trajectories from a symmetric Choquet diet term whose component and pair weights solve convex quadratic programs after cross-fitting. Generated reference bodies teach how forecast measurement changes should alter a frozen image-to-3D generator's conditioning.
C9LIwN1t1n.key_idea: Fit a linear-in-weights signed Choquet diet term over convex cones, then map forecast measurement changes to a frozen 3D generator's conditioning.
C9LIwN1t1n.evidence: The paper derives two convex polyhedral weight cones and evaluates forecasts on 7,876 participants from two studies against a diet-free neural trajectory model.
C9LIwN1t1n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the interpretable diet decomposition and convex estimation of component and pair effects.
C9LIwN1t1n.main_concern: The diet term's incremental contribution remains weak or unclear relative to the diet-free trajectory networks.

D3OajsXgpi.one_liner: Attention-distance variance characterizes biological sequence arrangement, while observer features support a separate distilled provenance detector.
D3OajsXgpi.problem: Realistic generated DNA and proteins require ways to characterize distributional differences and screen sequence provenance efficiently.
D3OajsXgpi.method: The paper measures positional attention variance in frozen biological language models using label-selected attention heads and arrangement-preserving controls. A separate detector combines frozen observer representations with multiscale sequence features and distills into a faster student.
D3OajsXgpi.key_idea: Measure variation across positions in attention-weighted distance, and separately fuse observer representations with multiscale sequence features for provenance classification.
D3OajsXgpi.evidence: Experiments cover six DNA generators, a protein panel, dinucleotide-preserving shuffles, held-out generators, substitution perturbations, and teacher-student timing.
D3OajsXgpi.claimed_gains: The detector reaches macro AUROC 0.995 in five-fold cross-validation and 0.970 with generator families held out, while its student runs 69 times faster on one GPU or 7.6 times faster with CPU features included.
D3OajsXgpi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the attention-variance observation and shuffling evidence useful for studying arrangement differences beyond local nucleotide composition.
D3OajsXgpi.main_concern: Supervised attention-head selection and incomplete independent validation limit claims that pAV is a generally meaningful sequence statistic.

5VnclmLDDe.one_liner: Shared trace probes and stability-aware integration make change-of-variables action densities usable for PPO flow policies.
5VnclmLDDe.problem: Trace-estimation noise, cost, and numerical instability discourage direct policy-gradient optimization of flow-policy action densities.
5VnclmLDDe.method: CoVE-PPO optimizes the change-of-variables density of executed actions, sharing trace probes between old and new policies and choosing stable integration nodes. Its EDC parameterization outputs bounded divergence directly.
5VnclmLDDe.key_idea: Share trace-estimation probes across the policy ratio so error depends on Jacobian differences, and place integration nodes within the solver's stability region.
5VnclmLDDe.evidence: State- and vision-based robot-manipulation experiments compare on-policy baselines and examine probe sharing, flow stiffness, and EDC parameterization.
5VnclmLDDe.claimed_gains: As few as 1 probe matches the full trace's learning performance.
5VnclmLDDe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate probe sharing and the analysis linking flow stiffness to integration stability.
5VnclmLDDe.main_concern: Single-task evaluations with short action chunks do not establish computational and expressivity trade-offs for larger policies or higher-dimensional actions.

eU753ZhN5y.one_liner: Gradient-attribution co-occurrence graphs reveal recurring neuron communities, which ablation tests assess for causal roles in prediction.
eU753ZhN5y.problem: Neuron groups that explain isolated forward passes may not form reusable computational units across inputs.
eU753ZhN5y.method: The method builds a graph connecting neurons repeatedly attributed together and applies unsupervised community detection. Held-out interventions test community necessity, sufficiency within selected layers, and layer necessity.
eU753ZhN5y.key_idea: Cluster neurons by repeated gradient-attribution co-occurrence, then ablate or retain communities to test their contribution within selected layers.
eU753ZhN5y.evidence: Experiments on Llama-3.1-8B use ten million discovery prompts, held-out causal tests, behavioral case studies, and shuffled-community controls.
eU753ZhN5y.claimed_gains: With communities capped at 128 neurons across all layers, 13.9% of held-out prompts have at least one layer's contribution explained on a neuron-sparse basis.
eU753ZhN5y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value automated discovery of recurring neuron groups across a broad corpus beyond manually chosen behaviors.
eU753ZhN5y.main_concern: The causal criteria and subspan interventions need clarification because necessity and sufficiency do not clearly refer to the same neuronal subset.

O3YSEw6s4o.one_liner: Learned layerwise expert counts redistribute a fixed activation budget during dense-to-MoE conversion.
O3YSEw6s4o.problem: Dense-to-MoE conversion methods use uniform expert utilization across layers despite differing allocation needs.
O3YSEw6s4o.method: Spectral-MoE learns either static per-layer utilization scalars or dynamic per-token schedules on top of analytic or learned conversions. Dynamic allocation constrains each choice by remaining-layer feasibility and consumes the remaining budget in the final layer.
O3YSEw6s4o.key_idea: Allocate integer expert counts heterogeneously across layers while preserving an exact per-token total through feasible remainder bounds.
O3YSEw6s4o.evidence: Experiments compare uniform, static, and dynamic allocation on analytic and learned dense-to-MoE bases for Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B.
O3YSEw6s4o.claimed_gains: At 25% FFN utilization, dynamic allocation reduces WikiText-2 perplexity relative to uniform allocation on the learned base by 1.03, 3.14, and 2.72 points for Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B, respectively.
O3YSEw6s4o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value exact budget conservation and consistent quality gains from redistributing expert utilization.
O3YSEw6s4o.main_concern: The reproduced DOT-MoE baseline underperforms published results, making the reported allocation gains difficult to attribute.

1kI6KlrEh1.one_liner: Co-trained prototype drift projection reweights class-wise knowledge distillation for exemplar-free class-incremental learning.
1kI6KlrEh1.problem: In exemplar-free class-incremental learning, cached class prototypes become stale at unequal rates across old classes as the backbone evolves, making uniform distillation suboptimal.
1kI6KlrEh1.method: Online Drift Projection (ODP) co-trains a projection module alongside the evolving feature extractor to map stored old-class prototypes into the current feature space without past exemplars. The resulting class-wise prototype displacement upweights high-drift classes in a drift-weighted knowledge distillation objective.
1kI6KlrEh1.key_idea: Co-train an online projection module to map cached old-class prototypes into the current feature space and upweight high-displacement classes during distillation.
1kI6KlrEh1.evidence: Experiments on CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, ImageNet-100, and pretrained CUB-200 compare against AdaGauss and DPCR alongside surrogate-oracle drift correlation analyses.
1kI6KlrEh1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ODP is clearly written, estimates class-wise drift without stored exemplars or inference overhead, and supports its mechanism with surrogate-oracle drift correlation diagnostics.
1kI6KlrEh1.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to prior prototype-projection methods such as BiCyc, LDC, and DPCR, note missing uniform-distillation controls in ablations, and point out degraded performance on fine-grained CUB-200.

gMwMuCy6uy.one_liner: Adversarial prefix nudges and multi-level identity signaling expose anti-stereotypical decision flipping in aligned LLMs.
gMwMuCy6uy.problem: Surface-level LLM fairness benchmarks evaluate static outcome accuracy alone, missing asymmetric decision fragility under pressure and biased internal or verbalized reasoning.
gMwMuCy6uy.method: FairStress evaluates LLM decision processes across 300 cases in 29 high-stakes domains using four degrees of implicit-to-explicit demographic identity signaling, adversarial nudging prefixes, and verbalized plus internal reasoning analyses, alongside tests of bias mitigations.
gMwMuCy6uy.key_idea: Test LLM decision processes across implicit-to-explicit demographic identity levels, adversarial nudging prefixes, and verbalized or internal reasoning traces.
gMwMuCy6uy.evidence: Comprehensive benchmarking evaluates 15 open and API language models across 29 domains and roughly 13 million generated text samples with human validation.
gMwMuCy6uy.claimed_gains: On minority versus majority pairs with explicit identity, accuracy differs by only 2.9 points, yet one added sentence makes 15 models abandon correct majority-favoring answers 9.3 points more often and flip ties toward the minority 23.9 points more often.
gMwMuCy6uy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is carefully designed at large empirical scale across 15 models and 29 domains, systematically connecting surface accuracy, perturbation robustness, and procedural reasoning.
gMwMuCy6uy.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing related work on counterfactual and robustness-based fairness, inconsistent demographic cue specificity across attributes, tiny reasoning-lexicon effect sizes, and an unquestioned strict-meritocracy framing.

jrTPIJRwVx.one_liner: AdsorbSample trains a geometry-conditioned diffusion sampler on interatomic-potential energies to generate flexible adsorbate configurations.
jrTPIJRwVx.problem: Catalyst placement methods require expensive dense labels and often restrict adsorbate search to rigid translations and rotations.
jrTPIJRwVx.method: AdsorbSample formulates placement as conditional Boltzmann sampling under a pretrained machine-learned interatomic potential. Geometry-specific sources, controllers, and differentiable restraints suppress implausible proposals while sampling full adsorbate coordinates.
jrTPIJRwVx.key_idea: Train conditional diffusion on MLIP energies while enforcing adsorbate–surface geometry through tailored sources, interaction branches, and restraint potentials.
jrTPIJRwVx.evidence: OC20-Dense experiments measure MLIP Pass@k, DFT-verified success, post-relaxation validity, and configuration diversity.
jrTPIJRwVx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value using available MLIP energies to reduce dense placement supervision and support flexible configuration search.
jrTPIJRwVx.main_concern: The small DFT evaluation subsets and missing uncertainty estimates limit confidence in the reported physical performance differences.

sayIgYD0hi.one_liner: Access-scoped agent benchmarks separate source inference from cost-aware agent allocation using oracle retrieval and diagnostic feedback.
sayIgYD0hi.problem: LLM orchestrators must infer required evidence sources and choose inexpensive agents with sufficient access, but joint competence remains unclear.
sayIgYD0hi.method: The benchmark fixes overlapping agent access scopes and tests retrieval-grounded engagement costs with oracle retrieval. Source disclosure, pricing changes, scope reassignment, and revision feedback diagnose inference and allocation failures.
