VheWdWd5kF.key_idea: Recovers recursive multifractal step graphon parameters in function space via a pre-trained neural inverse operator for size-generalizable generation.
VheWdWd5kF.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic data, empirical networks across domains, a scientific case study, and a zero-shot whole-graph generation benchmark, supported by conditional identifiability theory.
VheWdWd5kF.claimed_gains: Attains lower error on three of four metrics than a pre-trained graph foundation model and a per-graph optimization baseline on a zero-shot whole-graph generation benchmark.
VheWdWd5kF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that bridging interpretable mechanistic graphon models with fast amortized neural operator inference is well-motivated and cleanly structured.
VheWdWd5kF.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about presentation clarity, potential flaws in degree-sorting permutation invariance and proof C.2, and the gap between population identifiability and finite-sample recovery.

gh5KgPuULf.one_liner: Combines production-rate parameterization, derivative-matching initialization, and simultaneous collocation to prevent vanishing gradients in stiff neural ODEs.
gh5KgPuULf.problem: Shooting-based training of stiff neural ODEs suffers from vanishing sensitivities to fast decay rates, stalling optimization.
gh5KgPuULf.method: They avoid differentiating through an initial value solver by pairing a production-rate vector-field parameterization with transformed derivative-matching initialization and simultaneous Radau collocation. They analyze scalar decay dynamics to show nonvanishing log-rate gradients and test exact-fit identifiability via counterexample.
gh5KgPuULf.key_idea: Replaces IVP solver differentiation with production-rate parameterization, derivative-matching warm starts, and simultaneous collocation to preserve fast-rate gradients.
gh5KgPuULf.evidence: Supported by analytical propositions on scalar decay models, an identifiability counterexample, and 50 runs each across six stiff dynamical system benchmarks.
gh5KgPuULf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear framing separating representation, optimization, and identifiability, along with candid limitation reporting across six stiff benchmarks.
gh5KgPuULf.main_concern: Reviewers note the method combines existing components with mixed empirical results, relies on scalar linear decay theory, and omits some related-work baselines.

kk6kQRpwGm.one_liner: Evolves coding environments in a closed loop using policy-relative task states via prefix scaffolding and difficulty escalation.
kk6kQRpwGm.problem: Existing recursive self-improvement methods evolve environments open-loop without adapting task difficulty to the agent's changing capabilities, leaving solved or unsolved tasks uninformative.
kk6kQRpwGm.method: Frontier-RSI evaluates tasks after each learning round to label them as unsolved, frontier, or saturated relative to the updated policy. A curriculum operator turns saturated tasks into harder escalation variants and converts unsolved tasks into learnable prefix tasks with verified intermediate progress.
kk6kQRpwGm.key_idea: Categorizes tasks as unsolved, frontier, or saturated per round and applies prefix scaffolding or difficulty escalation to keep tasks near the policy frontier.
kk6kQRpwGm.evidence: Evaluated across foundation models of varying capability levels and coding benchmarks including Terminal-Bench 2 and SWE-Bench Pro.
kk6kQRpwGm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-loop U/F/S task framing and bidirectional prefix/escalation operators clearly address open-loop curriculum failure modes.
kk6kQRpwGm.main_concern: Reviewers cite conflated ablations lacking a fresh-task control, missing variance or significance tests on small absolute gains, and teacher-query overhead.

YklF5DeUdQ.one_liner: Constructs randomized threshold decision trees (PrioriTree) achieving O(log m) competitive ratio on high-priority centers and O(log k) overall.
YklF5DeUdQ.problem: Standard explainable k-medians clustering enforces a uniform Theta(log k) competitive ratio across all clusters, ignoring higher-stakes priority centers.
YklF5DeUdQ.method: They introduce priority-aware explainable clustering under l1 k-medians and propose PrioriTree, using ancestor-sampling leaf expansion to build a 2k-leaf threshold decision tree. They extend the algorithm to multiple priority classes and full center-level priority rankings via recursive partitioning.
YklF5DeUdQ.key_idea: Uses ancestor-sampling leaf expansion in threshold decision trees to trade extra leaves for O(log m) or O-tilde(log i) competitive ratios on high-priority centers.
YklF5DeUdQ.evidence: Supported solely by theoretical upper bounds and lower-bound constructions (via the Set Elimination Game), with no empirical experiments.
YklF5DeUdQ.claimed_gains: Achieves O(log m) competitive ratio for m high-priority centers with 2k leaves while keeping O(log k) overall, and O-tilde(log i) for rank-i centers.
YklF5DeUdQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree priority-aware explainable clustering is a well-motivated theoretical extension with strong upper-bound guarantees.
YklF5DeUdQ.main_concern: Reviewers note gaps between upper and lower bounds in Theorem 1.2, lack of any empirical evaluation, and potential interpretability loss from >k leaves (up to sk or O(k (log log k)^(1+eps))).

eSOioRqbC1.one_liner: Pretrains a causal Transformer via horizon-conditioned JEPA and finetunes only the predictor to output monotonic event survival CDFs.
eSOioRqbC1.problem: Rare critical events in multivariate time series lack sufficient labeled data for supervised training of deep forecasting models.
eSOioRqbC1.method: HEPA pretrains a causal Transformer encoder using a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) where a horizon-conditioned predictor forecasts future latent representations from unlabeled series. It then freezes the encoder and finetunes only the predictor to output a monotonic discrete-time survival CDF over future horizons.
eSOioRqbC1.key_idea: Pretrains a causal Transformer with horizon-conditioned latent JEPA prediction, then freezes it and finetunes only the predictor as a survival CDF head.
eSOioRqbC1.evidence: Evaluated across 14 event-prediction benchmarks in 11 domains (including C-MAPSS, water contamination, cyberattacks, and volatility) against PatchTST, iTransformer, MAE, and Chronos-2.
eSOioRqbC1.claimed_gains: Matches or exceeds PatchTST, iTransformer, MAE, and Chronos-2 on at least 10 of 14 benchmarks each with an order of magnitude fewer tuned parameters and, on lifecycle datasets, an order of magnitude less labeled data.
eSOioRqbC1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree HEPA is clearly presented, parameter-efficient, and broadly evaluated across 14 benchmarks and 11 domains.
eSOioRqbC1.main_concern: Reviewers question the necessity of two-stage predictor finetuning (as random predictor initialization differs by <=0.003 AUPRC and end-to-end matches it) and missing frozen-random-encoder controls for JEPA.

S9bOsGKCkd.one_liner: Audits greedy causal search step-by-step, showing Markov-equivalent tie-breaking and edit ordering account for major accuracy loss.
S9bOsGKCkd.problem: Score-based and LLM-assisted causal discovery methods construct graphs edge-by-edge, yet how individual candidate-edit scores and tie-breaking drive final graph errors is poorly understood.
S9bOsGKCkd.method: The authors replay greedy hill climbing from the empty graph and compare every candidate edit at each iteration against the ground-truth graph, separating exact score ties from misordered edits. They test edge-reversal moves, fixed variable orderings, and LLM-based candidate reordering using variable names.
S9bOsGKCkd.key_idea: Decomposes step-by-step greedy causal search errors into score-indistinguishable Markov-equivalent ties and candidate-edit misorderings, showing semantic LLM reordering resolves many ties.
S9bOsGKCkd.evidence: Evaluated on five discrete Bayesian network benchmarks spanning 11 to 441 variables, testing reversal moves, variable orderings, and frontier LLMs.
S9bOsGKCkd.claimed_gains: Choosing correctly at ties eliminates up to 59% of the search's distance to the true equivalence class across benchmark networks of 11 to 441 variables.
S9bOsGKCkd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the step-by-step diagnostic of candidate selection and tie-breaking during greedy causal discovery to be an interesting and well-designed measurement perspective.
S9bOsGKCkd.main_concern: Reviewers cite poor presentation clarity, missing formal mathematical definitions, omitted discussion of prior step-by-step hill-climbing studies (Kitson & Constantinou), and limited network scale.

BGSlOIzOXG.one_liner: Audits multi-agent LLM communication by freezing initial reasoning and measuring correctness-conditioned answer correction and preservation.
BGSlOIzOXG.problem: Final accuracy in multi-agent LLM systems conflates error correction with answer corruption and cannot separate communication gains from extra reasoning passes or architecture.
BGSlOIzOXG.method: Independent-Communicate-Revise (ICR) freezes initial agent trajectories, conditions revision on both agents' initial correctness, and compares against a no-message revision control. It decomposes outcomes into correction rate and preservation rate across textual and latent communication channels and receiver verification policies.
BGSlOIzOXG.key_idea: Freezes initial reasoning trajectories and uses a no-message revision control to measure correctness-conditioned correction and preservation rates separately from aggregate accuracy.
BGSlOIzOXG.evidence: Evaluated on four reasoning benchmarks including MedQA and GPQA-D using Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B across textual, latent, and verification-guided communication.
BGSlOIzOXG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing multi-agent communication into correction and preservation against a no-message baseline is clean and addresses a real evaluation gap.
BGSlOIzOXG.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments rely on a single stochastic decoding realization from identical small Qwen3 models (4B/8B), leaving generation variance and heterogeneous-agent generalization untested.

qZVGWQneRt.one_liner: Benchmarks adaptive multi-turn voice jailbreaks on live full-duplex speech models and defends with an async LLM monitor.
qZVGWQneRt.problem: Full-duplex speech models suffer from latency constraints that leave them vulnerable to adaptive multi-turn jailbreaks and interruptions, which single-turn or scripted evaluations miss.
qZVGWQneRt.method: Crescendo-Live pairs an LLM user simulator with a streaming speech-to-speech loop to run adaptive multi-turn escalation and barge-in attacks. Daimonion defends by running an asynchronous LLM safety monitor over the conversation that injects internal steering instructions mid-reply into a refusal-trained frontend.
qZVGWQneRt.key_idea: Tests live adaptive multi-turn voice jailbreaks with user barge-in and mitigates them via an asynchronous LLM safety monitor injecting mid-reply steering tokens.
qZVGWQneRt.evidence: Evaluated across full-duplex speech models (including PersonaPlex-7B, MiniCPM-o, VoiceChat) on live multi-turn calls and interruption ablations.
qZVGWQneRt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating adaptive multi-turn jailbreaks with live interruptions addresses a realistic and underexplored threat model for full-duplex speech models.
qZVGWQneRt.main_concern: Reviewers note that Daimonion is only tested on one frontend (PersonaPlex-7B) without isolating the async monitor's gain from refusal fine-tuning or comparing against defense baselines.

kI1ZMwT9Xu.one_liner: Interleaves continuous bulk and single-cell transcriptome embeddings with text in a 9B multimodal LLM trained on 5.21M conversations.
kI1ZMwT9Xu.problem: Text-serialized gene expression profiles lose quantitative information, while prior omics-encoder LLMs support only narrow biological tasks.
kI1ZMwT9Xu.method: OmicsLM projects bulk and single-cell transcriptomes into compact continuous embeddings interleaved with natural-language instructions. The authors build a 157-task instruction corpus, perform continued pretraining on 20B tokens and SFT on 5.21M conversations, and introduce the 3,000-question GEO-OmicsQA benchmark.
kI1ZMwT9Xu.key_idea: Projects continuous transcriptome profiles into an LLM's embedding space and trains across 157 biological tasks linking quantitative profiles with text explanations.
kI1ZMwT9Xu.evidence: Evaluated on the publication-disjoint GEO-OmicsQA benchmark (3,000 questions) and PerturbQA.
kI1ZMwT9Xu.claimed_gains: Achieves the best results among evaluated models on GEO-OmicsQA (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
kI1ZMwT9Xu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the large-scale omics-language training corpus, multi-profile comparative interface, and GEO-OmicsQA benchmark.
kI1ZMwT9Xu.main_concern: Reviewers note limited architectural novelty (standard linear projection), unavailable processed training data for reproducibility, and small accuracy drops when profiles are swapped.

ZqGO6Oex3j.one_liner: Combines compressed visual features, physical histories, and Bayesian variable selection for probabilistic world-model forecasting.
ZqGO6Oex3j.problem: World-model forecasting needs to capture temporal dependence and parameter/disturbance uncertainty while remaining interpretable.
ZqGO6Oex3j.method: ViBR-WM compresses visual features, applies Bayesian variable selection over visual, physical, and trend/seasonal/cycle predictors, and averages posterior forecasts across subsets for recursive and direct physical-target prediction.
ZqGO6Oex3j.key_idea: Pairs compressed visual representations with Bayesian model-averaged regression and variable selection for uncertainty-aware physical forecasting.
ZqGO6Oex3j.evidence: Evaluated across four forecasting tasks (object motion, vegetation greenness, solar power) against Temporal Straightening, ConvLSTM, PredRNN, and SimVP.
ZqGO6Oex3j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the combination of visual features and Bayesian regression straightforward, compact, and transparently reported.
ZqGO6Oex3j.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty, unused trend/seasonal/cycle components in selected configs, missing non-Bayesian/non-visual ablations, and weak baselines.

YwykX7usJf.one_liner: Derives a closed-form dual variable for chance-constrained flow fine-tuning to maximize reward while controlling constraint-satisfaction probability.
YwykX7usJf.problem: Existing diffusion and flow steering methods optimize average rewards or constraints rather than controlling the probability that generated samples satisfy downstream criteria.
YwykX7usJf.method: CCFO formulates distributional steering with a probabilistic feasibility constraint, derives a closed-form optimal dual variable, and decouples optimization into dual-multiplier estimation followed by entropy-regularized fine-tuning with a feasibility-adjusted pseudo-reward.
YwykX7usJf.key_idea: Decouples chance-constrained flow fine-tuning into closed-form dual-variable estimation and single-step entropy-regularized reward optimization.
YwykX7usJf.evidence: Demonstrated on 2D illustrative examples, high-dimensional text-to-image generation, and protein sequence design.
YwykX7usJf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the two-stage closed-form dual formulation clean, simple, and well-motivated for probabilistic constraint control.
YwykX7usJf.main_concern: Experimental comparisons show text-to-image gains within error bars against a coarsely tuned baseline, periodic multiplier updates in protein design deviate from the one-shot theory, and fine-tuned models do not always meet target feasibility probabilities.

mavAtv9Ip6.one_liner: Measures non-target dimension leakage in LLM judges with CorrGap and iteratively strips unrelated CoT evidence via DimCheck.
mavAtv9Ip6.problem: Multi-dimensional LLM judges often let irrelevant evaluation dimensions influence their target-dimension scores despite high overall human agreement.
mavAtv9Ip6.method: The paper proposes CorrGap, which compares score-to-ground-truth correlations across target-score-controlled groups, and DimCheck, which iteratively prompts an LLM (or a smaller trained editor) to remove non-target evidence from judge chains of thought.
mavAtv9Ip6.key_idea: Quantifies inter-dimension judge leakage via controlled group correlation differences and mitigates it by iteratively pruning unrelated evidence from judge CoTs.
mavAtv9Ip6.evidence: Validated CorrGap with FActScore, synthetic perturbations, and human annotations, and evaluated DimCheck across three LLMs and four open-ended text tasks.
mavAtv9Ip6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper highlights an important failure mode in multi-dimensional LLM evaluation and validates CorrGap with careful controls.
mavAtv9Ip6.main_concern: DimCheck yields modest effect sizes at substantial computational cost, relies on self-editing by the same potentially biased judge, and lacks checks on whether relevant evidence is accidentally removed.

mzTsDwGV3w.one_liner: Uses token-relabeled text compartments to show that language models can learn near-perfect translation without cross-form transfer.
mzTsDwGV3w.problem: Whether learning to map between different surface forms of the same knowledge automatically produces sample-efficient transfer learning across them.
mzTsDwGV3w.method: The authors render identical text into c disjoint vocabularies via token-for-token relabeling, training models up to 42M parameters with and without shared embedding initializations or paired translation examples.
mzTsDwGV3w.key_idea: Isolates surface-form transfer from semantic and syntactic confounds by training models on token-for-token relabeled disjoint-vocabulary compartments.
mzTsDwGV3w.evidence: Trained models from 1.1M to 41.9M parameters on up to 131B tokens across varying compartment counts c and paired-data ratios.
mzTsDwGV3w.claimed_gains: Paired examples teach models to convert between compartments at 99.7-100% exact match, yet reduce sample-efficiency cost only past a threshold determined by c and learning rate.
mzTsDwGV3w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean, controlled vocabulary-offset design and the finding that exact translation does not guarantee shared representations.
mzTsDwGV3w.main_concern: The setup is highly synthetic with small models and block size 64, key sweeps rely on single seeds without confidence intervals, and underlying mechanisms are not deeply investigated.

szmwO84A7W.one_liner: Scoring judge-human disagreement over sparse-autoencoder features discovers VLM-judge biases and supplies directions for adaptive activation steering.
szmwO84A7W.problem: Existing VLM-judge bias analyses rely on predefined biases or output behavior rather than discovering unspecified biases inside model representations.
szmwO84A7W.method: The method extracts hidden-state features with sparse autoencoders and scores each by differences between judge and human weighting. Selected features guide activation steering, with a lightweight policy adapting interventions per input.
szmwO84A7W.key_idea: A bias score compares how judges and humans weigh the same sparse feature, linking internal bias discovery directly to feature-direction steering.
szmwO84A7W.evidence: Experiments use two open-weight judge models and two datasets, surfacing biases in safety, visual grounding, instruction following, and multilingual interaction.
szmwO84A7W.claimed_gains: Steering with bias features yields statistically significant accuracy improvements for both judges, with gains on relevant task subsets of up to 11.6 percentage points.
szmwO84A7W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using one internal representation for bias discovery and mitigation is intuitive and that human preferences provide a reasonable reference.
szmwO84A7W.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the bias-discovery evidence weak because correlations are tiny and only three hand-picked features per model are steered.

ePyRvO95ky.one_liner: Composing B-spline Kolmogorov-Arnold networks estimates covariate-time hazards nonparametrically with dimension-independent convergence exponents.
ePyRvO95ky.problem: Cox models and generalized additive models require manual specification of interactions and time-varying effects for right-censored clinical outcomes.
ePyRvO95ky.method: KAPLAN-HR uses B-spline KANs to estimate conditional hazard jointly over covariates and time. A single layer recovers a GAM, while deeper compositions represent interactions and time-varying effects.
ePyRvO95ky.key_idea: Compositional B-spline KANs represent joint covariate-time hazard functions, with convergence rates governed by representation smoothness rather than covariate dimension.
ePyRvO95ky.evidence: The paper proves a nonparametric hazard-estimator convergence rate and evaluates six clinical benchmarks against established statistical and deep survival models.
ePyRvO95ky.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the GAM connection and theoretical convergence analysis strengthen the model beyond a simple architecture substitution.
ePyRvO95ky.main_concern: All reviewers question the practical benefit because benchmark differences from the best baselines are not statistically significant.

hsO0iX5XH3.one_liner: Accumulating GPTQ Hessians across recurrence steps addresses calibration blindness, while adapter analysis exposes recurrent quantization feedback.
hsO0iX5XH3.problem: Standard post-training quantization overlooks how looped Transformers recirculate errors and how shared layers encounter different activation directions across recurrence steps.
hsO0iX5XH3.method: The paper separates feedback exposure at non-residual transition layers from calibration blindness in step-0 GPTQ Hessians. It accumulates calibration Hessians over recurrent trajectories and tests the failure mechanisms across looped architectures and controlled systems.
hsO0iX5XH3.key_idea: Trajectory calibration weights each shared layer's GPTQ Hessian with activations from every recurrence step instead of only step 0.
hsO0iX5XH3.evidence: Experiments cover nine checkpoints from seven looped architectures, Huginn-3.5B, R-Llama, linear filters, Mamba state-space models, and GSM8K exact match.
hsO0iX5XH3.claimed_gains: Trajectory-calibrated GPTQ outperforms one-step GPTQ and RTN on all nine checkpoints and recovers bf16-level GSM8K accuracy on Huginn under strict exact match.
hsO0iX5XH3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the topic is timely and that controlled feedback interventions and broad checkpoint experiments clarify recurrent quantization failures.
hsO0iX5XH3.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the one-step GPTQ baseline and adapter-focused analysis generalize across looped architectures, with one also reporting a calibration-split mismatch.

uk53yrXGFI.one_liner: WordBench provides 23 procedurally generated algebraic word-problem families with deterministic symbolic search environments and exact verification.
uk53yrXGFI.problem: Most mathematical benchmarks for LLMs and RL remain static problem collections rather than interactive, verifiable search environments.
uk53yrXGFI.method: WordBench combines procedurally generated datasets (12,824 instances in WordBench-Lit plus generators for fresh instances), deterministic symbolic search environments, and exact verification of traces, action sequences, or algebraic objects across 23 rewrite and witness-construction families, with Lean verification of accepted solutions.
uk53yrXGFI.key_idea: Pairs procedural algebraic word-problem generators with deterministic symbolic search environments and exact solution verification.
uk53yrXGFI.evidence: Benchmarks breadth-first search, best-first search, PPO agents, and LLMs across 23 algebraic word-problem families and 12,824 WordBench-Lit instances.
uk53yrXGFI.claimed_gains: PPO solves 99.1% of instances on Thompson's group, illustrating solver-dependent difficulty across families.
uk53yrXGFI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the generative, verifiable benchmark design spanning diverse algebraic families to mitigate contamination and support RL and LLM search.
uk53yrXGFI.main_concern: Verification and Lean grounding claims are inconsistent with the appendix, and the PPO evaluation uses a small architecture and training-time metrics.

kgdraAm0fG.one_liner: AxisRubric discovers preference-relevant evaluation axes via instruction-blind and instruction-informed observers to judge multimodal generation.
kgdraAm0fG.problem: Textual instructions and predefined rubrics miss perceptual delivery-quality differences observable only in generated multimodal outputs, causing axis omission and dilution.
kgdraAm0fG.method: AxisRubric is a three-phase rubric construction framework that uses instruction-blind and instruction-informed observers to discover delivery-quality and instruction-following axes, consolidates them into a calibrated taxonomy, and generates instance-specific rubrics for multimodal preference judgment.
kgdraAm0fG.key_idea: Separates instruction-blind output observation from instruction-informed observation to discover delivery-quality axes and consolidate instance-specific rubrics.
kgdraAm0fG.evidence: Evaluated across image, audio, and video generation benchmarks with component ablations and multiple author/judge configurations, plus a preliminary study on human-validated axes.
kgdraAm0fG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating delivery quality from instruction following via an instruction-blind observer is a clear and practical formulation for multimodal judging.
kgdraAm0fG.main_concern: Evaluation sets are too small (120 instances per benchmark) without uncertainty estimates, and ablations do not isolate the dual-observer design under matched budgets.

FmYfvQzaHc.one_liner: PAHF personalizes agents online using explicit per-user memory updated via pre-action clarification and post-action human feedback.
FmYfvQzaHc.problem: Static preference models and offline user profiles fail to adapt to new users and preferences that drift over time.
FmYfvQzaHc.method: Personalized Agents from Human Feedback (PAHF) runs a three-step online loop: asking pre-action clarification questions when ambiguous, grounding actions in retrieved explicit per-user memory, and updating memory from post-action feedback. The authors also introduce a four-phase evaluation protocol and two benchmarks.
FmYfvQzaHc.key_idea: Combines explicit per-user memory with dual feedback channels—pre-action clarification and post-action correction—in an online interaction loop.
FmYfvQzaHc.evidence: Supported by theoretical analysis and experiments across a four-phase protocol on two benchmarks (embodied manipulation and online shopping) using multiple LLMs and memory backends.
FmYfvQzaHc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear problem framing separating partial observability from non-stationarity and the well-structured four-phase evaluation protocol.
FmYfvQzaHc.main_concern: Experiments rely solely on simulated users with overly diagnostic feedback and abrupt preference shifts, leaving real-human effectiveness and margin over post-action-only baselines unclear.

fSPdrJTyjB.one_liner: VibeServe uses a two-level coding-agent loop to synthesize and benchmark bespoke end-to-end LLM serving systems.
fSPdrJTyjB.problem: General-purpose LLM serving stacks require extensive manual engineering yet miss workload-, architecture-, and hardware-specific optimization opportunities.
fSPdrJTyjB.method: VibeServe employs an outer agentic loop to plan and track system-design search and an inner loop to implement candidate serving stacks, verify correctness, and benchmark performance on the target workload.
fSPdrJTyjB.key_idea: Uses an outer design-search loop and an inner implementation-and-benchmarking loop to generate full serving stacks specialized per target scenario.
fSPdrJTyjB.evidence: Evaluated in a standard deployment setting against vLLM and across six non-standard scenarios covering specialized model architectures, workloads, and hardware platforms such as MI300A and PyTorch-MPS.
fSPdrJTyjB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find synthesizing complete serving systems compelling and highlight strong results in non-standard scenarios where general stacks lack support.
fSPdrJTyjB.main_concern: The paper omits the economic and compute cost of agentic synthesis and relies on plain baseline configurations or approximate shortcuts in several comparisons.

l5YeoEF1nK.one_liner: Evaluates procedural knowledge conflict in LLMs via SQLShift and PandasShift, diagnosing prior leakage onto memorized operators.
l5YeoEF1nK.problem: Internal memorized knowledge and external contextual instructions are entangled with reasoning, obscuring whether LLMs generalize under procedural knowledge conflicts.
l5YeoEF1nK.method: The authors formalize abstract versus surface-form knowledge, construct SQLShift and PandasShift by swapping or renaming common SQL and Pandas operators, and measure prior leakage across models while testing gradient-ascent unlearning and controlled post-training.
l5YeoEF1nK.key_idea: Swaps or renames SQL and Pandas operators in context to measure how strongly LLMs anchor on internal procedural priors over external rules.
l5YeoEF1nK.evidence: Evaluates 17 open-source models (4B–405B) on SQLShift and PandasShift (104 questions over ten generated tables), plus unlearning and vintage-LLM post-training experiments.
l5YeoEF1nK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the focus on procedural rather than factual knowledge conflict, the controlled operator-remapping setup, and the broad 17-model evaluation.
l5YeoEF1nK.main_concern: Task coverage is narrow and artificial (single-step aggregation with reassigned core symbols like SELECT/MIN), limiting generalization to realistic API updates.

jq6gl30xmI.one_liner: pSGP trains probabilistic supervised graph predictors without graph matching via permutation-equivariant conditional flow matching.
jq6gl30xmI.problem: Supervised graph prediction methods that align predicted and target nodes incur cubic-time matching costs and struggle with multiple valid non-isomorphic outputs.
jq6gl30xmI.method: pSGP casts supervised graph prediction as conditional generation over graph-isomorphism classes using permutation-equivariant conditional flow matching, supporting discrete and continuous graph features with quadratic-time coordinate-wise training losses and modal decoding at inference.
jq6gl30xmI.key_idea: Applies permutation-equivariant conditional flow matching with coordinate-wise losses on arbitrarily indexed targets, yielding index-invariant empirical risk without node matching.
jq6gl30xmI.evidence: Proves empirical-risk invariance to target indexing and evaluates on six established SGP benchmarks plus a new genotype-based probabilistic graph prediction benchmark.
jq6gl30xmI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value avoiding explicit graph matching via an index-invariant conditional flow formulation and note strong empirical benchmark accuracy.
jq6gl30xmI.main_concern: Methodological novelty over prior graph flow/diffusion models (DeFoG, DIRECTO, FlowSG) is insufficiently isolated, and end-to-end inference runtime is not clearly compared.

704O9hAfev.one_liner: Evaluates 12 time-series foundation models on sparse-event timing via within-window ranking and frozen-backbone linear probes.
704O9hAfev.problem: Standard time-series foundation model benchmarks evaluate value forecasting accuracy, overlooking sparse-event tasks where decisions depend on ranking which future periods contain activity.
704O9hAfev.method: The authors formalize within-window sparse-event ranking using chance-corrected AP and AUC skill with exact tie-block expectations. They benchmark released point forecasts, quantile averages, forecast-output logistic readouts, and linear probes on frozen pretrained versus randomly initialized TSFM backbones alongside raw-context logistic regression.
704O9hAfev.key_idea: Benchmark within-window sparse-event ranking using tie-aware chance-corrected AP/AUC skill, contrasting TSFM forecasts, frozen-backbone linear probes, randomized backbones, and raw-context logistic regression.
704O9hAfev.evidence: Evaluated across five sparse datasets, 12 TSFMs for forecasting, and 10 frozen backbones (50 backbone-dataset pairs) for linear probing.
704O9hAfev.claimed_gains: Released TSFM point forecasts improve AP skill over training-free references by at most 0.031; linear probes beat point forecasts in 49/50 pairs, beat forecast-output readouts in 44/50 pairs, and beat randomized backbones in 45/50 pairs.
704O9hAfev.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing within-window sparse-event ranking and separating forecast quality, supervised probing, and pretraining value is thorough and well-designed.
704O9hAfev.main_concern: Probing omits top-performing forecasters (Moirai-2.0, TimesFM-2.5/3), normalization differences confound comparisons against raw logistic regression, and classical intermittent-demand datasets are excluded.

jCw0PAbjTI.one_liner: Introduces VisionValueBench to measure cultural value orientations leaked by multilingual text-to-image models on neutral social prompts.
jCw0PAbjTI.problem: Cultural evaluations of text-to-image systems focus on recognizable artifacts like landmarks or clothing while overlooking implicit cultural values conveyed in generated social scenes.
jCw0PAbjTI.method: VisionValueBench operationalizes six Hofstede cultural value dimensions across 960 value-neutral social scenarios with varying prompt languages and geographic cues. The authors evaluate six T2I configurations to measure directional bias (visual value leakage) across languages and regions.
jCw0PAbjTI.key_idea: Translate Hofstede cultural dimensions into 960 value-neutral multilingual prompts with decoupled language and geographic cues to audit visual value leakage in T2I outputs.
jCw0PAbjTI.evidence: Evaluates six T2I configurations across 960 social scenarios with VLM scoring and a small human validation check (5 annotators, 20 images noted in reviews).
jCw0PAbjTI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting T2I cultural evaluation from surface artifacts to implicit values with decoupled language and geographic cues is timely and well-motivated.
jCw0PAbjTI.main_concern: Reviewers question whether prompts are truly value-neutral to depict, whether non-visual Hofstede dimensions suit images, and note tiny human validation (20 images) and dense presentation.

2JPu7E5lEi.one_liner: Trains a continuous tabular diffusion model with theoretically justified cross-entropy loss for categoricals and classifier-free guidance for rare subpopulations.
2JPu7E5lEi.problem: Conditional tabular generation struggles with mixed numerical and high-cardinality imbalanced categorical features, especially when conditioning on rare subpopulations.
2JPu7E5lEi.method: DiffLTM trains a continuous diffusion Large Tabular Model using MSE for numericals and cross-entropy loss for categorical columns, paired with a theoretical justification for cross-entropy and extended conditional generation. The paper also proposes rare-subpopulation metrics and evaluates econometric synthetic-control fidelity on labor data.
2JPu7E5lEi.key_idea: Combine continuous tabular diffusion with cross-entropy categorical loss and classifier-free conditional generation to model imbalanced categories and rare subpopulations.
2JPu7E5lEi.evidence: Supported by a theoretical justification of cross-entropy loss and experiments on four US Census labor datasets plus an econometric return-to-schooling case study.
2JPu7E5lEi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the rare-subpopulation econometric case study is informative and the paper is clear and tackles a relevant problem.
2JPu7E5lEi.main_concern: Methodological novelty is minimal (continuous diffusion with CE and CFG already exists, and the CE theorem covers a toy case), while evaluation is restricted to four US Census tables and omits key baselines like TabDDPM, ARF, and Harpoon.

NOkzW1XOzE.one_liner: Orchestrates multiple relative camera pose estimators per image pair using a profiler, learned ranker, and pose-error verification network.
NOkzW1XOzE.problem: No single relative camera pose estimator excels across wide baselines, low texture, appearance shifts, and occlusions, leaving an oracle gap across complementary models.
NOkzW1XOzE.method: PoseAgent profiles each image pair's appearance, semantic, and geometric traits, uses a learned ranker to order candidate pose estimators, and runs the top estimator. A learned verification network estimates pose error and triggers fallback to lower-ranked estimators until acceptance or budget exhaustion.
NOkzW1XOzE.key_idea: Profile image-pair traits to rank candidate pose estimators, execute the top choice, and use a learned pose-error verifier to trigger adaptive fallback.
NOkzW1XOzE.evidence: Evaluated across four main pose datasets plus fixed-order tests on ScanNet1500 and MegaDepth1500, with ranker-only, verifier-only, and fixed-order ablations.
NOkzW1XOzE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that estimator complementarity clearly motivates per-pair selection and that component ablations show consistent gains over standalone candidates in the pool.
NOkzW1XOzE.main_concern: Full-system transfer is untested (ScanNet1500/MegaDepth1500 omit the learned ranker), total runtime versus accuracy is unmeasured at matched cost, the candidate pool omits stronger models (MASt3R, RoMa v2), and the fixed cascade is overclaimed as agentic.

wTN6bgPHsd.one_liner: Masks hyperspectral pixels in a low-dimensional spectral component basis rather than wavelength bands for masked autoencoder pretraining.
wTN6bgPHsd.problem: Adjacent hyperspectral wavelengths are so linearly correlated that band-level MAE masking requires up to 90% masking ratios, leaving encoders with sparse spectral views.
wTN6bgPHsd.method: CoMask projects hyperspectral pixels onto a low-dimensional spectral basis (e.g., PCA, NMF, SPICE) spanning all wavelengths and zeros out selected components. Because every wavelength remains present at reduced fidelity, reconstruction difficulty scales with removed spectral signal rather than hidden band indices.
wTN6bgPHsd.key_idea: Project hyperspectral pixels onto a global spectral basis and mask basis coefficients so every wavelength is degraded proportionally without hiding entire bands.
wTN6bgPHsd.evidence: Evaluated across three hyperspectral benchmarks and three encoder scales under a shared harness, comparing fixed bases (DCT, wavelet), fitted bases, random bases, and band masking.
wTN6bgPHsd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting spectral correlation to mask in a component basis is well-motivated and holding input degradation fixed across bases is a clean diagnostic.
wTN6bgPHsd.main_concern: At matched degradation, unstructured corruptions like random bases or white noise match CoMask on EnMAP, a low-rank-preprocessing plus band-masking control is missing, and NMF basis scaling is under-specified.

q8TDsCug4I.one_liner: Jointly learns cross-view satellite retrieval and sub-meter localization from a shared representation with consistency supervision and localization-aware re-ranking.
q8TDsCug4I.problem: Cross-view geolocalization pipelines typically separate satellite image retrieval from fine-grained localization, preventing mutual reinforcement and duplicating inference compute.
q8TDsCug4I.method: GeoSync trains one shared cross-view representation to perform global retrieval and multi-scale local feature matching for fine-grained localization, adding consistency supervision across positive/semi-positive references and a sub-meter refinement module. Localization-aware re-ranking then feeds localization evidence back to refine retrieved candidates.
q8TDsCug4I.key_idea: Share one cross-view encoder across retrieval and sub-meter localization with semi-positive consistency supervision and localization-aware candidate re-ranking.
q8TDsCug4I.evidence: Evaluated on VIGOR and DReSS benchmarks for retrieval, fine-grained localization, boundary robustness, and inference efficiency.
q8TDsCug4I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying retrieval and fine-grained localization into a compact shared-representation pipeline has clear engineering value and strong end-to-end performance.
q8TDsCug4I.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over existing components (especially AuxGeo's PCM), coupled ablations that fail to isolate semi-positive vs cross-tile supervision, and evaluation restricted to known-orientation panoramas.

G7WskHuRMT.one_liner: Co-evolves candidate solutions with explicit working hypotheses that compete for search budget and revise jointly from shared execution history.
G7WskHuRMT.problem: Existing tree-search discovery agents rely primarily on scalar candidate scores and ignore how execution outcomes confirm or refute the hypotheses motivating them.
G7WskHuRMT.method: MESH maintains a high-level global belief state of structured hypotheses (target candidate, mechanism, intervention, expected outcome) that compete for execution budget based on improvements and direct bounded low-level refinement sequences, periodically revising all beliefs jointly from shared history.
G7WskHuRMT.key_idea: Allocate bounded multi-step search budgets across explicit working hypotheses and jointly revise the global belief state from both successful and failed execution outcomes.
G7WskHuRMT.evidence: Evaluated across 19 tasks from MLGym and MLE-bench (as noted in reviews) with ablations and comparisons to search baselines such as AB-MCTS-A.
G7WskHuRMT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating candidate quality from underlying hypotheses and revising explicit beliefs using both successful and failed outcomes is a coherent, useful framework.
G7WskHuRMT.main_concern: Reviewers question whether explicit beliefs are validated independently of adaptive planning, flag reporting discrepancies and missing seed uncertainty, and note narrow evaluation confined to ML engineering tasks.

1drbtiZoXC.one_liner: Recovers multimodal reranking accuracy via a single ridge-fitted shallow-state readout fused with retriever scores under a closed-form correlation rule.
1drbtiZoXC.problem: Multimodal LLM cross-encoder reranking is slow, while compressed alternatives often need relevance labels to recover accuracy and ignore first-stage retriever scores.
1drbtiZoXC.method: SelfRank fits a single readout vector on a frozen MLLM's shallow representation to match its own uncompressed score via one centered ridge solve, then fuses the readout with retriever scores using a closed-form correlation-maximizing weight.
1drbtiZoXC.key_idea: Fit a label-free single-vector readout on shallow MLLM states via centered ridge regression to teacher scores and fuse it with retriever scores via a closed-form correlation rule.
1drbtiZoXC.evidence: Evaluated across 12 datasets from ViDoRe 2 and ViDoRe 3 using two retrievers and two multimodal backbones.
1drbtiZoXC.claimed_gains: Comes within 1.5 percentage points of a full cross-encoder in NDCG@5 while running up to 41x faster.
1drbtiZoXC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the label-free, frozen-backbone readout and closed-form score fusion are lightweight and deliver strong accuracy-latency results across 12 ViDoRe benchmarks.
1drbtiZoXC.main_concern: Reviewers cite normalization mismatches weakening the closed-form optimality proof, missing close baselines (miniReranker, Qwen3-VL-Reranker), unclear offline caching details, and disorganized presentation.

4HfACAyIjt.one_liner: Uses an ADMM optimizer to solve two-sided curvature-aware pruning and sparse-plus-low-rank compression while preserving influence functions.
4HfACAyIjt.problem: Post-training pruning typically ignores internal-gradient alignment, and existing solvers for two-sided curvature-aware objectives that preserve influence functions are prohibitively slow.
4HfACAyIjt.method: CACTUS formulates two-sided curvature-aware compression (incorporating both layer activations and backpropagated gradients) as an ADMM optimization problem with cached eigendecompositions supporting both pure pruning and sparse-plus-low-rank weight decompositions.
4HfACAyIjt.key_idea: Optimize a two-sided activation-and-gradient curvature objective for pruning or sparse-plus-low-rank compression via an ADMM solver with cached eigendecompositions.
4HfACAyIjt.evidence: Evaluated on Llama-3.2-1B and Llama-3.2-3B (and additional model families in reviews) on C4 perplexity, WikiText-2 gradient cosine similarity, influence ranking, and BIG-Bench Hard data selection.
4HfACAyIjt.claimed_gains: At 50% pruning of Llama-3.2-1B, reduces the C4 perplexity gap to dense by 24%, raises WikiText-2 per-sample gradient cosine similarity from 0.445 to 0.512, runs over 15x faster than LLM-Surgeon, and reaches 49.44% vs. 47.22% on BIG-Bench Hard with 5% selected data on Llama-3.2-3B.
4HfACAyIjt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree CACTUS is a practical, efficient ADMM solver for the two-sided curvature objective that works for both pruning and sparse-plus-low-rank compression across broad evaluations.
4HfACAyIjt.main_concern: Reviewers note limited conceptual novelty since the objective and influence connection come from LLM-Surgeon and IProX, and point out that end-to-end influence-estimation speedup and memory savings are not demonstrated.

dTOzCPtMjI.one_liner: Replaces policy-sized PPO value networks in agentic RL with a tiny probe trained on the policy's own activations.
dTOzCPtMjI.problem: Agentic PPO over long multi-turn trajectories uses a separate policy-sized critic that requires pretraining and incurs heavy memory and compute overhead.
dTOzCPtMjI.method: The authors train a small linear/lightweight value probe directly on the language model agent's internal activations—either cold-started alongside the policy or warm-started and frozen—using four orders of magnitude fewer parameters than a policy-sized critic.
dTOzCPtMjI.key_idea: Predict PPO state values with a tiny activation probe on the policy's own hidden states instead of maintaining a separate policy-sized critic network.
dTOzCPtMjI.evidence: Evaluated on agentic benchmarks (including WebShop and BFCL with Qwen3-4B and granite-4.1-3b per reviews) across cold/warm start, off-policy updates, and fixed-critic ablations.
dTOzCPtMjI.claimed_gains: Matches a policy-sized critic's performance with four orders of magnitude fewer critic parameters.
dTOzCPtMjI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the probe critic is simple, well-motivated, cuts PPO training memory substantially, and nearly matches policy-sized critics across tested tasks.
dTOzCPtMjI.main_concern: Reviewers note little analysis explaining why probes work or when they fail across models/tasks, reliance on GAE lambda near 1, and missing critic-size and critic-free PPO baselines.

U2qHsQU6Qq.one_liner: Uses a hierarchical RL allocation-sensitive value bridge to provide immediate post-bargaining feedback in multiplayer self-play.
U2qHsQU6Qq.problem: When trade value depends on a surrounding long-horizon decision problem, bargaining sub-policies face sparse, high-variance reward signals.
U2qHsQU6Qq.method: The framework decomposes control into macro-game play and a bargaining sub-policy connected by a learned allocation-sensitive value bridge that estimates post-exchange minus pre-exchange value to give immediate bargaining feedback during self-play.
U2qHsQU6Qq.key_idea: Train a lower-dimensional allocation-sensitive surrogate value bridge to supply immediate post-trade reward differences to a hierarchical bargaining sub-policy.
U2qHsQU6Qq.evidence: Evaluated in a four-player Settlers of Catan variant across two independently seeded self-play league lineages with policy-swap and no-bridge ablations.
U2qHsQU6Qq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing macro-control from bargaining with a value bridge cleanly addresses credit assignment and is backed by statistically careful policy-swap evaluation.
U2qHsQU6Qq.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic novelty, evaluation confined to a single game (Catan), and hand-designed potential/resource features in the auxiliary critic contradicting the claim of no prescribed exchange values.

xIuaaiFQOs.one_liner: Empirically tests how task difficulty and chain-of-thought reliance affect CoT monitorability across hint-based and secret-side-task evaluations.
xIuaaiFQOs.problem: Safety research often assumes that harder tasks force greater chain-of-thought reliance and therefore automatically make models easier to monitor.
xIuaaiFQOs.method: The authors compare dual-mode models with and without CoT across varying task difficulties in hint-based biasing and adversarial secret-side-task evaluations, and test a simple CoT truncation heuristic to mitigate length-induced monitoring drops.
xIuaaiFQOs.key_idea: Measure CoT reliance via reasoning vs. non-reasoning accuracy gaps across difficulty levels and test whether higher reliance actually improves monitor detection of hints and secret side tasks.
xIuaaiFQOs.evidence: Systematic empirical study using dual-mode hybrid models on synthetic symbolic tasks (e.g., Count Bits) under hint-based and secret-side-task monitoring setups.
xIuaaiFQOs.claimed_gains: Increasing CoT reliance can reduce hint-based monitorability by up to 30 percentage points, while a truncation heuristic recovers up to 16 percentage points.
xIuaaiFQOs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important, timely safety assumption and uses clean dual-mode controls to show that CoT reliance does not guarantee monitorability.
xIuaaiFQOs.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the reasoning-vs-direct accuracy gap truly measures CoT necessity for the monitored behavior and note all experiments use prompted synthetic symbolic tasks.

wcha9RbRG7.one_liner: Measures logical inconsistency when LLM judges evaluate full rulesets versus individual rules and tests prompting, rule refinement, and consistency training.
wcha9RbRG7.problem: Judge models evaluating a full multi-rule specification reach conclusions that conflict with their own rule-by-rule judgments, potentially softening hard constraints.
wcha9RbRG7.method: The authors compare isolated-rule and full-ruleset judgments across LLMs to quantify multi-rule interpretation shifts, and evaluate mitigation via prompting, iterative rule refinement (RULEFORGE), and consistency training.
wcha9RbRG7.key_idea: Audit isolated-rule versus full-ruleset judge discrepancies and reduce multi-rule interpretation shifts through prompting, iterative rule rewriting, and consistency training.
wcha9RbRG7.evidence: Empirical study across multiple LLMs on rulesets including OpenAI's model spec, with ablations separating judge reasoning flaws from ruleset ambiguity.
wcha9RbRG7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper highlights a practically important multi-rule inconsistency failure mode in LLM judges and presents well-structured diagnostic experiments.
wcha9RbRG7.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about sampling variance inflating the aggregate inconsistency metric, soft rules confounding inconsistency rates, policy drift from rule rewriting, and missing comparisons to recent rubric-interference work.

shAa3UHk7I.one_liner: Converts structural and evolutionary tool outputs into compact prompts so frozen LLMs can rank protein variants zero-shot.
shAa3UHk7I.problem: General-purpose LLMs lag behind specialized protein models on zero-shot variant effect prediction, and it is unclear whether scaling biological evidence closes this gap without retraining.
shAa3UHk7I.method: BioEvidence is a training-free, model-agnostic interface that formats structural and evolutionary features from standard biological tools into compact text evidence for frozen LLMs, evaluated with modality, coverage, and shuffled-evidence controls.
shAa3UHk7I.key_idea: Supply frozen LLMs with compact, aligned structural and evolutionary features from standard bioinformatics tools as an external test-time evidence scaling axis.
shAa3UHk7I.evidence: Evaluated across six LLMs (including GPT-5.6 Sol and an open-weight pre-cutoff checkpoint) on ProteinGym and a 25-assay temporal panel.
shAa3UHk7I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is well-motivated and the modality, coverage, and shuffled-evidence controls cleanly show that aligned biological evidence improves zero-shot variant ranking.
shAa3UHk7I.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited methodological novelty beyond prompt formatting, potential assay-label memorization/leakage in LLMs, and confounding mutation-localization headers with biological payload gains.

m6QGSNiipd.one_liner: Replaces deterministic SSM selection gates with KL-regularized Bernoulli or Exponential stochastic gates for robustness and self-interpretability.
m6QGSNiipd.problem: Deterministic state-space models like Mamba lack built-in token-level self-interpretability and degrade under localized sequence perturbations and adversarial attacks.
m6QGSNiipd.method: Baleen treats SSM selection as a random variable regularized by a closed-form KL divergence to a sparsity prior, instantiating Bernoulli state-transition gates (Baleen-B) and Exponential time-intervals (Baleen-E) whose gate values double as inference-time token attribution heatmaps.
m6QGSNiipd.key_idea: Sample SSM transition gates (Bernoulli) or time intervals (Exponential) under a closed-form KL sparsity penalty to balance memory compression, robustness, and built-in token attribution.
m6QGSNiipd.evidence: Evaluated on language benchmarks at 370M and 7B scales against Mamba2, sequence perturbation/adversarial robustness tests, and text classification attribution fidelity against IG and Grad-CAM.
m6QGSNiipd.claimed_gains: Improves average language benchmark accuracy over Mamba2 by 0.95 points at 370M and 1.38 points at 7B, and reduces sequence-perturbation accuracy drop by over 15%.
m6QGSNiipd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree regularizing stochastic selection directly inside the SSM recurrence is a simple, interesting design with encouraging robustness and attribution fidelity results.
m6QGSNiipd.main_concern: Reviewers identify gaps in the theoretical justification: the KL penalty prior depends on current inputs (breaking the information-bottleneck bound), and average gate values do not generally guarantee valid target-specific token attribution rankings.

0Aktkd6y6q.one_liner: Repurposes seven ML/NLP conference papers into 54 containerized tasks to benchmark autonomous AI research agents against human baselines.
0Aktkd6y6q.problem: Evaluating whether LLM agents can execute end-to-end machine learning research requires realistic, contamination-checked codebases with objective metrics and expert human baselines.
0Aktkd6y6q.method: ResearchGym extracts datasets, evaluation harnesses, and baseline code from oral and spotlight ML/NLP papers while withholding the proposed methods, creating seven containerized single-GPU environments with 54 gradable tasks.
0Aktkd6y6q.key_idea: Benchmark end-to-end research agents by withholding the proposed method from published ML/NLP paper repositories and grading agents against the papers' original baselines and metrics.
0Aktkd6y6q.evidence: Evaluated frontier LLM agents across 235 bounded-time and extended runs over 7 containerized environments (54 subtasks).
0Aktkd6y6q.claimed_gains: Agents improve over provided baselines in only 57 of 235 evaluations and complete 20% of tasks on average, though rare runs match expert human methods.
0Aktkd6y6q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the manually validated, containerized environments built from real papers with contamination checks and extensive agent failure analysis form a careful evaluation suite.
0Aktkd6y6q.main_concern: Reviewers argue that hill-climbing on fixed benchmark metrics measures ML engineering rather than open-ended ideation, and note that 54 subtasks stem from only 7 environments with incomplete cross-framework ablations.

9AE85mlisx.one_liner: Automates literature-scale conjecture extraction, LLM proving, and multi-stage triage to focus expert mathematician review.
9AE85mlisx.problem: AI-assisted mathematical discovery is bottlenecked by scarce human expert time spent choosing suitable open problems and reviewing generated proofs.
9AE85mlisx.method: Find, Attempt, and Recommend (FAR) ingests a literature corpus for a given research direction, extracts candidate open conjectures, attempts proofs with reasoning models, and applies automated grading and triage to recommend a filtered shortlist for expert review.
9AE85mlisx.key_idea: Use a search-and-recommender cascade over math literature to extract open conjectures, run automated proof attempts, and triage candidate artifacts before expert verification.
9AE85mlisx.evidence: Tested in a combinatorics pilot starting from 5,245 papers, with expert verification of 15 selected recommended artifacts.
9AE85mlisx.claimed_gains: From 5,245 combinatorics papers, recovers 6,453 candidate conjectures and filters them to 4,717 apparently well-posed open conjectures.
9AE85mlisx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pipeline produced genuine, verified mathematical proofs and counterexamples to published conjectures while candidly reporting its own failures.
9AE85mlisx.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of ablations on extraction/grading stages, reliance on unvalidated model-assigned importance scores, and cherry-picked human review of only 15 of 77 recommended artifacts without false-negative audits.

i8uzIhvtJz.one_liner: Tracks per-constraint pass/fail transitions as prompt constraints grow and audits how LLM-judge errors distort multi-constraint failure measurements.
i8uzIhvtJz.problem: Aggregate all-or-nothing scores on multi-constraint instruction benchmarks hide whether models fail newly added constraints, break previously satisfied ones, or suffer from judge noise.
i8uzIhvtJz.method: The authors decompose growing prompts into per-constraint transitions (satisfying new vs. breaking prior constraints) and audit automated constraint extraction and LLM-as-judge reliability against rule-based checkers and human annotations.
i8uzIhvtJz.key_idea: Decompose multi-constraint instruction evaluation into per-constraint survival versus new-constraint failure while auditing LLM-judge protocol disagreement against rule checkers and human labels.
i8uzIhvtJz.evidence: Analyzed four instruction-tuned models on FollowBench (and ManyIFEval per keywords), including a rule-based Llama slice and human annotation of 392 tracked constraints.
i8uzIhvtJz.claimed_gains: Two judging protocols disagree by up to 55.9 percentage points on identical outputs; the LLM judge fails 30.2% of rule-passing constraints, 13 of 14 apparent recoveries are judge errors, human annotators confirm 297 of 392 constraints, and breakage rises up to 4.7 points per added constraint remain compatible with the data.
i8uzIhvtJz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fine-grained transition decomposition and measurement audit revealing severe LLM-judge artifacts are timely and consequential for instruction-following evaluation.
i8uzIhvtJz.main_concern: Reviewers cite unclear organization and undefined metrics/terminology, and question whether label-perturbation checks truly establish robustness to the measured judge-error mechanism.

nVGeJRTQr6.one_liner: Demonstrates API-only regeneration and concept-extraction watermark attacks, and proposes per-image registered semantic carriers (K-SemMark-R).
nVGeJRTQr6.problem: Image watermarks are vulnerable to off-the-shelf generative regeneration, while fixed-inventory content watermarks leak their private concept sets across generated images.
nVGeJRTQr6.method: The authors attack 13 watermarks via repeated GPT-Image-2 regeneration and extract fixed concepts from IConMark to enable targeted removal and spoofing. They then propose K-SemMark-R, which independently samples prompt-compatible semantic carriers per image and stores verified carriers in a private registry.
nVGeJRTQr6.key_idea: Replace shared fixed watermark inventories with per-image sampled semantic carriers stored in a private registry after showing API regeneration and concept-extraction attacks.
nVGeJRTQr6.evidence: Evaluated across 13 post-hoc and in-generation watermarking methods, 60 baseline attack configurations, and 3,000 watermarked images for concept extraction.
nVGeJRTQr6.claimed_gains: Repeated GPT-Image-2 regeneration achieves 89% average removal across 13 methods; concept extraction recovers 79% of concepts from 3,000 images, enabling 93.9% removal after ten edits and 70.4% spoofing success.
nVGeJRTQr6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the broad, realistic API-only attack evaluation and the compelling demonstration of concept-inventory leakage enabling removal and spoofing in IConMark.
nVGeJRTQr6.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty in regeneration attacks, absence of adaptive attacks against K-SemMark-R's semantic carriers, missing retrieval-only registry baselines, and small defense sample sizes.
